title: Psalms 1:1 (#1)
content:
What does the happy man not do?

He does not do what the wicked advise him to do.

title: Psalms 1:1 (#2)
content:
Where does the happy man not stand?

He does not stand in the pathway of sinners.

title: Psalms 1:1 (#3)
content:
Where does the happy man not sit?

He does not sit in the seat of scoffers.

title: Psalms 1:2 (#2)
content:
When does the man meditate on the instruction of Yahweh?

He meditates on it day and night.

title: Psalms 1:2 (#1)
content:
In what does the man delight?

He delights in the instruction of Yahweh.

title: Psalms 1:3 (#2)
content:
What will happen to everything the man does?

Whatever he does will prosper.

title: Psalms 1:3 (#1)
content:
What is the man like?

He is like a tree set to grow by streams of water.

title: Psalms 1:4 (#1)
content:
What are wicked people like?

They are like the chaff that the wind chases away.

title: Psalms 1:5 (#1)
content:
What will happen to wicked people in the judgment?

They will not stand in the judgment.

title: Psalms 1:6 (#1)
content:
Who knows the way of the righteous?

Yahweh knows the way of the righteous.

title: Psalms 1:6 (#2)
content:
What will happen to the way of the wicked?

The way of the wicked will perish.

title: Psalms 2:2 (#1)
content:
Who are the rulers conspiring against?

They are conspiring against Yahweh and against his anointed.

title: Psalms 2:3 (#1)
content:
What do the rulers want to tear apart and throw off?

They want to tear apart the restraints Yahweh and his chosen king put on them and cast off their rule.

title: Psalms 2:4 (#1)
content:
Who sits in the heavens and mocks the nations who rebel?

The Lord mocks them.

title: Psalms 2:6 (#1)
content:
Who has the Lord anointed?

The Lord has anointed his king on Zion, his holy mountain.

title: Psalms 2:7 (#1)
content:
What decree does Yahweh give to the psalmist?

Yahweh says, “You are my son! Today I have begotten you.”

title: Psalms 2:8 (#1)
content:
What will Yahweh do with the nations and most distant regions of the earth?

Yahweh will give them as an inheritance and possession.

title: Psalms 2:9 (#1)
content:
What will happen to the nations?

They will be broken and smashed.

title: Psalms 2:11 (#1)
content:
How should the kings and rulers respond to Yahweh’s decree?

They should serve Yahweh in fear and rejoice with trembling.

title: Psalms 2:12 (#2)
content:
What happens to all those who take refuge in the son?

They will have a life that is truly good.

title: Psalms 2:12 (#1)
content:
Why should the kings give allegiance to Yahweh’s son?

They should give him allegiance so that he will not be angry and they will not perish.

title: Psalms 3:1 (#1)
content:
What does David say about how many enemies he has?

David says that his so many enemies who have decided to oppose him.

title: Psalms 3:3 (#1)
content:
What does David say Yahweh is to him?

David says Yahweh is a shield that protects him and he is the one who encourages.

title: Psalms 3:4 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh do when David calls out to him?

He answers David from his holy hill.

title: Psalms 3:6 (#1)
content:
Who does David say he will not fear because of Yahweh’s protection?

David will not be afraid of the many people who stand against him.

title: Psalms 3:7 (#1)
content:
What does David say Yahweh does to his enemies?

Yahweh destroys David’s enemies power like he is breaking animals’ teeth.

title: Psalms 3:8 (#1)
content:
From whom does salvation come?

Salvation comes from Yahweh.

title: Psalms 4:1 (#1)
content:
Who does David ask to answer when he calls?

David prays for the God of his righteousness to answer when he calls.

title: Psalms 4:2 (#1)
content:
What does David say the people are doing to his glory?

They are dishonoring him instead of honoring him.

title: Psalms 4:3 (#1)
content:
Who does Yahweh set apart for himself?

Yahweh sets apart the faithful for himself.

title: Psalms 4:4 (#1)
content:
What does David tell people to do while lying on their beds?

David tells them to meditate in their hearts and be silent.

title: Psalms 4:5 (#1)
content:
What kind of sacrifices does David say to offer?

He says to offer sacrifices of righteousness.

title: Psalms 4:5 (#2)
content:
In whom does David say to trust?

He says to trust in Yahweh.

title: Psalms 4:6 (#1)
content:
What do many people say?

Many people ask who will show them anything good.

title: Psalms 4:7 (#1)
content:
What has Yahweh put in David’s heart?

Yahweh has put more joy in his heart than others have in their hearts when their grain and new wine abound.

title: Psalms 4:8 (#1)
content:
Who makes David safe and secure when he lies down in peaceful sleep?

Yahweh alone makes David safe and secure.

title: Psalms 5:1 (#1)
content:
Who does David ask listen to what he says and understand his murmuring?

David asks Yahweh to listen to what he says and understand his distressed sigh.

title: Psalms 5:2 (#1)
content:
What names does David use for the one who listens to the sound of his cry?

David calls him his king and his God.

title: Psalms 5:3 (#1)
content:
What does David say he will do each morning?

David says he will prepare for Yahweh and watch.

title: Psalms 5:4 (#1)
content:
What does God certainly not do?

He certainly does not approve of evil, and evil people will not be his guests.

title: Psalms 5:5 (#1)
content:
Who will not stand in God’s presence?

The arrogant will not stand in God’s presence.

title: Psalms 5:5 (#2)
content:
Whom does God hate?

God hates all who do evil things.

title: Psalms 5:6 (#1)
content:
What will God do to liars?

God will destroy liars.

title: Psalms 5:6 (#2)
content:
Who does Yahweh despise?

Yahweh despises violent and deceitful men.

title: Psalms 5:7 (#1)
content:
Why will David come into Yahweh’s house?

David will come into Yahweh’s house because of Yahweh’s great covenant faithfulness.

title: Psalms 5:7 (#2)
content:
How will David bow down toward Yahweh’s holy temple?

David will bow down in reverence.

title: Psalms 5:8 (#1)
content:
Why does David ask Yahweh to guide him in righteousness?

David asks Yahweh to guide him in righteousness because of those who are watching him.

title: Psalms 5:9 (#1)
content:
How does David describe his enemies?

David describes his enemies as untrustworthy, desiring to destroy people, speaking things that are vile like the smell of an open grave, and flattering people to trap and destroy them.

title: Psalms 5:10 (#1)
content:
What does David ask God to do to his enemies because of their many transgressions and their rebellion against God?

David asks God to declare his enemies guilty and to drive them out.

title: Psalms 5:11 (#1)
content:
Why should those who take refuge in God shout for joy?

They should shout for joy because God defends them.

title: Psalms 5:12 (#1)
content:
What will Yahweh do for the righteous?

Yahweh will bless the righteous and surround them with his favor as with a shield.

title: Psalms 6:1 (#1)
content:
What is David asking Yahweh not to do?

He asks Yahweh not to rebuke him in his anger or discipline him in his wrath.

title: Psalms 6:2 (#1)
content:
What is David asking Yahweh to do because David is frail?

David asks Yahweh to have mercy on him and to heal him.

title: Psalms 6:4 (#1)
content:
Why does David say that Yahweh should rescue and save him?

Because of Yahweh’s covenant faithfulness.

title: Psalms 6:5 (#1)
content:
What will not be remembered in death?

In death there is no remembrance of Yahweh.

title: Psalms 6:6 (#1)
content:
What does David do to his bed because he is weary and groaning?

All night he soaks it with his tears.

title: Psalms 6:7 (#1)
content:
What happens to David’s eyes because of his grief and because of all his adversaries?

His vision becomes weak, so that he cannot see well.

title: Psalms 6:8–9 (#1)
content:
Why should those who practice iniquity get away from David?

Because Yahweh has heard the sound of his weeping and his appeal for mercy and accepts his prayer.

title: Psalms 6:10 (#1)
content:
What does David ask God to make happen to his enemies?

He asks that all his enemies will be ashamed and greatly troubled and they will turn back.

title: Psalms 7:1 (#1)
content:
In whom does David take refuge?

David takes refuge in Yahweh his God.

title: Psalms 7:1 (#2)
content:
What is David asking Yahweh to do?

David is asking Yahweh to save him from those who chase him, and to rescue him.

title: Psalms 7:3–5 (#1)
content:
What does David say should happen to him if he has done wrong?

David says that if he has done wrong, his enemy should be allowed to chase and capture him and leave him lying dead.

title: Psalms 7:6 (#2)
content:
What does David say Yahweh has already ordered?

David says that Yahweh has already ordered judgment.

title: Psalms 7:6 (#1)
content:
What is David asking Yahweh to do in Yahweh’s anger?

David is asking Yahweh show that he is greater than what David’s furious enemies can do.

title: Psalms 7:7 (#1)
content:
What does David want Yahweh to do concerning the peoples?

David wants Yahweh to take his rightful place ruling over all the peoples.

title: Psalms 7:8 (#1)
content:
Who does David want Yahweh to judge?

David wants Yahweh to judge all the peoples, including himself.

title: Psalms 7:9 (#1)
content:
What does David say the righteous God does?

David says God examines thoughts and desires.

title: Psalms 7:10 (#2)
content:
Who does God save?

God saves the upright in heart.

title: Psalms 7:10 (#1)
content:
Where does David’s protection come from?

David’s protection comes from God.

title: Psalms 7:11 (#1)
content:
How does David describe God?

David describes God as a righteous judge who is indignant each day.

title: Psalms 7:12 (#1)
content:
What will God do if a person does not repent?

God will sharpen his sword and will prepare his bow for battle.

title: Psalms 7:14 (#1)
content:
How does David describe the wicked person who does not repent?

David describes the wicked person as filled with evil intentions, as though pregnant with them, and as one who lies as naturally as giving birth.

title: Psalms 7:15 (#1)
content:
What happens to the wicked man who digs a pit?

He falls into the hole he has made.

title: Psalms 7:16 (#1)
content:
What happens to the trouble and violence of the wicked man?

He experiences the bad and violent things that he wants to do to others.

title: Psalms 7:17 (#2)
content:
To whom will David sing praise?

David will sing praise to the name of Yahweh, the Most High.

title: Psalms 7:17 (#1)
content:
For what will David give thanks to Yahweh?

David will give thanks to Yahweh for his righteousness.

title: Psalms 8:1 (#1)
content:
Whose name is magnificent in all the earth?

The name of Yahweh our Lord is magnificent.

title: Psalms 8:2 (#1)
content:
What did Yahweh establish out of the mouth of children and nursing ones?

Yahweh established strength.

title: Psalms 8:2 (#2)
content:
Why did Yahweh establish strength from the mouths of children and nursing ones?

He established it in order to cause the enemy and avenger to end.

title: Psalms 8:3 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist see when he looks at the sky that causes him to wonder why God pays attention to people?

He sees the heavens, the moon, and the stars that God set in place.

title: Psalms 8:5 (#1)
content:
How does the human race compare to the heavenly beings?

Yahweh made humans only a little lower than the heavenly beings.

title: Psalms 8:5 (#2)
content:
With what did Yahweh crown humans?

He crowned them with glory and majesty.

title: Psalms 8:6 (#1)
content:
What did Yahweh make mankind to do?

Yahweh made mankind to rule over the works of Yahweh’s hands.

title: Psalms 8:7–8 (#1)
content:
What are some things that Yahweh put under mankind’s feet?

He put all sheep and oxen, and even the animals of the field, the birds of the sky, and the fish of the sea, and everything that passes on the paths of the seas under mankind’s feet.

title: Psalms 8:9 (#1)
content:
Whose name is magnificent in all the earth?

The name of Yahweh our Lord is magnificent.

title: Psalms 9:1 (#1)
content:
How will David give thanks to Yahweh and of what will he tell?

He will give thanks to Yahweh with his whole heart and tell about all his marvelous deeds.

title: Psalms 9:3 (#1)
content:
When David’s enemies turn back, what happens to them?

The enemies stumble and perish before Yahweh.

title: Psalms 9:4 (#1)
content:
What has the righteous judge done for David?

The righteous judge sits on his throne and has defended David’s just cause.

title: Psalms 9:5 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh do to the nations and the wicked?

He rebukes the nations, destroys the wicked, and blots out their name forever and ever.

title: Psalms 9:6 (#1)
content:
What happens to the enemy?

The enemy are finished in desolation forever, and all remembrance of them perishes.

title: Psalms 9:7 (#1)
content:
Who sits forever and has established his throne for justice?

Yahweh sits forever and has established his throne for justice.

title: Psalms 9:8 (#1)
content:
How does Yahweh judge the world and what does he do for the nations?

Yahweh judges the world fairly and makes just decisions for the nations.

title: Psalms 9:9 (#1)
content:
What will Yahweh be for the oppressed?

Yahweh will be a stronghold for the oppressed in times of trouble.

title: Psalms 9:10 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say about those who know Yahweh’s name?

Those who know Yahweh’s name trust in him, because Yahweh has not abandoned those who seek him.

title: Psalms 9:11 (#1)
content:
What does David say the people are to do for Yahweh, who sits in Zion?

They are to sing praises to Yahweh and tell the nations what Yahweh has done.

title: Psalms 9:12 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh not forget?

He does not forget the cry of the poor.

title: Psalms 9:13 (#1)
content:
What is David asking Yahweh to do for him?

He is asking Yahweh to have mercy on him.

title: Psalms 9:13 (#2)
content:
By whom is David oppressed?

David is oppressed by those who hate him.

title: Psalms 9:14 (#1)
content:
Where will David rejoice in salvation?

David will rejoice in salvation in the gates of the daughter of Zion.

title: Psalms 9:15 (#1)
content:
What has happened to the nations?

The nations have sunk down into the pit that they made and their feet are caught in the net that they hid.

title: Psalms 9:16 (#1)
content:
Who has revealed himself and done justice?

Yahweh has revealed himself and done justice.

title: Psalms 9:17 (#1)
content:
Where are the wicked sent?

They are sent to Sheol, along with all the nations that forget God.

title: Psalms 9:18 (#1)
content:
What will not happen to the needy and the afflicted?

The needy will not be forgotten forever, nor will the hope of the afflicted perish forever.

title: Psalms 9:19 (#1)
content:
What does David want Yahweh to prevent humanity from doing?

David wants Yahweh to arise and not let humanity prevail.

title: Psalms 9:20 (#1)
content:
What is David asking Yahweh to do to the nations?

He is asking Yahweh to terrify them and make them know that they are mere men.

title: Psalms 10:1 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist ask Yahweh at the beginning of the psalm?

The psalmist asks why Yahweh stands far off and hides in times of trouble.

title: Psalms 10:2 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist ask Yahweh to do to the wicked?

The psalmist asks that the wicked be caught in the schemes they have planned to use against the afflicted.

title: Psalms 10:3 (#1)
content:
What does the wicked man do regarding Yahweh?

The wicked man despises Yahweh and praises those who steal from others.

title: Psalms 10:4 (#1)
content:
Why does the wicked man not seek God?

The wicked man does not seek God because he is so proud.

title: Psalms 10:6 (#1)
content:
What does the wicked man say in his heart?

The wicked man says in his heart that he will never be shaken and will never face distress.

title: Psalms 10:7 (#1)
content:
What is the wicked man always talking about?

He constantly curses, lies, threatens others, and is always talking about harming others and doing wrong.

title: Psalms 10:8 (#1)
content:
What does the wicked man do to innocent people?

He hides in ambush near the villages, murders the innocent in secret, and watches for helpless people.

title: Psalms 10:9 (#1)
content:
What animal is the wicked man like?

He is like a lion that hides in a secret place and waits to seize the afflicted.

title: Psalms 10:11 (#2)
content:
What does the wicked man think about his evil deeds?

He thinks that God will not notice his evil deeds.

title: Psalms 10:11 (#1)
content:
What does the wicked man say in his heart about God?

The wicked man says that God has forgotten, that God has hidden his face, and that God will never see.

title: Psalms 10:12 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist ask Yahweh to do?

The psalmist asks Yahweh to take action to prove that he is powerful by paying attention to oppressed people.

title: Psalms 10:13 (#1)
content:
What does the wicked man say in his heart?

The wicked man says in his heart that God will not seek him out.

title: Psalms 10:14 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say Yahweh does for helpless people?

Yahweh sees the mischief done to them, and helpless people and orphans trust him as their helper.

title: Psalms 10:15 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist ask Yahweh to do to the wicked?

The psalmist asks Yahweh to make the wicked powerless and their wickedness come to nothing.

title: Psalms 10:16 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say about Yahweh’s reign?

Yahweh is king forever and ever, and the nations have perished from his land.

title: Psalms 10:17–18 (#1)
content:
How does Yahweh respond to the afflicted?

Yahweh hears the desires of the afflicted, strengthens their heart, attends to them, and acts justly for the orphan and oppressed.

title: Psalms 10:18 (#1)
content:
How does Yahweh respond to the needs of the oppressed?

He strengthens their heart, listens to their prayer, and defends them.

title: Psalms 11:1 (#1)
content:
In whom does David take refuge?

David takes refuge in Yahweh.

title: Psalms 11:1 (#2)
content:
What do some people tell David he should do?

They tell him to flee to the mountains like a bird.

title: Psalms 11:2 (#1)
content:
How do the wicked prepare to attack the upright in heart?

They prepare their bows and make ready their arrows while hiding in darkness.

title: Psalms 11:4 (#1)
content:
What is Yahweh doing in his holy temple?

His eyes watch and examine all people.

title: Psalms 11:5 (#1)
content:
Who does Yahweh test?

He tests both the righteous and the wicked.

title: Psalms 11:5 (#2)
content:
Who does Yahweh hate?

He hates those who love to do violence.

title: Psalms 11:6 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist ask Yahweh to do to the wicked?

He asks Yahweh to rain snares, fire, and brimstone upon them, with a scorching wind as their portion.

title: Psalms 11:7 (#2)
content:
What will happen to the upright?

The upright will see Yahweh’s face.

title: Psalms 11:7 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh think of righteousness?

He loves righteousness.

title: Psalms 12:1 (#1)
content:
Why does David ask Yahweh for help?

David asks Yahweh for help because the faithful have come to an end and have vanished from among the sons of man.

title: Psalms 12:2 (#1)
content:
How does everyone speak to his neighbor?

Everyone speaks lies to his neighbor and speaks insincerely, with flattering lips.

title: Psalms 12:3 (#1)
content:
What does David want Yahweh to do to the flattering lips?

David wants Yahweh to cut off all flattering lips so that they cannot continue to boast.

title: Psalms 12:4 (#1)
content:
What do some people boast about?

Some boast that with their tongue they will be powerful, they control what they say, and that no one is master over them.

title: Psalms 12:5 (#1)
content:
What will Yahweh do for the poor and the needy?

Yahweh will arise and provide safety for which they long.

title: Psalms 12:6 (#1)
content:
What are the words of Yahweh like?

Yahweh’s words are pure words, like silver refined in a furnace and purified seven times.

title: Psalms 12:7 (#1)
content:
What does David say Yahweh will do for his people?

David says Yahweh will keep and protect them from this wicked generation forever.

title: Psalms 12:8 (#1)
content:
What causes the wicked to walk proudly?

The wicked walk proudly when people praise wicked actions.

title: Psalms 13:1 (#1)
content:
What does David repeatedly ask Yahweh at the beginning of this psalm?

David repeatedly asks Yahweh how long he will forget him and hide his face from him.

title: Psalms 13:2 (#1)
content:
What is David experiencing while waiting for Yahweh to answer?

David must carry sorrow in his heart every day, and his enemy has the upper hand over him.

title: Psalms 13:3 (#2)
content:
What does David fear will happen if Yahweh does not answer?

David fears he will die.

title: Psalms 13:3 (#1)
content:
How does David ask Yahweh to respond to his prayer?

He asks Yahweh to consider him, answer him, and restore his strength.

title: Psalms 13:4 (#1)
content:
What does David not want his enemy to say about him?

He does not want his enemy to say that he has prevailed over David.

title: Psalms 13:4 (#2)
content:
What will happen if David is defeated?

His enemies will rejoice when he is brought down.

title: Psalms 13:5 (#2)
content:
What does David ask that his heart might do?

He asks that his heart might rejoice in Yahweh’s salvation.

title: Psalms 13:5 (#1)
content:
In what has David trusted?

David has trusted in Yahweh’s covenant faithfulness.

title: Psalms 13:6 (#1)
content:
Why will David sing to Yahweh?

David will sing because Yahweh has treated him very generously.

title: Psalms 14:1 (#1)
content:
What does a fool say in his heart?

A fool says, “There is no God.”

title: Psalms 14:2 (#1)
content:
Why does Yahweh looks down on the sons of mankind?

He looks down to see if there are any who understand, who seek after him.

title: Psalms 14:3 (#1)
content:
Who has done evil and corrupted themselves?

Everyone has done evil and corrupt things and no one does what is right.

title: Psalms 14:4 (#1)
content:
Who does not call on Yahweh?

Those who make a practice of doing wicked things and acting violently toward Yahweh’s people, do not call on Yahweh.

title: Psalms 14:5 (#1)
content:
Why do those who do not call on Yahweh tremble with dread?

They tremble with dread because God is with the righteous assembly.

title: Psalms 14:6 (#1)
content:
Who is the refuge of the poor person?

Yahweh is his refuge.

title: Psalms 14:7 (#1)
content:
What does David want to come from Zion?

David wants the salvation of Israel to come from Zion.

title: Psalms 14:7 (#2)
content:
When will Jacob rejoice and Israel be glad?

When Yahweh restores the prosperity of his people.

title: Psalms 15:1–2 (#1)
content:
What kind of person may stay in Yahweh’s tabernacle and live on his holy hill?

The person who walks blamelessly, does what is right, and speaks truth from his heart may stay in Yahweh’s tabernacle and live on his holy hill.

title: Psalms 15:3 (#1)
content:
What does this blameless person not do with his tongue?

He does not insult or say bad things with his tongue.

title: Psalms 15:4 (#3)
content:
When this person swears to his own disadvantage, what does he not do?

He does not take back his promises, even if it causes them trouble to do that.

acai.preferred_label: Bring Honor and Glory on Oneself

title: Psalms 15:4 (#2)
content:
Who does this blameless person honor?

He honors those who fear Yahweh.

acai.preferred_label: Bring Honor and Glory on Oneself

title: Psalms 15:4 (#1)
content:
Who does this blameless person despise?

He despises the person God rejects.

acai.preferred_label: Bring Honor and Glory on Oneself

title: Psalms 15:5 (#3)
content:
What will never happen to the blameless person who does these things?

He will never be shaken.

title: Psalms 15:5 (#1)
content:
When this blameless person lends money, what does he not do?

He does not charge interest.

title: Psalms 15:5 (#2)
content:
What does this blameless person not take bribes to do?

He does not take bribes to testify against the innocent.

title: Psalms 16:1 (#1)
content:
What does David ask God to do for him?

David wants God to protect him because he takes refuge in God.

title: Psalms 16:2 (#1)
content:
What does David recognize about his relationship to Yahweh?

David recognizes that Yahweh is his Lord, and that everything good David has comes from Yahweh.

title: Psalms 16:3 (#1)
content:
Who are the holy ones on the earth?

They are majestic people, and David delights greatly in them.

title: Psalms 16:4 (#1)
content:
What will happen to those who hasten after another god?

Their sorrows will be multiplied.

title: Psalms 16:4 (#2)
content:
In what ways will David not worship other gods?

He will not pour out drink offerings of blood, and he will not speak their names with his lips.

title: Psalms 16:5 (#1)
content:
What does David say Yahweh is to him?

David says Yahweh is the portion of his inheritance and his cup, and Yahweh controls what happens to him.

title: Psalms 16:6 (#1)
content:
What does David recognize that Yahweh has done for him?

David recognizes that Yahweh has greatly blessed him.

title: Psalms 16:7–8 (#1)
content:
Why does David bless Yahweh?

David blesses Yahweh because Yahweh counsels him.

title: Psalms 16:9 (#1)
content:
How does David’s heart respond to Yahweh?

David’s heart is glad, and he rejoices. He will rest securely.

title: Psalms 16:10 (#1)
content:
What does David say Yahweh will not allow to happen to his faithful one?

Yahweh will not abandon his faithful one to Sheol where dead people go and will save him from dying.

title: Psalms 16:11 (#1)
content:
What benefits does David get from Yahweh?

Yahweh reveals to David the path of life, gives him joy in Yahweh’s presence, and provides delights at his right hand forever.

title: Psalms 17:1 (#1)
content:
What does David ask God to do for him?

David asks Yahweh to listen to his plea for justice, pay attention to his call for help, and give ear to his prayer.

title: Psalms 17:2 (#1)
content:
What does David pray will come from Yahweh’s presence?

David prays that his vindication will come from Yahweh’s presence.

title: Psalms 17:3 (#1)
content:
What does David say Yahweh found when he tested David at night?

Yahweh examined David’s heart, visited him in the night, and detected nothing wrong; David has determined that he will not sin by what he says.

title: Psalms 17:4 (#1)
content:
How has David kept himself from the paths of the violent?

By the word of Yahweh’s lips, David has kept himself from the paths of the violent.

title: Psalms 17:6 (#1)
content:
Why does David call on God?

David calls on God because God answers him.

title: Psalms 17:7 (#2)
content:
Who does God save by his right hand?

He saves those who take refuge in him from their enemies.

title: Psalms 17:7 (#1)
content:
What does David ask God to show him?

He asks God to show his covenant faithfulness to him in a wonderful way.

title: Psalms 17:8–9 (#1)
content:
How does David ask God to protect him from the wicked?

David asks God to protect him as carefully as people protect their own eyes and to protect him from the wicked like mother birds protect their babies under their wings.

title: Psalms 17:10 (#1)
content:
How does David describe his enemies?

He says his enemies have no mercy on anyone, and their mouths speak with pride.

title: Psalms 17:11 (#1)
content:
What have David’s enemies done to him?

They have surrounded him and set their eyes on him, crouching low to attack him.

title: Psalms 17:13 (#1)
content:
What does David ask Yahweh to do to his enemies?

He asks Yahweh to arise, confront his enemies and make them bow down, and to rescue him from the wicked with his sword.

title: Psalms 17:14 (#1)
content:
From whom is David asking Yahweh to rescue him by his hand?

He is asking Yahweh to rescue him from men of this world whose prosperity is in this life alone.

title: Psalms 17:14 (#2)
content:
What does Yahweh provide for the men of this world?

Yahweh fills their bellies with riches; they are satisfied with sons, and they leave their abundance to their children.

title: Psalms 17:15 (#1)
content:
What does David expect to happen when he sees Yahweh’s face in righteousness?

He will be satisfied with a sight of Yahweh.

title: Psalms 18:1 (#1)
content:
What does David express toward Yahweh?

David says that he loves Yahweh.

title: Psalms 18:3 (#1)
content:
What happens when David calls on Yahweh?

David is saved from his enemies.

title: Psalms 18:6 (#1)
content:
Where was Yahweh when he heard David’s voice?

Yahweh heard David’s voice from his temple.

title: Psalms 18:7 (#1)
content:
Why were the foundations of the mountains shaken?

They were shaken because God was angry.

title: Psalms 18:9–10 (#1)
content:
How did Yahweh come down from the heavens?

With a dark cloud under his feet, he rode on a cherub and flew swiftly on the wings of the wind.

title: Psalms 18:14 (#1)
content:
How did Yahweh scatter his enemies?

He shot his lightning like arrows and made his enemies so afraid that they ran away in different directions.

title: Psalms 18:15 (#1)
content:
What exposed the foundations of the world?

Yahweh’s rebuke and the blast of the breath of his nostrils exposed the foundations of the world.

title: Psalms 18:16 (#1)
content:
Out of what did Yahweh pull David?

It was as if he pulled David out of the deep water of the ocean.

title: Psalms 18:19 (#1)
content:
Why did Yahweh save David?

Yahweh saved David because Yahweh delighted in him.

title: Psalms 18:27 (#2)
content:
What does Yahweh do to those who are proud?

Yahweh humiliates them.

title: Psalms 18:27 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh do to afflicted people?

He saves afflicted people.

title: Psalms 18:30 (#1)
content:
How does David describe God’s way?

He says God’s way is perfect.

title: Psalms 18:37 (#1)
content:
What did David do to his enemies?

David pursued his enemies and destroyed them.

title: Psalms 18:41 (#1)
content:
What happened when David’s enemies called to Yahweh?

Yahweh did not answer them.

title: Psalms 18:43 (#1)
content:
Over what has Yahweh made David the head?

Yahweh made David the head over nations.

title: Psalms 18:48 (#1)
content:
From whom does Yahweh deliver David?

Yahweh delivers David from his enemies.

title: Psalms 18:50 (#1)
content:
To whom does Yahweh show his covenant faithfulness?

He shows his covenant faithfulness to his anointed one, to David and to his descendants forever.

title: Psalms 19:1 (#1)
content:
What do the heavens declare and the sky proclaim?

The heavens declare the glory of God, and the sky proclaims the work of his hands.

title: Psalms 19:2 (#1)
content:
What do the days and nights continually declare?

Day after day, words flow forth, and night after night knowledge is declared.

title: Psalms 19:4 (#1)
content:
What goes out through all the earth and to the end of the world?

Their words go out through all the earth to the end of the world.

title: Psalms 19:5 (#1)
content:
What is the sun like?

The sun is like a bridegroom and like a strong man.

title: Psalms 19:7 (#2)
content:
What does the testimony of Yahweh do?

The testimony of Yahweh makes the simple wise.

title: Psalms 19:7 (#1)
content:
What does the law of Yahweh do?

The law of Yahweh restores the soul.

title: Psalms 19:8 (#1)
content:
What do the precepts of Yahweh do?

The precepts of Yahweh make the heart rejoice.

title: Psalms 19:8 (#2)
content:
What does the commandment of Yahweh do?

The commandment of Yahweh shows them how he wants them to behave.

title: Psalms 19:10 (#1)
content:
How do the judgments of Yahweh compare to gold?

They are of greater value than gold, even much more than much fine gold.

title: Psalms 19:11 (#1)
content:
What do the judgments of Yahweh do for the servant?

By them the servant is warned, and there is great reward in keeping them.

title: Psalms 19:12 (#1)
content:
From what does David ask Yahweh to acquit him?

He asks Yahweh to acquit him from his hidden faults.

title: Psalms 19:14 (#1)
content:
What does David want to be acceptable to Yahweh?

David wants the words of his mouth and the meditation of his heart to be acceptable to Yahweh.

title: Psalms 20:1 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist pray that Yahweh will do for the king in his time of trouble?

The psalmist prays that Yahweh will answer the king in his time of trouble and protect him.

title: Psalms 20:2 (#1)
content:
From where does David want Yahweh to send help and support?

He asks that Yahweh send help from the sanctuary and support from Zion.

title: Psalms 20:3 (#1)
content:
What does David want Yahweh to remember and accept?

David asks that Yahweh remember all the grain offerings and accept the burnt offering.

title: Psalms 20:4 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist ask Yahweh to grant the king?

The psalmist asks that Yahweh grant the king what his heart desires and fulfill all his plans.

title: Psalms 20:5 (#1)
content:
In what does David say they will rejoice?

David says they will rejoice in the salvation that Yahweh gives.

title: Psalms 20:6 (#1)
content:
Who does David say that Yahweh will rescue?

David knows that Yahweh will rescue his anointed.

title: Psalms 20:7 (#1)
content:
In what do other people trust?

Some trust in chariots and others in horses to defeat their enemies.

title: Psalms 20:7 (#2)
content:
What do David and his people do instead of trusting in chariots or horses?

They remember to trust in the power of Yahweh their God.

title: Psalms 20:8 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say happens to enemies compared to his own people?

The enemies bow down and fall, but the psalmist and his people rise and stand firm.

title: Psalms 20:9 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist ask Yahweh to do at the end of the psalm?

The psalmist asks Yahweh to save, and prays that the king will answer them when they call.

title: Psalms 21:1 (#1)
content:
In what does the king rejoice?

He rejoices in Yahweh’s strength and in the salvation Yahweh provides.

title: Psalms 21:2 (#1)
content:
What has Yahweh done for the king?

Yahweh has given the king his heart’s desire and has not held back the request of his lips.

title: Psalms 21:3 (#1)
content:
What has Yahweh brought to the king and placed on his head?

He has brought the king rich blessings and placed a crown of refined gold on his head.

title: Psalms 21:4 (#1)
content:
What did Yahweh give the king after the king asked for it?

Yahweh gave the king life and long days forever and ever.

title: Psalms 21:5 (#1)
content:
Why is the king’s glory great?

His glory is great because of Yahweh’s salvation.

title: Psalms 21:5 (#2)
content:
What has Yahweh bestowed upon the king?

Yahweh has bestowed splendor and majesty.

title: Psalms 21:7 (#1)
content:
Why will the king not be shaken?

He will not be shaken because he trusts in Yahweh through the Most High’s covenant faithfulness.

title: Psalms 21:8 (#1)
content:
What will Yahweh’s hand find?

Yahweh’s hand will find all his enemies, those who hate him.

title: Psalms 21:9 (#1)
content:
What will Yahweh do to his enemies?

He will burn them up, and they will be consumed in his wrath.

title: Psalms 21:10 (#1)
content:
What will Yahweh do to the offspring of his enemies?

He will destroy their offspring and their descendants.

title: Psalms 21:11–12 (#1)
content:
Why will the plot of Yahweh’s enemies not succeed?

It will not succeed because Yahweh will turn them back and draw his bow against them.

title: Psalms 21:13 (#1)
content:
How will the people exalt Yahweh?

They will sing and praise his power.

title: Psalms 22:1 (#1)
content:
What is David asking God?

David is asking why God has abandoned him, why he is so far from David.

title: Psalms 22:2 (#1)
content:
What does David do in the daytime and at night?

David cries out in the daytime, and at night David is not silent.

title: Psalms 22:3 (#1)
content:
How does David refer to God?

David refers to God as holy, sitting as king with the praises of Israel.

title: Psalms 22:4–5 (#1)
content:
What did David’s ancestors do and how did God respond?

They trusted in God, he rescued them, and they were not disappointed.

title: Psalms 22:6 (#1)
content:
How does David describe himself?

David says he is a worm and not a man, a disgrace to humanity and despised by the people.

title: Psalms 22:8 (#1)
content:
What do the people that taunt and mock David say to him?

They say that he trusts in Yahweh and that Yahweh should rescue him since Yahweh delights in him.

title: Psalms 22:9–10 (#1)
content:
How long has David trusted God?

David trusted Yahweh when he was on his mother’s breasts and since he was in his mother’s womb.

title: Psalms 22:11 (#1)
content:
What is David asking God to do for him?

He is asking God to not be far away from him because trouble is near and there is no one to help.

title: Psalms 22:12–13 (#1)
content:
What is surrounding David like a roaring lion?

His enemies, like many strong bulls of Bashan, surround him, and they are opening their mouths wide against him like a roaring lion.

title: Psalms 22:14–15 (#1)
content:
How does David describe himself?

He says he is being poured out like water, all his bones are dislocated, his heart is like wax, his strength has dried up, his tongue sticks to the roof of his mouth.

title: Psalms 22:16 (#1)
content:
What has surrounded David and encircled him?

Dogs have surrounded him and a company of evildoers encircled him, having pierced his hands and feet.

title: Psalms 22:18 (#1)
content:
What was done to the garments and the clothes?

The garments were divided and lots were cast for the clothes.

title: Psalms 22:19 (#1)
content:
What does David request of Yahweh?

He requests that Yahweh not be far away and hurry to help him.

title: Psalms 22:20–21 (#1)
content:
From what does David want to be rescued and saved?

He wants his life delivered from the sword, rescued from the hand of the dog, and saved from the mouth of the lion and the horns of wild oxen.

title: Psalms 22:22 (#1)
content:
What will David declare to his brothers, and where will he praise Yahweh?

He will declare Yahweh’s name to his brothers and praise him in the midst of the assembly.

title: Psalms 22:23 (#1)
content:
Who should praise, honor, and stand in awe of Yahweh?

All who fear Yahweh, all descendants of Jacob, and all descendants of Israel should praise, honor, and stand in awe of him.

acai.preferred_label: Bring Honor and Glory on Oneself

title: Psalms 22:24 (#1)
content:
When did Yahweh hear the afflicted one?

He heard the afflicted one when he cried to him.

title: Psalms 22:25 (#1)
content:
Where will David praise and fulfill his vows?

He will praise Yahweh in the great assembly and fulfill his vows before those who fear Yahweh.

title: Psalms 22:26 (#1)
content:
Who will eat, be satisfied, and praise Yahweh?

The poor will eat and be satisfied, and those who seek Yahweh will praise him.

title: Psalms 22:27 (#1)
content:
What will all the peoples of the earth and what will the families of the nations do?

The peoples of the earth will remember and turn to Yahweh and all the families of the nations will bow down before him.

title: Psalms 22:28 (#1)
content:
Over what does Yahweh rule?

Yahweh rules over the nations.

title: Psalms 22:29 (#1)
content:
Who will bow before Yahweh?

Both the wealthy of the earth and those who are dying and cannot preserve their own lives will bow before him.

title: Psalms 22:30–31 (#1)
content:
What will future generations do?

They will come and declare to a people not yet born what Yahweh has done.

title: Psalms 23:1 (#1)
content:
Who is David’s shepherd?

David’s shepherd is Yahweh.

title: Psalms 23:2 (#1)
content:
Where does Yahweh make David lie down?

Yahweh makes David lie down in green pastures.

title: Psalms 23:2 (#2)
content:
Where does Yahweh lead David?

Yahweh leads David beside tranquil water.

title: Psalms 23:3 (#2)
content:
Where does Yahweh guide David?

Yahweh guides David along right paths.

title: Psalms 23:3 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh restore?

Yahweh restores David’s soul.

title: Psalms 23:4 (#1)
content:
When David walks through the valley of deep darkness, who is with him?

Yahweh is with David.

title: Psalms 23:5 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh prepare before David?

Yahweh prepares a table in the presence of David’s enemies.

title: Psalms 23:5 (#2)
content:
What does Yahweh anoint?

Yahweh anoints David’s head with oil.

title: Psalms 23:6 (#1)
content:
What will pursue David all the days of his life?

Goodness and covenant faithfulness will pursue David.

title: Psalms 23:6 (#2)
content:
Where will David live all the days of his life?

David will live in the house of Yahweh for a very long time.

title: Psalms 24:1–2 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say belongs to Yahweh?

The earth and its fullness belong to Yahweh, along with the world and everyone who lives in it, because he founded it upon the seas and established it upon the rivers.

title: Psalms 24:3–4 (#1)
content:
Who will ascend the mountain of Yahweh and stand in his holy place?

Those who have clean hands and a pure heart, who have not lifted up their soul to what is false and have not sworn deceitfully, will ascend Yahweh’s mountain and stand in his holy place.

title: Psalms 24:5–6 (#1)
content:
What will those who seek Yahweh receive?

Those who seek Yahweh and seek his face will receive a blessing and righteousness from the God of their salvation.

title: Psalms 24:7 (#1)
content:
Why are the gates to be lifted up?

So that the King of glory may come in.

title: Psalms 24:8–10 (#1)
content:
Who is the King of glory?

Yahweh is the King of glory. He is strong and mighty in battle, and he commands armies.

title: Psalms 25:2 (#1)
content:
For what does David ask God?

David asks God to not let him be shamed, and to not let his enemies rejoice over him.

title: Psalms 25:4–5 (#1)
content:
What does David ask Yahweh to teach him?

David asks Yahweh to make known to him Yahweh’s ways and paths, and to lead him in Yahweh’s truth.

title: Psalms 25:6–7 (#1)
content:
What does David ask Yahweh to remember?

David asks Yahweh to remember his compassion and covenant faithfulness, but not to remember the sins of David’s youth or his transgressions.

title: Psalms 25:8–9 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh do because he is good and upright?

He teaches the sinful in the way, leads the humble in justice, and teaches the humble his way.

title: Psalms 25:10 (#1)
content:
What are all the paths of Yahweh?

They are covenant love and faithfulness for those who keep his covenant and his testimonies.

title: Psalms 25:11 (#1)
content:
Why does David ask Yahweh to forgive his iniquity?

David asks Yahweh to forgive his iniquity for the sake of Yahweh’s name.

title: Psalms 25:12–13 (#1)
content:
What will Yahweh do for the man who fears Yahweh?

Yahweh will teach him in the way he is to choose, his life will remain in prosperity, and his descendants will inherit the land.

title: Psalms 25:14 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh share with those who fear him?

Yahweh shares his secret with those who fear him and makes his covenant known to them.

title: Psalms 25:15 (#1)
content:
Why does David continually keep his eyes on Yahweh?

Because Yahweh will rescue David when his enemies attempt to hurt him.

title: Psalms 25:16 (#1)
content:
When David is alone and afflicted, what does he request of Yahweh?

David asks Yahweh to turn toward him and be gracious to him.

title: Psalms 25:17–19 (#1)
content:
When the troubles of David’s heart are enlarged, what does he ask of Yahweh?

David asks Yahweh to bring him out of his distresses, to see his affliction and his trouble and forgive all of his sins, and to see his enemies who are many and who hate him with violent hatred.

title: Psalms 25:20 (#1)
content:
Why does David ask Yahweh to not let him be shamed?

Because David takes refuge in Yahweh.

title: Psalms 25:22 (#1)
content:
From what does David ask God to redeem Israel?

He asks God to redeem Israel from all of his troubles.

title: Psalms 26:1 (#1)
content:
How does David say that he has walked?

David says he has walked with integrity and has trusted in Yahweh without wavering.

title: Psalms 26:2 (#1)
content:
What does David ask Yahweh to examine and test?

He asks Yahweh to test the purity of his inner parts and heart.

title: Psalms 26:3 (#1)
content:
What is before David’s eyes?

Yahweh’s covenant faithfulness is before David’s eyes.

title: Psalms 26:4 (#1)
content:
With whom does David not associate or mingle?

David does not associate with deceitful people or mingle with dishonest people.

title: Psalms 26:5 (#2)
content:
With whom does David say he will not sit?

David says he will not sit with the wicked.

title: Psalms 26:5 (#1)
content:
What does David hate?

David hates gathering with evil people.

title: Psalms 26:6–7 (#1)
content:
What does David do as he goes around Yahweh’s altar?

He sings songs of thanksgiving and recounts all of Yahweh’s wonderful acts.

title: Psalms 26:8 (#1)
content:
How does David feel about the place where Yahweh lives?

He loves the place where Yahweh lives and his glory appears.

title: Psalms 26:9 (#1)
content:
What does David ask Yahweh not to do?

David asks Yahweh not to gather his soul with the sinful or his life with men of blood.

title: Psalms 26:11 (#1)
content:
How does David say that he will walk?

David says that he will walk in integrity.

title: Psalms 26:12 (#1)
content:
Where does David’s foot stand and where will he bless Yahweh?

His foot stands on level ground and he will bless Yahweh among the assemblies.

title: Psalms 27:1 (#1)
content:
Why should David not fear anyone?

David should not fear anyone since Yahweh is his light, his salvation, and the refuge of his life.

title: Psalms 27:2 (#1)
content:
What happened when evildoers advanced against David?

His enemies and those who were hostile to him stumbled and fell.

title: Psalms 27:3 (#1)
content:
In what situations will David not fear but rather remain confident?

His heart will not fear even though an army encamps against him and war rises up against him.

title: Psalms 27:4 (#1)
content:
What has David asked of Yahweh?

David has asked that he may dwell in the house of Yahweh all the days of his life, to look upon the beauty of Yahweh, and to inquire in his temple.

title: Psalms 27:5 (#1)
content:
What will Yahweh do for David in the day of trouble?

Yahweh will protect him in his tabernacle and keep him safe as if he were setting him high upon a rock where David’s enemies cannot reach him.

title: Psalms 27:6 (#1)
content:
How will David offer worship to Yahweh?

David will offer sacrifices of joy, sing, and make music to Yahweh.

title: Psalms 27:7 (#1)
content:
What does David ask Yahweh to do?

David asks Yahweh to hear his voice, to be gracious to him, and to answer him.

title: Psalms 27:8 (#1)
content:
What does David’s heart say to Yahweh?

David’s heart says that he will seek Yahweh’s face.

title: Psalms 27:9 (#1)
content:
What does David ask Yahweh not to do?

David asks Yahweh not to hide his face from him, not to turn his servant away in anger, nor to abandon or leave him.

title: Psalms 27:10 (#1)
content:
What does David say Yahweh will do even though his father and mother have left him?

David says that Yahweh will care for him even though his father and mother have left him.

title: Psalms 27:11 (#1)
content:
What does David ask Yahweh to do because of his enemies?

David asks Yahweh to teach him Yahweh’s way and guide him so that he remains safe from his enemies.

title: Psalms 27:12 (#1)
content:
Why does David ask Yahweh not to give him up to his adversaries?

David asks this because false witnesses and violent accusers have risen against him.

title: Psalms 27:13 (#1)
content:
What did David believe that helped him?

David believed that he would see the goodness of Yahweh and trust him as long as he lived.

title: Psalms 27:14 (#1)
content:
What does David encourage the people to do?

David encourages the people to wait on Yahweh, to be strong, and to let their heart be courageous.

title: Psalms 28:1 (#1)
content:
To whom does David cry out?

David cries out to Yahweh, his rock.

title: Psalms 28:1 (#2)
content:
What will happen to David if Yahweh does not respond to him?

David will join those who go down to the grave.

title: Psalms 28:2 (#1)
content:
Who does David want to hear the sound of his pleading?

David wants Yahweh to hear the sound of his pleading.

title: Psalms 28:3 (#1)
content:
What does David ask Yahweh not to do?

David asks Yahweh not to drag him away with the wicked.

title: Psalms 28:4 (#1)
content:
What does David ask Yahweh to give the wicked?

David asks Yahweh to give them what their deeds deserve and to repay them for their evil deeds.

title: Psalms 28:5 (#1)
content:
What do the wicked not give heed to?

The wicked do not give heed to the works of Yahweh or the action of his hands.

title: Psalms 28:6 (#1)
content:
What has Yahweh heard?

Yahweh has heard the sound of David’s pleading.

title: Psalms 28:7 (#1)
content:
Who is David’s strength and shield?

Yahweh is David’s strength and shield.

title: Psalms 28:7 (#2)
content:
In whom does David’s heart trust?

David’s heart trusts in Yahweh and greatly rejoices.

title: Psalms 28:8 (#2)
content:
Who is the saving refuge of his anointed one?

Yahweh is the saving refuge of his anointed one.

title: Psalms 28:8 (#1)
content:
Who is the strength of his people?

Yahweh is the strength of his people.

title: Psalms 28:9 (#1)
content:
Who does David want Yahweh to save and bless?

David wants Yahweh to save his people and bless his inheritance.

title: Psalms 29:1 (#1)
content:
Who does David say should ascribe glory and strength to Yahweh?

David says the sons of God should ascribe glory and strength to Yahweh.

title: Psalms 29:3 (#1)
content:
To what does David compare the voice of Yahweh?

David compares the voice of Yahweh to thunder over the waters.

title: Psalms 29:5 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh break?

Yahweh breaks the cedars of Lebanon.

title: Psalms 29:8 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh shake?

Yahweh shakes the wilderness of Kadesh.

title: Psalms 29:9 (#1)
content:
What do the people in Yahweh’s temple declare?

Everyone in his temple declares Yahweh’s glory.

title: Psalms 29:10 (#1)
content:
How long does Yahweh sit as king?

Yahweh sits as king forever.

title: Psalms 29:11 (#1)
content:
What two things will Yahweh give his people?

Yahweh will give strength to his people and will bless his people with peace.

title: Psalms 30:1 (#1)
content:
Why does David extol Yahweh?

He extols Yahweh because Yahweh has drawn him up and has not allowed David’s enemies to rejoice over him.

title: Psalms 30:2 (#1)
content:
What did Yahweh do when David cried for help?

Yahweh healed David.

title: Psalms 30:3 (#1)
content:
In what way did Yahweh restore David?

Yahweh caused David to get well and restored him when he was about to die.

title: Psalms 30:4 (#1)
content:
What are the faithful told to do in remembrance of Yahweh’s holiness?

The faithful are told to sing praise to Yahweh and to give him thanks.

title: Psalms 30:5 (#1)
content:
How long does Yahweh’s anger and favor last?

Yahweh’s anger is only for a moment, but his favor is for a lifetime.

title: Psalms 30:5 (#2)
content:
What happens after weeping comes for a night?

Joy comes in the morning.

title: Psalms 30:6 (#1)
content:
What did David say when his life was going well?

David said that he would never be shaken.

title: Psalms 30:7 (#1)
content:
What happened to David when Yahweh hid his face?

When Yahweh hid his face, David was dismayed.

title: Psalms 30:8 (#1)
content:
What did David seek from the Lord?

David sought favor from the Lord.

title: Psalms 30:10 (#1)
content:
What things is David asking Yahweh to do for him?

David is asking Yahweh to hear him, to be gracious to him, and to be his helper.

title: Psalms 30:11 (#1)
content:
What has Yahweh done for David?

Yahweh has turned David’s mourning into dancing, causing him to change from being sad to being joyful.

title: Psalms 30:12 (#1)
content:
What does David say his glory will do?

David’s glory will sing praise to Yahweh and not be silent. He will give thanks to Yahweh his God forever.

title: Psalms 31:1 (#1)
content:
In whom does David take refuge?

David takes refuge in Yahweh.

title: Psalms 31:1–2 (#1)
content:
What does David ask Yahweh to become for him?

He asks Yahweh to be his rocky summit of refuge and a stronghold to save him.

title: Psalms 31:3 (#1)
content:
Why does Yahweh lead and guide David?

Yahweh leads and guides David for the sake of his own name.

title: Psalms 31:4 (#1)
content:
What does David believe that Yahweh will protect him from?

Yahweh will rescue him from the evil plans his enemies have made to hurt him.

title: Psalms 31:5 (#1)
content:
Into what does David commit his spirit?

David puts himself into the care of Yahweh.

title: Psalms 31:6 (#1)
content:
Who does David hate?

He hates those who keep idols of worthlessness.

title: Psalms 31:7 (#1)
content:
Why will David be glad and rejoice in Yahweh’s covenant faithfulness?

David will be glad and rejoice because Yahweh has seen his affliction and known the troubles of his soul.

title: Psalms 31:8 (#1)
content:
Where has Yahweh set David’s feet?

Yahweh has set David’s feet in an open space.

title: Psalms 31:9 (#1)
content:
Why does David ask Yahweh to be gracious to him?

David is in distress and his eye has wasted away from grief.

title: Psalms 31:10 (#1)
content:
Why does David’s strength fail and his bones waste away?

His strength fails and his bones waste away because of his iniquity.

title: Psalms 31:11 (#1)
content:
How do people respond to David?

His enemies treat him with contempt, his neighbors are especially horrified by him, and those who see him outside flee from him.

title: Psalms 31:12 (#1)
content:
To what does David compare himself?

David says he is as forgotten as a dead man whom no one thinks about, and that he is like a broken vessel.

title: Psalms 31:13 (#1)
content:
Why is David so troubled?

He hears the whispering of many and there is terror on every side, as his enemies conspire together to take his life.

title: Psalms 31:15 (#1)
content:
From whom does David ask God to rescue him?

He asks God to rescue him from his enemies and from those who pursue him.

title: Psalms 31:16 (#1)
content:
What does David ask God to do for his servant?

David asks God to make his face shine upon his servant and to save him in Yahweh’s covenant faithfulness.

title: Psalms 31:17 (#1)
content:
What does David ask God not to let happen to him?

David asks Yahweh not to let him have shame.

title: Psalms 31:18 (#1)
content:
Why should lying lips be silenced?

They speak arrogant and contemptuous things against the righteous.

title: Psalms 31:19 (#1)
content:
For whom is God’s goodness stored up?

Yahweh’s goodness is stored up for those who fear him.

title: Psalms 31:20 (#1)
content:
From what does Yahweh protect those who revere him?

He protects them from the evil plots of the enemies who accuse them.

title: Psalms 31:21 (#1)
content:
Why is Yahweh to be blessed?

Yahweh showed David his marvelous covenant faithfulness when David was in a besieged city.

title: Psalms 31:22 (#1)
content:
What did Yahweh do for David even though David said that he was cut off from God’s eyes?

Yahweh heard his plea for help when David cried out to him.

title: Psalms 31:23 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh do for his faithful followers?

Yahweh preserves the faithful but pays back the proud in full.

title: Psalms 31:24 (#1)
content:
What advice does David give to those who wait for Yahweh?

He tells them to be firm and courageous.

title: Psalms 32:1 (#1)
content:
Who does the psalmist describe as truly happy?

The psalmist describes as truly happy those whose transgression is lifted up and whose sin is covered.

title: Psalms 32:3–4 (#1)
content:
What happened to David when he did not confess his sins?

His bones wasted away and he groaned all day long. Yahweh’s hand was heavy on him day and night, and his vitality was sapped by the summer heat.

title: Psalms 32:5 (#1)
content:
What did God do when David acknowledged his sin and no longer hid his iniquity?

God forgave the guilt of David’s sin.

title: Psalms 32:6 (#1)
content:
What should godly people do when they realize they have sinned?

They should pray to Yahweh when they realize that they have sinned.

title: Psalms 32:6 (#2)
content:
What assurance does the psalmist give to the godly who pray to Yahweh?

A flood of great waters will not reach them.

title: Psalms 32:7 (#1)
content:
With what does Yahweh surround the psalmist?

Yahweh surrounds him with shouts of deliverance.

title: Psalms 32:8 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh promise to do for those who come to him?

Yahweh promises to instruct and teach them about the way they should go, and to counsel them personally.

title: Psalms 32:9 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist warn against being like?

The psalmist warns against being like a horse or mule without understanding, which must be controlled with a bit and bridle.

title: Psalms 32:10 (#1)
content:
What will happen to the one who trusts in Yahweh?

Yahweh’s covenant faithfulness will surround him.

title: Psalms 32:11 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist call on the righteous and upright in heart to do?

The psalmist calls them to be glad in Yahweh, rejoice, and shout for joy.

title: Psalms 33:1 (#1)
content:
In whom does the psalmist say the righteous should rejoice?

The righteous should rejoice in Yahweh.

title: Psalms 33:2 (#1)
content:
With what instruments does the psalmist say to play to give thanks to Yahweh?

The psalmist says to give thanks to Yahweh with the harp and with the lyre of ten strings.

title: Psalms 33:4 (#1)
content:
How does the psalmist describe Yahweh’s word and work?

Yahweh’s word is upright and all his work is done in faithfulness.

title: Psalms 33:5 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh love?

Yahweh loves righteousness and justice.

title: Psalms 33:6 (#1)
content:
What was made by the word of Yahweh?

The heavens and the stars were created by Yahweh commanding it.

title: Psalms 33:7 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say Yahweh does to the waters of the sea?

He gathers the waters of the sea together like a heap.

title: Psalms 33:8 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say all the inhabitants of the world should do?

All the inhabitants of the world should deeply revere Yahweh.

title: Psalms 33:11 (#1)
content:
How long will the counsel of Yahweh stand?

The counsel of Yahweh stands forever, the plans of his heart to every generation.

title: Psalms 33:14 (#1)
content:
On whom does Yahweh look down from where he lives?

Yahweh looks down on all the people, on all who live on the earth.

title: Psalms 33:18 (#1)
content:
Whom does Yahweh watch over?

Yahweh watches over those who deeply revere him and confidently expect him to faithfully love them.

title: Psalms 33:21 (#1)
content:
Why does the psalmist say the heart rejoices in Yahweh?

The heart rejoices in Yahweh because the people trust in his holy name.

title: Psalms 34:1 (#1)
content:
How often will David praise Yahweh?

David will praise Yahweh at all times.

title: Psalms 34:2 (#1)
content:
Who does David want to hear when he boasts in Yahweh?

David wants the humble to hear it and rejoice.

title: Psalms 34:3 (#1)
content:
What is David asking people to do with him?

David is asking them to magnify Yahweh and exalt his name together.

title: Psalms 34:4 (#1)
content:
What happened when David sought Yahweh?

Yahweh answered David and delivered him from all his fears.

title: Psalms 34:5 (#1)
content:
What happens to those who look to Yahweh?

They are radiant and their faces are not ashamed.

title: Psalms 34:6 (#1)
content:
What did Yahweh do when this afflicted man called out to him?

Yahweh heard him and saved him from all his troubles.

title: Psalms 34:7 (#1)
content:
What does the angel of Yahweh do when he encamps around those who fear him?

The angel of Yahweh rescues them.

title: Psalms 34:8 (#1)
content:
Who is the man who is happy?

The man who takes refuge in Yahweh is happy.

title: Psalms 34:9 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say is true for those who fear Yahweh?

There is no lack for those who fear Yahweh.

title: Psalms 34:10 (#1)
content:
What does David say about those who seek Yahweh?

Those who seek Yahweh will not lack anything good.

title: Psalms 34:11 (#1)
content:
What does David invite the sons to do?

David invites them to come and listen to him so that he can teach them the fear of Yahweh.

title: Psalms 34:13–14 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say a man who desires life should do?

He should guard his tongue from evil and his lips from speaking deceit, turn away from evil, do good, seek peace, and pursue it.

title: Psalms 34:15 (#1)
content:
How does Yahweh pay attention to the righteous?

Yahweh pays attention and listens when the righteous call to him for help.

title: Psalms 34:16 (#1)
content:
What will Yahweh do to the doers of evil?

Yahweh will cut off their remembrance from the earth.

title: Psalms 34:17 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh do when the righteous cry out?

He hears and delivers them from all their troubles.

title: Psalms 34:18 (#2)
content:
Who does Yahweh save?

Yahweh saves those with a crushed spirit.

title: Psalms 34:18 (#1)
content:
To whom is Yahweh near?

He is near the brokenhearted.

title: Psalms 34:19–20 (#1)
content:
What happens to the righteous who have many troubles?

Yahweh delivers him from all of them and guards all his bones.

title: Psalms 34:21 (#2)
content:
What will happen to those who hate the righteous?

Those who hate the righteous will be found guilty.

title: Psalms 34:21 (#1)
content:
What will happen to the wicked?

Evil will kill the wicked.

title: Psalms 34:22 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh do for his servants?

He redeems the soul of his servants, and those who take refuge in him will not be guilty.

title: Psalms 35:1 (#1)
content:
What does David ask Yahweh to do for him?

David asks Yahweh to work against those who work against him, and fight against those who fight against him.

title: Psalms 35:2–3 (#1)
content:
What does David ask Yahweh to do?

He asks Yahweh to protect him and come to save him.

title: Psalms 35:4 (#1)
content:
What does David want to happen to those who plan to harm him?

David wants them to be turned back and confounded.

title: Psalms 35:5 (#1)
content:
Who does David want to drive away his enemies?

He wants the angel of Yahweh to drive them away.

title: Psalms 35:7 (#1)
content:
What did David’s enemies do without cause?

They tried to kill David as though they had set their net and dug a pit for him to fall into.

title: Psalms 35:8 (#1)
content:
What does David want to happen to his enemies?

David wants destruction to overtake them by surprise, for them to be caught in their own nets, and for them to fall to their destruction.

title: Psalms 35:9 (#1)
content:
In what will David rejoice?

He will rejoice in Yahweh’s salvation.

title: Psalms 35:11–12 (#1)
content:
Why is David sorrowful?

He is sorrowful because unrighteous witnesses rise up to accuse him falsely, and repay him evil for good.

title: Psalms 35:13–14 (#1)
content:
How did David respond to his enemies’ troubles?

David wore sackcloth, fasted for them, went about in grief and bent down in mourning for them.

title: Psalms 35:15–16 (#1)
content:
How did his enemies respond to David’s suffering?

They rejoiced and celebrated and then gathered to attack, slander, and mock him in anger.

title: Psalms 35:17–18 (#1)
content:
When will David thank Yahweh in front of his people?

He will thank Yahweh when he is rescued from his enemies’ destructive attacks.

title: Psalms 35:20 (#1)
content:
What do David’s enemies do instead of speaking peace?

They devise deceitful words against those who live in peace.

title: Psalms 35:22–23 (#1)
content:
What does David want Yahweh to do since he has seen David’s troubles?

He wants Yahweh to not be silent, to not be far away, and to arouse and awake to his defense.

title: Psalms 35:24 (#1)
content:
Why does David say Yahweh should defend him?

He says Yahweh should defend him because of Yahweh’s righteousness.

title: Psalms 36:2 (#1)
content:
How does the wicked man respond to his own sin?

They are so proud that they refuse to recognize how wrongly they act.

title: Psalms 36:3 (#1)
content:
What are the wicked man’s words like?

His words are sinful and deceitful.

title: Psalms 36:3 (#2)
content:
What does the wicked man not want to be?

He does not want to be wise and to do good.

title: Psalms 36:4 (#1)
content:
What does the wicked man do while he lies in bed?

He plans ways to sin while he lies in bed.

title: Psalms 36:5 (#1)
content:
What reaches to the heavens and to the clouds?

Yahweh’s covenant faithfulness reaches to the heavens, and his trustworthiness reaches to the clouds.

title: Psalms 36:6 (#1)
content:
What is Yahweh’s righteousness like?

His righteousness is as permanent as the mountains of God, and his judgments are vast and mysterious as the deepest oceans.

title: Psalms 36:6 (#2)
content:
What does Yahweh take care of?

Yahweh takes care of all living creatures, both people and animals.

title: Psalms 36:7 (#1)
content:
To what does the psalmist compare how God protects people?

God protects people just as a bird shelters its young under its wings.

title: Psalms 36:9 (#1)
content:
Who is the fountain of life by whose light we see?

Yahweh is the one who causes everything to live and makes it possible to understand what is true.

title: Psalms 36:10 (#1)
content:
To whom does David ask God to extend his covenant faithfulness?

David asks God to extend God’s covenant faithfulness fully to those who know God.

title: Psalms 36:11 (#1)
content:
What does David ask God not to let happen?

David asks God not to let the foot of the arrogant man come near him, and the hand of the wicked to drive him away.

title: Psalms 36:12 (#1)
content:
What has happened to the evildoers?

They have fallen and are knocked down and are not able to get up.

title: Psalms 37:1–2 (#1)
content:
Why does David say to not be upset because of evildoers?

He says to not be worried about evildoers because they will soon dry up as the grass and plants wither and die.

title: Psalms 37:4 (#1)
content:
Why does David say to delight in Yahweh?

He says to delight in Yahweh and he will give you the desires of your heart.

title: Psalms 37:5–6 (#1)
content:
Why does David say to trust in Yahweh?

He says to trust in Yahweh and he will act on your behalf, display your justice like the daylight and your innocence like the day at noon.

title: Psalms 37:7 (#1)
content:
What does David say people should do before Yahweh?

David says to be still before Yahweh and wait patiently for him, and to not be angry if someone succeeds with their evil plans.

title: Psalms 37:8–10 (#1)
content:
Why does David say to not be angry and frustrated or to worry about evildoers?

They will be cut off and disappear, but those who wait for Yahweh will inherit the land.

title: Psalms 37:11 (#1)
content:
What will happen to the meek?

They will inherit the land and delight in peacefulness.

title: Psalms 37:14–15 (#1)
content:
What will happen to the wicked who have tried to kill those who are upright?

The swords of the wicked will pierce their own hearts and their bows will be broken.

title: Psalms 37:16–17 (#1)
content:
Why is the little that the righteous have better than the abundance of many wicked people?

The little that the righteous have is better because the arms of the wicked people will be broken, but Yahweh will support the righteous people.

title: Psalms 37:18–19 (#1)
content:
How will Yahweh provide for the blameless?

The blameless will not be ashamed when times are bad, they will have enough to eat, and their heritage will be forever.

title: Psalms 37:20 (#1)
content:
What will happen to Yahweh’s enemies?

His enemies will be like the glory of the pastures which will be consumed and disappear in the smoke.

title: Psalms 37:23–24 (#1)
content:
What is the benefit of having Yahweh establish a man’s steps?

Even if something bad happens to him, he will not fail completely for Yahweh is taking care of him.

title: Psalms 37:25 (#1)
content:
What has David not seen happen to the righteous person?

He has not seen the righteous person abandoned or his children begging for bread.

title: Psalms 37:26 (#1)
content:
How does the righteous person act?

He is gracious, generous, and he lends freely.

title: Psalms 37:27 (#1)
content:
What should people do to live in the land forever?

They should turn away from evil and do what is right.

title: Psalms 37:29 (#1)
content:
What will the righteous inherit?

They will inherit the land and live there forever.

title: Psalms 37:30 (#1)
content:
What does the mouth of the righteous person speak?

The mouth of the righteous person speaks wisdom and increases justice.

title: Psalms 37:32–33 (#1)
content:
What will happen to the righteous person whom the wicked person seeks to kill?

Yahweh will not abandon him into the evil person’s hand nor condemn him when he is judged.

title: Psalms 37:34 (#1)
content:
What will happen to those who wait for Yahweh?

Yahweh will raise them up to possess the land.

title: Psalms 37:35–36 (#1)
content:
What will happen to the wicked and violent person?

He had been powerful but then he passed away and was nowhere to be found.

title: Psalms 37:39–40 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh do for the righteous?

Yahweh protects them in time of trouble, and helps and rescues them.

title: Psalms 38:1 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist ask Yahweh not to do?

He asks Yahweh not to rebuke him in his anger and not to punish him in his wrath.

title: Psalms 38:1–2 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say Yahweh’s discipline feels like to him?

He says he feels as though Yahweh had shot arrows into him and his hand had struck him.

title: Psalms 38:3 (#1)
content:
Why does the psalmist say his whole body is sick?

His whole body is sick because of Yahweh’s anger, and there is no peace in his bones because of his sin.

title: Psalms 38:4 (#1)
content:
How does the psalmist describe his iniquities?

He says his iniquities overwhelm him and are a burden too heavy for him to bear.

title: Psalms 38:5 (#1)
content:
What has happened to the psalmist’s wounds?

His wounds are infected and smell because of his foolish sins.

title: Psalms 38:6 (#1)
content:
How does the psalmist describe his daily condition?

He is stooped over and humiliated every day, and he goes about mourning all day long.

title: Psalms 38:7 (#1)
content:
What fills the psalmist within?

He is filled with burning from within, and there is no health in his flesh.

title: Psalms 38:8 (#1)
content:
How does the psalmist describe the extent of his suffering?

He is numb and utterly crushed, and he groans because of the anguish of his heart.

title: Psalms 38:9 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say the Lord knows about him?

The Lord understands his heart’s deepest yearnings, and his groanings are not hidden from the Lord.

title: Psalms 38:10 (#1)
content:
What three things does the psalmist say are happening to him physically?

His heart is pounding, his strength is fading, and his eyesight is dimming.

title: Psalms 38:11 (#1)
content:
How do the psalmist’s friends and neighbors respond to his condition?

His friends and loved ones shun him because of his condition, and his relatives stand far away.

title: Psalms 38:12 (#1)
content:
What do those who seek the psalmist’s life do to him?

They lay snares for him and speak destructive and deceitful words against him all day long.

title: Psalms 38:13–14 (#1)
content:
How does the psalmist respond to those who seek to harm him?

He acts like a deaf man who hears nothing and a mute man who says nothing in reply.

title: Psalms 38:15 (#1)
content:
In whom does the psalmist place his hope?

He waits for Yahweh and trusts that the Lord his God will answer him.

title: Psalms 38:16 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist fear will happen if his foot slips?

He fears his enemies will rejoice and gloat over him.

title: Psalms 38:17 (#1)
content:
What two things does the psalmist say about his current situation?

He says he is about to stumble and that he is in constant pain.

title: Psalms 38:18 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist confess to Yahweh?

He confesses his guilt and says he is troubled about his sin.

title: Psalms 38:19–20 (#1)
content:
How do the psalmist’s enemies treat him?

His enemies are numerous, hate him without cause, repay him evil for good, and accuse him even though he has pursued what is good.

title: Psalms 38:20 (#1)
content:
How do his enemies repay the good he has done?

They repay David evil for good and they hurl accusations at him.

title: Psalms 38:21 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist ask Yahweh not to do?

He asks Yahweh not to abandon him and not to stay far away from him.

title: Psalms 38:21–22 (#1)
content:
What names does David use when he asks Yahweh for help?

He calls him, “Yahweh”, “God”, “Lord”, and “my salvation.”

title: Psalms 38:22 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist ask Yahweh to do?

He asks Yahweh to come quickly to help him.

title: Psalms 39:1 (#1)
content:
What did David decide to do?

David decided to watch what he said so that he would not sin with his tongue. He would keep silent while in the presence of an evil man.

title: Psalms 39:2–3 (#1)
content:
What happened when David kept silent and kept back his words from saying anything good?

David’s pain grew worse, and his heart became hot and burned like a fire when he thought about what was happening.

title: Psalms 39:4 (#1)
content:
What does David want to know about his life?

David wants to know when his life will end, how long his days are, and how transient he is.

title: Psalms 39:5 (#1)
content:
What does David say his life is like before Yahweh?

David’s lifetime is like nothing before Yahweh.

title: Psalms 39:6 (#1)
content:
What does David say everyone hurries to do?

David says everyone hurries to accumulate riches, even though they do not know who will receive them after they die.

title: Psalms 39:7 (#1)
content:
Who is David’s only hope?

The Lord is David’s only hope.

title: Psalms 39:8 (#1)
content:
What does David ask the Lord to rescue him from?

David asks the Lord to rescue him from his sins.

title: Psalms 39:8 (#2)
content:
Of what does David not want to be the object?

David does not want to be the object of the ridicule of foolish people.

title: Psalms 39:9 (#1)
content:
How does David respond to what the Lord did?

David is silent and does not open his mouth.

title: Psalms 39:10 (#1)
content:
What does David ask the Lord to stop?

David asks the Lord to stop punishing him as he feels he is about to die.

title: Psalms 39:11 (#1)
content:
What happens when the Lord disciplines people for sin?

When the Lord disciplines people for sin, he destroys what they treasure, and only gives them a short time to live.

title: Psalms 39:12 (#1)
content:
Why does David ask Yahweh to hear his prayer?

David asks because he is living before Yahweh on earth only for a short time, a refugee like all his ancestors were.

title: Psalms 39:13 (#1)
content:
What does David ask Yahweh to do before David dies?

David asks Yahweh to leave him alone so that David may be happy again before he dies.

title: Psalms 40:1 (#1)
content:
What did Yahweh do after David waited patiently for him?

Yahweh listened to David and heard his cry.

title: Psalms 40:2 (#1)
content:
What did Yahweh do for David?

Yahweh rescued David from the terrible things that had been happening to him as if he’d been in a pit of mud but was lifted out onto a safe and solid rock.

title: Psalms 40:3 (#1)
content:
What will many do because God has put a new song in David’s mouth?

Many will see it and honor him and will trust in Yahweh.

title: Psalms 40:4 (#1)
content:
Who is blessed?

The man is blessed who makes Yahweh his trust and does not honor the proud or those who turn away from Yahweh to lies.

title: Psalms 40:5 (#1)
content:
How does David describe God’s deeds and thoughts?

God’s wonderful deeds are many and his thoughts about us cannot be numbered.

title: Psalms 40:7–8 (#1)
content:
What is written about David in the scroll of God’s law?

It is written that he delights to do God’s will and that he deeply treasures God’s laws.

title: Psalms 40:9 (#1)
content:
What has David proclaimed in the great assembly?

He has proclaimed good news of God’s righteousness in the great assembly.

title: Psalms 40:10 (#1)
content:
What has David not concealed?

He has not concealed God’s righteousness in his heart nor God’s covenant faithfulness nor trustworthiness from the great assembly.

title: Psalms 40:11 (#1)
content:
What does David pray that Yahweh will do for him?

David prays that Yahweh not keep back his acts of mercy from David, but rather, let Yahweh’s covenant faithfulness and his trustworthiness always preserve David.

title: Psalms 40:12 (#1)
content:
What does David say is happening to him?

Troubles that cannot be numbered surround him, and his iniquities have caught up with him so that he can no longer see clearly. They are more than the hairs on his head, and his heart has failed him.

title: Psalms 40:13 (#1)
content:
What does David pray that Yahweh will be pleased to do?

He prays that Yahweh will be pleased to rescue him.

title: Psalms 40:14 (#1)
content:
What does David pray will happen to those who pursue his life?

He prays that they have shame and be completely disappointed, and that they be turned back and brought to dishonor.

title: Psalms 40:16 (#1)
content:
What does David pray for those who seek Yahweh and love his salvation?

He prays that they rejoice and be glad in Yahweh, and that they say continually, “May Yahweh be great.”

title: Psalms 40:17 (#1)
content:
How does David describe the Lord?

The Lord thinks about him, is his help, and comes to David’s rescue.

title: Psalms 41:1 (#1)
content:
Who does David say is the one who is blessed?

The one who is helps powerless people has a good life.

title: Psalms 41:1–2 (#1)
content:
What will Yahweh do for the person who considers the lowly?

Yahweh will rescue him, preserve him and keep him alive, and he will be happy on the earth.

title: Psalms 41:2 (#1)
content:
What will Yahweh not do to the blessed person?

Yahweh will not turn him over to the will of his enemies.

title: Psalms 41:3 (#1)
content:
What will Yahweh do for the blessed person on the bed of suffering?

Yahweh will support him on the bed of suffering and make his bed of sickness into a bed of healing.

title: Psalms 41:4 (#1)
content:
Why did David ask Yahweh to have mercy on him?

He asked Yahweh to be gracious to him because he had sinned against Yahweh.

title: Psalms 41:5 (#1)
content:
What evil do his enemies speak against David?

They ask when he will die and his name will perish.

title: Psalms 41:6 (#1)
content:
What does David’s enemy say to him?

His enemy says worthless things.

title: Psalms 41:7 (#1)
content:
What do those who hate David whisper and hope for?

Those who hate David whisper together against him and plan for his hurt.

title: Psalms 41:9 (#1)
content:
