What has David’s own close friend in whom he trusted done?

His own close friend has betrayed him.

title: Psalms 41:10 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist ask Yahweh to do for him?

The psalmist asks Yahweh to have mercy on him and raise him up so that he can pay back his enemies.

title: Psalms 41:11 (#1)
content:
How does David know that Yahweh delights in him?

David knows this because his enemy does not triumph over him.

title: Psalms 41:12 (#1)
content:
How does Yahweh help David?

Yahweh upholds him in his integrity and will keep David before his face forever.

title: Psalms 41:13 (#1)
content:
When may Yahweh be praised?

Yahweh may be praised from always, from everlasting to everlasting.

title: Psalms 42:1 (#1)
content:
How does the psalmist describe his longing for God?

He says his soul longs for God just as a deer pants for streams of water.

title: Psalms 42:2 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say his soul does?

His soul thirsts for God, for the living God.

title: Psalms 42:3 (#1)
content:
What has the psalmist’s crying become for him?

His weeping has taken the place of his food day and night.

title: Psalms 42:4 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist call to mind?

He calls to mind how he went with the crowd and led them in procession to the house of God with a voice of rejoicing and praise.

title: Psalms 42:5 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist tell his soul to do?

He tells his soul to wait for God, for he will again thank God, the one who brings him salvation.

title: Psalms 42:7 (#1)
content:
What do the psalmists say passes over them?

He says all of God’s breakers and waves pass over him.

title: Psalms 42:8 (#2)
content:
What happens at night for the psalmist?

At night, God’s song is with the psalmist, a prayer to the God of his life.

title: Psalms 42:8 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh command in the daytime?

Yahweh commands his covenant faithfulness in the daytime.

title: Psalms 42:9 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say to God, his rock?

He asks why God has forgotten him, and why David walks about mourning because of the oppression of the enemy.

title: Psalms 42:10 (#1)
content:
What do the psalmist’s enemies say to him, and how does it affect him?

They mock him all day by asking where his God is, and it feels like crushing pain in his bones.

title: Psalms 42:11 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist tell his soul at the end of the psalm?

He tells his soul to wait for God, for he will again praise God, who saves him.

title: Psalms 43:1 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist ask God to do for him?

He asks God to vindicate him and plead his case against a nation that is not faithful.

title: Psalms 43:2 (#1)
content:
Why does the psalmist appeal to God to vindicate him?

He appeals to God because God is the God of his refuge.

title: Psalms 43:3 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist ask God’s light and faithfulness to do?

He asks them to lead him and bring him to the mountain of God’s holiness and to God’s dwellings.

title: Psalms 43:4 (#2)
content:
What will the psalmist do with the lyre?

He will thank God with the lyre.

title: Psalms 43:4 (#1)
content:
Where does the psalmist want to come when God brings him there?

He wants to come to the altar of God.

title: Psalms 43:5 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist tell his soul to do instead of being cast down?

He tells his soul to wait for God, for he will again thank God who is his salvation and his God.

title: Psalms 44:1 (#1)
content:
What have the psalmists heard with their ears?

They have heard what work God did in their days, in the days of old.

title: Psalms 44:2 (#1)
content:
What did God do with his hand?

God drove out the nations with his hand and planted the people of Israel.

title: Psalms 44:3 (#1)
content:
How did the Israelites obtain the land?

They did not obtain the land by their own sword or by their own arm, but by God’s right hand because he favored them.

title: Psalms 44:5 (#1)
content:
What do the Israelites do through God?

Through God they defeat their enemies, and through God’s name they trample those who rise up against them.

title: Psalms 44:6 (#1)
content:
In what does the psalmist not trust?

He does not trust in his bow, and his sword does not save him.

title: Psalms 44:7 (#1)
content:
From what does God save them?

God saves them from their enemies and shames those who hate them.

title: Psalms 44:9 (#1)
content:
What has God done?

God has rejected and humiliated them and no longer goes out with their armies.

title: Psalms 44:10 (#2)
content:
What do those who hate the Israelites do?

Those who hate them take spoil for themselves.

title: Psalms 44:10 (#1)
content:
What does God make the Israelites do?

God makes them turn back from the adversary.

title: Psalms 44:11 (#1)
content:
What has God made the Israelites like?

God has made them like sheep destined for slaughter and has scattered them as slaves among the nations.

title: Psalms 44:13 (#1)
content:
What has God made the Israelites to their neighbors?

God has made them a reproach to their neighbors, a scorn and a derision to those around them.

title: Psalms 44:15–16 (#1)
content:
Why is the psalmist’s dishonor before him all the day long?

His dishonor is before him, and the shame of his face has covered him because of the voice of him who rebukes and insults, because of the enemy and the avenger.

title: Psalms 44:17 (#1)
content:
What have the Israelites not done?

They have not forgotten God nor dealt falsely with God’s covenant.

title: Psalms 44:18 (#1)
content:
What have the Israelites’ heart and steps not done?

Their heart has not turned back, nor have their steps turned aside from God’s way.

title: Psalms 44:19 (#1)
content:
What has God done to them?

God has allowed their enemies to ruin their land as if darkness has covered it.

title: Psalms 44:20–21 (#1)
content:
What would God discover?

God would discover whether they had forgotten the name of their God or spread out their hands to a foreign god.

title: Psalms 44:22 (#1)
content:
What are the Israelites considered to be because of God?

They are considered to be like sheep for slaughter.

title: Psalms 44:25 (#1)
content:
What has happened to the Israelites?

They are helpless as if they had fallen down and could not get up.

title: Psalms 44:26 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist pray that God would do?

He prays that God might rise up for their help and redeem them for the sake of God’s covenant faithfulness.

title: Psalms 45:1 (#1)
content:
What is the psalmist reciting to the king?

He is reciting his works to the king.

title: Psalms 45:2 (#1)
content:
How does the psalmist describe the king?

The king is fairer than the sons of man, grace is poured onto his lips, and God has blessed him forever.

title: Psalms 45:4 (#1)
content:
Why should the king ride out?

The king should ride out for the sake of truth, humility, and righteousness.

title: Psalms 45:5 (#1)
content:
How are the king’s arrows described?

His arrows are sharp as if piercing the hearts of the king’s enemies.

title: Psalms 45:6 (#1)
content:
How is God’s throne and a scepter of justice described?

His throne is forever and ever, and a scepter of justice is the scepter of God’s kingdom.

title: Psalms 45:7 (#1)
content:
What has the king loved and hated?

He loves righteousness and hates wickedness.

title: Psalms 45:8 (#1)
content:
Of what do all of the king’s garments smell?

All of his garments smell of myrrh, aloes, and cassia.

title: Psalms 45:9 (#1)
content:
Where are the daughters of kings and the queen?

Daughters of kings are among the king’s precious ones, and the queen stands at his right hand adorned in gold of Ophir.

title: Psalms 45:12 (#1)
content:
What will the rich do?

The rich among the people will beg for a favor.

title: Psalms 45:14 (#1)
content:
Where will the royal daughter be led?

She will be led to the king in embroidered dress.

title: Psalms 45:15 (#1)
content:
How and where will the virgins be led?

They will be led by joy and rejoicing; they will enter into the palace of the king.

title: Psalms 45:16 (#1)
content:
Who will take the place of the king’s fathers?

His sons will take the place of his fathers, and he will make them princes throughout all the earth.

title: Psalms 45:17 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist want the peoples of all generations to do regarding the king?

The psalmist wants to make the king’s name remembered in every generation, so the peoples will thank him forever and ever.

title: Psalms 46:1 (#1)
content:
How does the psalmist describe God?

God is a refuge and strength to them, and he greatly helps them in trouble.

title: Psalms 46:2 (#1)
content:
What do the psalmists say they will not do, even if the earth changes and the mountains shake into the sea?

They will not fear.

title: Psalms 46:4 (#1)
content:
What makes the city of God rejoice?

The channels of a stream make the city of God rejoice.

title: Psalms 46:5 (#1)
content:
What will the city of God not do?

The city of God will not be shaken.

title: Psalms 46:6 (#1)
content:
What happens to the earth when God utters his voice after the nations roar and kingdoms shake?

The earth melts.

title: Psalms 46:7 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say about Yahweh of armies and the God of Jacob?

Yahweh of armies is with them, and the God of Jacob is a stronghold to them.

title: Psalms 46:9 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh do to wars?

He makes wars cease to the end of the earth. He shatters the bow and cuts the spear in pieces, and he burns the wagons with fire.

title: Psalms 46:10 (#1)
content:
What does God tell the people to do?

Be still and know that he is God.

title: Psalms 46:10 (#2)
content:
What will happen to God among the nations?

He will be exalted among the nations and on the earth.

title: Psalms 46:11 (#1)
content:
What is the God of Jacob to them?

The God of Jacob is a stronghold to them.

title: Psalms 47:1–2 (#1)
content:
Why does the psalmist tell everyone to clap their hands and shout to God with a voice of rejoicing?

They should do this because Yahweh Most High is to be feared, and he is the great King over all the earth.

title: Psalms 47:3 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh do to peoples and nations?

He subdues peoples under the Israelites and the nations under their feet.

title: Psalms 47:5 (#1)
content:
How has God gone up?

God has gone up with a shout and the sound of a shofar.

title: Psalms 47:6–7 (#1)
content:
Why should everyone sing praises to God?

They should sing praises because God is the King of all the earth.

title: Psalms 47:8 (#1)
content:
Where does God reign?

God reigns over the nations.

title: Psalms 47:8 (#2)
content:
Where does God sit?

God sits on his holy throne.

title: Psalms 47:9 (#1)
content:
Where will the nobles of the peoples gather?

They will gather to the people of the God of Abraham.

title: Psalms 47:9 (#2)
content:
Why will the nobles gather to the people of the God of Abraham?

They will gather because God is greatly exalted.

title: Psalms 48:1 (#1)
content:
How does the psalmist describe Yahweh?

Yahweh is great and is greatly praised.

title: Psalms 48:2 (#1)
content:
How is Mount Zion described?

Mount Zion is high and beautiful, and it is a joy to all the earth.

title: Psalms 48:3 (#1)
content:
How is God known in the city?

God is known as a stronghold.

title: Psalms 48:4–6 (#1)
content:
What happened when the kings assembled themselves together and saw the city?

They marveled, became terrified, and hurried away; trembling seized them there.

title: Psalms 48:8 (#1)
content:
What will God do for the city of Yahweh of armies?

God will establish it forever.

title: Psalms 48:9 (#1)
content:
What have the worshippers compared in the midst of God’s temple?

They have compared God’s covenant faithfulness.

title: Psalms 48:10 (#1)
content:
How does the psalmist describe God’s right hand?

His right hand is full of righteousness.

title: Psalms 48:11 (#1)
content:
Why should Mount Zion rejoice and the daughters of Judah be glad?

They should rejoice and be glad because of God’s judgments.

title: Psalms 48:13 (#1)
content:
Why should the Israelites walk around Zion, count her towers, and consider her citadels?

They should do these things so that they may tell it to a later generation.

title: Psalms 48:14 (#1)
content:
What will God be for his people?

He will be their guide until death.

title: Psalms 49:1–2 (#1)
content:
Who does the psalmist call to hear him?

He calls all the people of the world to hear him, both common people and the wealthy alike.

title: Psalms 49:3 (#1)
content:
With what will the psalmist speak?

He will think carefully and speak with wisdom to help them understand things better.

title: Psalms 49:3 (#2)
content:
What will be the meditation of the psalmist’s heart?

The psalmist will speak of the things he has thought carefully about so they will have better understanding.

title: Psalms 49:6–7 (#1)
content:
What can those who trust in their wealth not do?

Those who trust in their wealth cannot pay God to keep a person from dying.

title: Psalms 49:8 (#1)
content:
How is the redemption of a person’s life costly?

No matter how much money a person has, they can never keep someone else from dying.

title: Psalms 49:9 (#1)
content:
Who can live forever?

No one can live forever or avoid seeing the Pit.

title: Psalms 49:10 (#1)
content:
What happens to the wise, the fool, and the brute alike?

The wise die, and the fool and the brute alike perish, and they leave their wealth to others.

title: Psalms 49:12 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say about a human regarding honor?

A human does not abide in honor but is likened to the beasts, which are destroyed.

title: Psalms 49:14 (#1)
content:
Who will be their shepherd?

It is as if death were a shepherd keeping them in the place where dead people are.

title: Psalms 49:14 (#2)
content:
What will the upright do someday?

One day God will make the upright rule over wicked people.

title: Psalms 49:15 (#1)
content:
What will God do for the psalmist?

God will rescue him from Sheol but will take him to himself.

title: Psalms 49:16 (#1)
content:
When does the psalmist say not to fear?

People should not be troubled when a man becomes rich and has many valuable possessions.

title: Psalms 49:18 (#1)
content:
According to the psalmist, when do people praise others?

People praise anyone who does well for themselves.

title: Psalms 49:19 (#2)
content:
What will the rich man and his fathers not see?

They will never see the light again.

title: Psalms 49:19 (#1)
content:
Where will the rich man go?

He will go to where his dead ancestors are.

title: Psalms 50:1 (#1)
content:
What does the psalm say that Yahweh does in the opening verse?

Yahweh speaks and summons the earth from where the sun rises to where it sets.

title: Psalms 50:4 (#1)
content:
Why does God call to the heavens above and to the earth?

He calls to the heavens above and to the earth so that he may judge his people.

title: Psalms 50:8 (#1)
content:
Of what does God say he will not accuse his people?

God says he will not accuse them regarding their sacrifices.

title: Psalms 50:10 (#1)
content:
Why does God say that he will take no bull or goat from his people?

God says that every beast of the forest is his, and the cattle on a thousand hills.

title: Psalms 50:14 (#1)
content:
What does God command his people to offer and to pay?

God commands them to offer a thank offering and to pay their vows to the Most High.

title: Psalms 50:17 (#1)
content:
What does God say the wicked hate and cast away?

God says that the wicked hate instruction and cast away his words.

title: Psalms 50:21 (#1)
content:
What does God say that the wicked think about him when God keeps silent?

They thought that he was someone just like them.

title: Psalms 50:22 (#1)
content:
Who will rescue the wicked when God tears them in pieces?

There will be no one to come deliver them.

title: Psalms 50:23 (#1)
content:
To whom will God show his salvation?

God will show his salvation to whoever offers a thank offering and orders their path rightly.

acai.preferred_label: Bring Honor and Glory on Oneself

title: Psalms 51:1 (#1)
content:
Why does David say that God should have mercy on him?

He says God should have mercy on him according to his covenant faithfulness.

title: Psalms 51:4 (#1)
content:
Against whom does David say he has sinned?

He says he has sinned against God, and only against God.

title: Psalms 51:5 (#1)
content:
When does David say that his sin began?

David says his sin began as soon as his mother conceived him.

title: Psalms 51:7 (#1)
content:
What does David ask God to do so that he may be purified?

He asks God to purify him with hyssop so he will be clean, and to remove his sins so he will be completely pure.

title: Psalms 51:10 (#1)
content:
What does David ask God to create and renew in him?

He asks God to create in him a clean heart, and to renew a loyal spirit within him.

title: Psalms 51:11 (#1)
content:
What does David ask God not to do to him?

He asks God to not cast him away from his presence, and to not take the Spirit of his holiness from him.

title: Psalms 51:12 (#1)
content:
What does David ask God to restore to him?

He asks God to restore to him the joy of his salvation and to support him with a willing spirit.

title: Psalms 51:14 (#1)
content:
What does David ask God to deliver him from?

He asks God to deliver him from the guilt of bloodshed.

title: Psalms 51:16 (#1)
content:
What does David say God does not want from him?

David says God does not delight in sacrifice, and would not accept a burnt offering from him.

title: Psalms 51:17 (#1)
content:
What are the sacrifices God wants?

The sacrifices of God are genuine humility and sorrow for sins.

title: Psalms 52:1 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say protects him all of the day?

The covenant faithfulness of God protects him all day.

title: Psalms 52:3 (#1)
content:
What does Doeg love more than good?

He loves evil more than good.

title: Psalms 52:4 (#1)
content:
What words does Doeg love?

He loves all words of destruction.

title: Psalms 52:5 (#1)
content:
What will God do to Doeg?

God will destroy him forever.

title: Psalms 52:7 (#1)
content:
In what did the man trust instead of God?

He trusted in the abundance of his wealth.

title: Psalms 52:8 (#1)
content:
In what will David place his own trust?

He will trust in the covenant faithfulness of God forever and ever.

title: Psalms 53:1 (#1)
content:
What does the fool say in his heart?

He says that there is no God.

title: Psalms 53:2–3 (#1)
content:
When God looks down from heaven at the people on earth, what does he find?

He finds that they have all turned away and corrupted themselves. There is no one who does good, not even one.

title: Psalms 53:4 (#1)
content:
What do the doers of iniquity do to God’s people?

They take from God’s people as easily as they eat bread, and they do not call upon God.

title: Psalms 53:5 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say happened to those who attacked Israel?

God defeated them and put them to shame, because he despises them.

title: Psalms 53:6 (#1)
content:
From where did David hope that salvation for Israel would come?

He hoped that the salvation of Israel would come from the God of Israel.

title: Psalms 54:1 (#2)
content:
What does David want God to do?

He wants God to save him and to vindicate him so people will realize that he has not done anything wrong.

title: Psalms 54:1 (#1)
content:
How did David ask God to save him?

He asked God to save him by the might of God’s name.

title: Psalms 54:2 (#1)
content:
What does David ask God to hear?

He asks God to hear his prayer and listen to his words.

title: Psalms 54:3 (#1)
content:
Who has risen up against David and sought his life?

Foreigners have risen up against him, and violent ones have sought his life.

title: Psalms 54:4 (#1)
content:
What does David say God is to him?

David says God is a helper to him and to those who sustain his life.

title: Psalms 54:5 (#1)
content:
What will God return to David’s enemies?

God will return harm to his enemies.

title: Psalms 54:6 (#1)
content:
Why will David praise Yahweh’s name?

He will praise Yahweh’s name because it is good.

title: Psalms 54:7 (#1)
content:
What does David say his eye will see after God delivers him from his troubles?

He will see the defeat of his enemies.

title: Psalms 55:4 (#1)
content:
What kind of terrors have fallen on David?

The terrors of death have fallen on him.

title: Psalms 55:6 (#1)
content:
Why does David wish that he had wings like a dove?

If he had wings like a dove, he could fly away and find a place to rest and be safe from his enemies.

title: Psalms 55:9 (#1)
content:
What does David ask the Lord to do to his enemies?

He asks the Lord to destroy them and to make them disagree about what to do.

title: Psalms 55:10–11 (#1)
content:
What is found in the middle of the city?

Iniquity and trouble are in the middle of the city, and calamity, oppression, and deceit are also found there.

title: Psalms 55:12–13 (#1)
content:
Who reproached David and powerfully opposed him?

David’s companion and acquaintance reproached and opposed him.

title: Psalms 55:15 (#1)
content:
What does David ask God to bring upon his enemies?

He asks for desolations to come upon them and for them to go down to Sheol alive.

title: Psalms 55:17 (#1)
content:
What does David do continually?

He complains and moans to God.

title: Psalms 55:19 (#1)
content:
Why will God hear and answer David’s prayer?

He will hear and answer because David’s enemies do not fear God.

title: Psalms 55:20 (#1)
content:
What does David’s friend do to his covenant?

He defiles his covenant by attacking his friends.

title: Psalms 55:23 (#1)
content:
To where will God bring down the wicked?

God will bring them down to the pit of the grave.

title: Psalms 56:1 (#1)
content:
Why does David ask God to be gracious to him?

He asks God to be gracious to him because men are fighting with him and oppressing him.

title: Psalms 56:2 (#1)
content:
What do David’s enemies do to him all day?

David’s enemies attack him and fight against him arrogantly.

title: Psalms 56:3 (#1)
content:
What does David say he will do when he is afraid?

When David is afraid, he will trust in God.

title: Psalms 56:4 (#1)
content:
What is the result of David’s trust in God?

David trusts in God, so he will not fear.

title: Psalms 56:5 (#1)
content:
What do David’s enemies do all day?

David’s enemies continually interfere and plan ways to harm him.

title: Psalms 56:5 (#2)
content:
What are David’s enemies’ thoughts toward David?

All their thoughts are against David for harm.

title: Psalms 56:7 (#1)
content:
How does David ask God to deal with David’s enemies?

David asks God to bring them down in defeat.

title: Psalms 56:8 (#1)
content:
What does David ask God to do with his tears?

David asks God to keep a record of his tears.

title: Psalms 56:9 (#1)
content:
When will David’s enemies turn back?

David’s enemies will turn back on the day that he calls to God.

title: Psalms 56:12 (#1)
content:
What does David vow to give to God?

David vows to pay a thank-offering to God.

title: Psalms 56:13 (#1)
content:
Where does David walk before God?

David walks before God in this world of the living.

title: Psalms 57:1 (#2)
content:
For how long does David take refuge in God?

David takes refuge in God until the calamities have passed by.

title: Psalms 57:1 (#1)
content:
Why does David ask God to be gracious to him?

He asks God to be gracious to him because he depends on God for protection.

title: Psalms 57:2 (#1)
content:
What does David say God does for him?

David says that God is the one who accomplishes things for him.

title: Psalms 57:3 (#1)
content:
What does David say God will send out to him?

David says that God will send out to him God’s covenant faithfulness and his truth.

title: Psalms 57:4 (#1)
content:
Among whom does David say he must lie down?

He must lie down among men who are as dangerous as lions and trying to kill him.

title: Psalms 57:5 (#1)
content:
Where does David ask God to let his glory be?

David asks God to let his glory be above all the heavens and all the earth.

title: Psalms 57:6 (#1)
content:
What does David say happens to those who dig a pit in front of him?

They themselves fall into the midst of it.

title: Psalms 57:8 (#1)
content:
What musical instruments does David call to wake up?

David calls the lyre and harp to wake up.

title: Psalms 57:9 (#1)
content:
Where will David give thanks to the Lord?

David will give thanks to the Lord among the peoples.

title: Psalms 57:9 (#2)
content:
Where will David sing praise to the Lord?

David will sing songs of praise to the Lord among the nations.

title: Psalms 57:11 (#1)
content:
Where does David ask for God’s glory to be exalted?

David asks for God’s glory to be exalted over all the heavens and all the earth.

title: Psalms 58:2 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say the sons of man do on the earth?

The sons of man commit violent crimes on the earth.

title: Psalms 58:3 (#1)
content:
When does David say the wicked go astray?

They go astray from the time when they are born.

title: Psalms 58:7 (#1)
content:
What does David ask God to do when the wicked try to harm people?

David asks God to keep them from hurting people, as if they were shooting arrows that had no heads.

title: Psalms 58:10 (#1)
content:
When will the righteous rejoice?

The righteous will rejoice when he sees God punish the wicked people.

title: Psalms 59:1 (#1)
content:
How does David ask God to deliver him from his enemies?

He asks God to set him on high, away from those who rise up against him.

title: Psalms 59:3 (#1)
content:
Who gather themselves together against David?

The mighty gather themselves together against David.

title: Psalms 59:5 (#1)
content:
Who does David ask Yahweh to not be merciful to?

He asks Yahweh to not be gracious to wicked people who are treacherous workers of iniquity.

title: Psalms 59:10 (#1)
content:
What does David say the God of his covenant faithfulness will do?

David says that the God of his covenant faithfulness will meet him and will defeat his enemies.

title: Psalms 59:13 (#1)
content:
How does David ask God to consume his enemies?

He asks God to consume them in wrath, and to consume them so that they will be no more.

title: Psalms 59:16 (#1)
content:
What does David say when he sings about God’s strength?

He says God is his stronghold and a refuge in the day of trouble.

title: Psalms 60:1 (#1)
content:
What has God done to the Israelites?

He has rejected them, become angry with them, and stopped helping them.

title: Psalms 60:2 (#1)
content:
What has God done to the earth?

He has made the earth tremble and has broken it apart.

title: Psalms 60:3 (#1)
content:
What has God made his people see?

He has made them see great difficulties.

title: Psalms 60:4 (#1)
content:
To whom has God given a banner?

He has given a banner to those who fear him.

title: Psalms 60:6 (#1)
content:
What does God say he will do with Shechem and the Valley of Succoth?

He says he will rejoice as he divides Shechem and measures out the Valley of Succoth for the Israelites to live in.

title: Psalms 60:8 (#1)
content:
What does God say he will do to Edom?

He says he will throw his sandal over Edom to show that it belongs to him.

title: Psalms 60:10 (#1)
content:
What does God not do for their armies?

He does not go out with their armies to enable them to defeat their enemies.

title: Psalms 60:11–12 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist ask God to do for them?

The psalmist asks God to give them help against their enemy.

title: Psalms 61:1 (#1)
content:
What does David ask God to do for him?

David asks God to hear his cry and to listen to his prayer.

title: Psalms 61:3 (#1)
content:
What has God been like for David?

God has been like a strong tower, a refuge and place of protection from the enemy for David.

title: Psalms 61:4 (#1)
content:
Where does David wish to live and take refuge?

David wishes to live with and to take refuge in God’s presence forever.

title: Psalms 61:5 (#1)
content:
What did God do for David when he heard his vows?

God gave him the blessings of those who honor God’s name.

title: Psalms 61:6 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist ask God to do for the king?

The psalmist asks God to add more years to the king’s life and to allow his descendants to rule after him.

title: Psalms 61:8 (#1)
content:
Why will David sing praise to God’s name forever?

David will sing praise to God’s name forever because he has vowed to do this each day as long as God lets him live.

title: Psalms 62:1 (#1)
content:
Why does David say his soul is in silence before God?

David says his soul is in silence before God because he knows that his salvation comes from God.

title: Psalms 62:2 (#1)
content:
What does David say God is to him?

David says God alone is his salvation and his protection, like a rock he could climb onto in order to be safe.

title: Psalms 62:4 (#1)
content:
How do David’s enemies treat him?

They plot together to bring him down from his high position, they delight in lies, and they bless with their mouths, but in their hearts they curse him.

title: Psalms 62:8 (#1)
content:
What does David tell the people to do?

He tells the people to trust in God always and to pour out their hearts before God.

title: Psalms 62:9 (#1)
content:
How does David describe ordinary people and important people?

Ordinary people lack power, and important people are not as powerful as they seem to be.

title: Psalms 62:10 (#1)
content:
What does David warn people not to trust in?

David warns people not to trust in oppression or robbery, and if wealth increases, not to set their hearts on it.

title: Psalms 62:11 (#1)
content:
What has David heard when God has spoken?

David has heard God say that he is the one who truly is powerful.

title: Psalms 62:12 (#1)
content:
To whom does covenant faithfulness belong?

Covenant faithfulness belongs to the Lord, who repays each person according to what he has done.

title: Psalms 63:1 (#1)
content:
How does David seek God?

He seeks God earnestly, his soul thirsts for him, and his body aches for him.

title: Psalms 63:2 (#1)
content:
What does David see when he gazes at God in the sanctuary?

He sees God’s power and glory.

title: Psalms 63:3–4 (#1)
content:
What will David do because of God’s covenant faithfulness?

David will praise God as long as he lives, he will bless God, and he will lift up his hands and pray to God.

title: Psalms 63:5 (#1)
content:
What does David compare his satisfaction in God to?

He compares his satisfaction in God to eating rich food, and he praises God joyfully.

title: Psalms 63:6 (#1)
content:
When does David meditate on God?

He thinks about God when on his bed and meditates on God in the night watches.

title: Psalms 63:7 (#1)
content:
Why does David shout joyfully?

He shouts joyfully because he is aware that God protects him just as a mother bird protects her chicks under her wings.

title: Psalms 63:8 (#1)
content:
Who upholds David?

The right hand of God upholds and protects David.

title: Psalms 63:9–10 (#1)
content:
What will happen to those who seek to destroy David’s life?

They will go into the lowest parts of the earth, they will die by the sword, and wild dogs will eat their corpses.

title: Psalms 63:11 (#2)
content:
What will happen to those who speak falsehood?

Those who speak falsehood will have their mouths shut.

title: Psalms 63:11 (#1)
content:
What will happen to those who swear by God?

Those who swear by God will exult in him and praise him.

title: Psalms 64:1 (#1)
content:
What is David asking God to do?

He wants God to hear his voice and to preserve his life from fear of his enemies.

title: Psalms 64:2 (#1)
content:
From what does David ask God to hide him?

He asks God to hide him from the secret plans of evildoers and from those who do evil things.

title: Psalms 64:3 (#1)
content:
What do David’s enemies do with their tongues?

They speak hostile things and cruel words which are like sharp swords.

title: Psalms 64:4 (#1)
content:
At whom do David’s enemies speak their cruel words?

They falsely accuse someone who is innocent like a person who shoots an arrow from a hiding place.

title: Psalms 64:5 (#1)
content:
What do David’s enemies say when they encourage each other to plan evil and to deceive people?

They say, “Who will see us?”

title: Psalms 64:7 (#1)
content:
How will God respond to David’s enemies?

God will judge and punish them, as if he were shooting an arrow and wounding them.

title: Psalms 64:8 (#1)
content:
Because of God’s actions, what will happen to the enemy?

The enemy will get into trouble because of their own tongue, and everyone who sees them will flee.

title: Psalms 64:9 (#1)
content:
How will all people respond when God judges David’s enemies?

All people will fear, tell others about God’s works, and consider what God has done.

title: Psalms 64:10 (#1)
content:
What will the righteous and all the upright in heart do?

The righteous people will rejoice in Yahweh and will trust in him for protection, and all the upright in heart will celebrate.

title: Psalms 65:1 (#1)
content:
To whom does the psalmist say a vow will be paid?

The psalmist says a vow will be paid to God in Zion.

title: Psalms 65:3 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say God will do about their transgressions?

The psalmist says God will forgive their transgressions.

title: Psalms 65:4 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say about the person God chooses and brings near to dwell in his courts?

That person is happy and will be satisfied with the goodness of God’s house and the holiness of his temple.

title: Psalms 65:5 (#1)
content:
How does the psalmist say God answers those who call to him?

God answers by doing fearsome things in righteousness.

title: Psalms 65:7 (#1)
content:
What does God quiet?

He quiets the roar of the seas and their waves, as well as the nations.

title: Psalms 65:8 (#1)
content:
How do people who live at the ends of the earth respond to God’s signs?

They fear and respect God and celebrate when they see his signs and actions.

title: Psalms 65:9 (#1)
content:
How does the psalmist say God helps the earth?

God waters it, enriches it, and prepares the earth to provide grain for its people.

title: Psalms 65:11 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say God crowns the year with?

God crowns the year with fields that are glorious with crops, as if he had put a golden crown on them and provides food in abundance.

title: Psalms 65:13 (#1)
content:
With what are the meadows and valleys covered?

The meadows are covered with flocks of sheep and goats, and the valleys are covered with grain.

title: Psalms 66:1 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist tell all the earth to do?

He tells everyone to shout to God and to joyfully praise him.

title: Psalms 66:3 (#1)
content:
What causes God’s enemies to cringe before him?

The greatness of God’s power causes his enemies to cringe before him.

title: Psalms 66:6 (#1)
content:
What miraculous deed did God do for his people?

He turned the sea into dry land so that the people passed through the river on foot.

title: Psalms 66:9 (#1)
content:
What does God do for his people?

He keeps them alive and does not allow anyone to destroy them.

title: Psalms 66:10 (#1)
content:
How has God tested his people?

He has tested them by allowing them to experience difficulties in order to refine them as silver is refined.

title: Psalms 66:12 (#1)
content:
Where did God bring his people out?

He brought them out to a place of abundance.

title: Psalms 66:13 (#1)
content:
With what will the psalmist come into God’s house?

He will come into God’s house with burnt offerings as he promised.

title: Psalms 66:15 (#1)
content:
What will the psalmist offer to God?

He will offer burnt offerings of fatlings with the smoke of rams, and also cattle with male goats.

title: Psalms 66:16 (#1)
content:
What will the psalmist declare to all who fear God?

He will declare what God has done for him.

title: Psalms 66:18 (#1)
content:
What would have happened if the psalmist had regarded iniquity in his heart?

The Lord would not have heard and answered his prayer.

title: Psalms 66:20 (#1)
content:
What two things has God not turned away from the psalmist?

God has not turned away the psalmist’s prayer or his covenant faithfulness from the psalmist.

title: Psalms 67:1–2 (#1)
content:
Why should God be gracious to his people and bless them?

He should be gracious and bless them so that his way may be known on the earth and his salvation among all the nations.

title: Psalms 67:3 (#1)
content:
Who should thank God?

All the peoples should thank God.

title: Psalms 67:4 (#1)
content:
Why should the nations rejoice and shout joyfully?

They should rejoice and shout joyfully because God judges the peoples with uprightness and guides the nations on the earth.

title: Psalms 67:6 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say the earth has given?

The earth has given its produce.

title: Psalms 67:7 (#1)
content:
What should happen because God has blessed his people?

All the people of the earth should fear and respect him.

title: Psalms 68:1 (#1)
content:
What does David want to happen to God’s enemies and to those who hate God?

He wants God’s enemies to be scattered and those who hate God to flee from his face.

title: Psalms 68:3 (#1)
content:
What should the righteous do?

The righteous should be glad, rejoice, exult, and be happy before God.

title: Psalms 68:6 (#1)
content:
What does God do for the lonely and the prisoners?

God provides families and homes for lonely people, and he brings prisoners out into prosperity.

title: Psalms 68:7–8 (#1)
content:
What did the earth and heavens do when God went out before his people?

The earth trembled and the heavens poured rain in God’s presence.

title: Psalms 68:9–10 (#1)
content:
What did God provide for his people?

God sent plentiful rain when his inheritance was weary and, in his goodness, he provided homes and food for the poor.

title: Psalms 68:11 (#1)
content:
Who proclaims the good news?

A great crowd of women proclaim the good news.

title: Psalms 68:12–13 (#1)
content:
What do the women who stay at home do when the enemy kings flee?

They divide the plunder, which includes treasures like a dove with silver wings and gold-colored feathers.

title: Psalms 68:16 (#1)
content:
At what does the psalmist say that the mountains might look at in envy?

He says that the mountains might look in envy at the mountain that God desires for his dwelling place, where Yahweh will live forever.

title: Psalms 68:17 (#1)
content:
To what does the psalmist compare the power of God?

The psalmist says that God is so powerful that it is as if he has thousands and thousands of chariots.

title: Psalms 68:19 (#1)
content:
What does the Lord do for his people daily?

The Lord daily helps his people as if he were carrying a heavy load for them.

title: Psalms 68:22 (#1)
content:
From where does the Lord say he will bring back his enemies?

The Lord says he will bring them back from a high mountain or from the depths of the sea.

title: Psalms 68:24–25 (#1)
content:
In what order does the procession of God go into the sanctuary?

The singers go first, the maidens playing timbrels are in the middle, and the musicians playing stringed instruments follow behind.

title: Psalms 68:26 (#1)
content:
Who should bless and praise God in the assembly?

The descendants of Israel should bless and praise God.

title: Psalms 68:27 (#1)
content:
What tribe is leading this parade?

Benjamin, the smallest tribe, is leading this parade.

title: Psalms 68:28 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say God has done for his people?

The psalmist says that God has commanded strength for his people, and he calls on God to show his strength, because God has done great things for them.

title: Psalms 68:30 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist ask God to rebuke?

The psalmist asks God to rebuke the king of Egypt and the armies of mighty nations with their subject peoples.

title: Psalms 68:31 (#1)
content:
Who will come from Egypt?

Nobles will come from Egypt.

title: Psalms 68:32 (#1)
content:
Who should sing praises to God?

The kingdoms of the earth should sing praises to God.

title: Psalms 68:34 (#1)
content:
To whom does the psalmist say strength should be ascribed?

The psalmist says to ascribe strength to God.

title: Psalms 68:35 (#1)
content:
What does God give to his people?

God gives strength and power to his people.

title: Psalms 69:1 (#1)
content:
From what does David ask God to save him?

He asks God to save him from great danger.

title: Psalms 69:3 (#1)
content:
What is happening to David as he waits for his God?

He is weary from calling out, his throat is parched, and his eyes fail.

title: Psalms 69:4 (#1)
content:
How many are David’s enemies who hate him?

There are so many it is as if they are more than the hairs on his head.

title: Psalms 69:5 (#1)
content:
What does God know about David?

God knows about David’s foolishness and about the sins he has committed.

title: Psalms 69:6 (#1)
content:
What does David not want to happen to those who wait for and seek God?

David asks that they not have shame or be humiliated because of him.

title: Psalms 69:9 (#1)
content:
What has consumed David?

Zeal for God’s house has consumed him.

title: Psalms 69:10 (#1)
content:
What did David do that others used to reproach him?

He wept and fasted, but it became a source of reproaches against him.

title: Psalms 69:11–12 (#1)
content:
In what way was David an object of insults?

His enemies made a proverb of him, using him as an example of a foolish person and singing insulting songs about him.

title: Psalms 69:13 (#1)
content:
How does David want Yahweh to answer his prayer?

He asks Yahweh to answer him at a time Yahweh’s choosing, rescuing him because of Yahweh’s own faithful love.

title: Psalms 69:16 (#1)
content:
Why should Yahweh turn to David?

Yahweh should turn to David because Yahweh’s covenant faithfulness is good and his compassion is great.

title: Psalms 69:18 (#1)
content:
What does David ask Yahweh to do because of David’s enemies?

He asks Yahweh to draw near to him, to save him, and to rescue him from his enemies.

title: Psalms 69:21 (#1)
content:
What did David’s enemies give him to eat and drink?

They put poison in his food and gave him vinegar to drink for his thirst.

title: Psalms 69:22 (#1)
content:
What does David want the table of his enemies to become?

He wants his enemies’ table to become a snare and a trap for them.

title: Psalms 69:25 (#1)
content:
What does David want to happen to his enemies’ encampment?

He wants their encampment to be deserted, with no one living in their tents.

title: Psalms 69:27 (#1)
content:
What does David ask Yahweh to add to his enemies?

He asks Yahweh to punish them for all their sins and to not let them enter into Yahweh’s righteousness.

title: Psalms 69:30–31 (#1)
content:
What will please God more than an ox or a bull?

Praising the name of God with a song and magnifying him with thanksgiving will please Yahweh more than an ox or a bull.

title: Psalms 69:33 (#1)
content:
How does Yahweh respond to the needy and his prisoners?

Yahweh hears and answers the needy and does not despise his prisoners.

title: Psalms 69:34 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say should praise God?

The psalmist says that the entire creation: the heavens, the earth, the seas, and everything moving in them should praise God.

title: Psalms 69:35–36 (#1)
content:
What will God do for Zion and the cities of Judah?

God will save Zion and strengthen the cities of Judah so that his people may dwell there and possess it, and the descendants of his servants will inherit it.

title: Psalms 70:1 (#1)
content:
What is David asking Yahweh to do?

David is asking Yahweh to act quickly to rescue him.

title: Psalms 70:2–3 (#1)
content:
What does David want God to do to those who seek after his life?

David wants God to put them to shame and humiliate them, to disgrace them and make them abandon their plans.

title: Psalms 70:4 (#1)
content:
What does David want all those who seek Yahweh to do?

He wants them to rejoice and be glad in Yahweh and to keep saying, “God is great!”

title: Psalms 70:5 (#1)
content:
What does David need from God because he is in difficult circumstances?

David needs God to hurry to help and to save him.

title: Psalms 71:1 (#1)
content:
Where does the psalmist say he takes refuge?

The psalmist says he takes refuge in Yahweh.

title: Psalms 71:2 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist ask Yahweh to do for him?

He asks Yahweh to deliver and rescue him, to consider his situation and save him.

title: Psalms 71:3 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist want Yahweh to be to him?

The psalmist wants Yahweh to be his savior and his protector.

title: Psalms 71:4 (#1)
content:
From whose hand does the psalmist want to be rescued?

He wants to be rescued from the hand of the wicked, and from the one who does wrong and the one who is cruel.

title: Psalms 71:5 (#1)
content:
How long has the psalmist trusted in Yahweh?

He has trusted in Yahweh since he was young.

title: Psalms 71:6 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say that he will do continually?

He says that he will always praise Yahweh.

title: Psalms 71:7 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say about Yahweh?

He says that Yahweh is his refuge and mighty protector.

title: Psalms 71:8 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist ask to do all day?

He asks to be able to praise Yahweh all day.

title: Psalms 71:9 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist ask God not to do when the psalmist is old and his strength fails?

He asks Yahweh not to cast him away or forsake him.

title: Psalms 71:10–11 (#1)
content:
What do the enemies of the psalmist say as they are plotting against him?

They say that God is not helping him, that they should pursue and seize him because God will not save him.

title: Psalms 71:12 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist ask God to do quickly?

The psalmist asks God not to be far from him and to hurry to help him.

title: Psalms 71:13 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist want to happen to those who are hostile to his life?

He wants them to be put to shame and disgraced, and he wants their plans to fail.

title: Psalms 71:14 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say he will continue to do?

The psalmist says he will hope and trust continually and will continue to praise Yahweh.

title: Psalms 71:15 (#1)
content:
What will the psalmist proclaim with his mouth about Yahweh?

He will tell of Yahweh’s righteousness and salvation all day.

title: Psalms 71:16 (#1)
content:
In whose strength does the psalmist say he will come?

The psalmist says he will come in the strength of Lord Yahweh.

title: Psalms 71:17–18 (#1)
content:
Why should Yahweh not forsake the psalmist?

Yahweh should not forsake him because the psalmist is declaring Yahweh’s wonderful doings to the next generation and his power to everyone who is to come.

title: Psalms 71:19 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say about God’s righteousness?

The psalmist says that God’s righteousness reaches to the heights and that no one is like God.

title: Psalms 71:20 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist ask God to do after he has experienced many troubles?

The psalmist asks God to revive him and to give him a good life again.

title: Psalms 71:21–22 (#1)
content:
For what does the psalmist give thanks with his harp?

He gives thanks to God for God’s faithfulness.

title: Psalms 71:23–24 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist do all day long?

He meditates on God’s righteousness all day long.

title: Psalms 72:1 (#1)
content:
What does Solomon ask God to give to the son of the king who is now the king?

Solomon asks God to give the king God’s own judgments and righteousness.

title: Psalms 72:5 (#1)
content:
How long does Solomon want the people to fear God?

He wants them to fear God for as long as the sun and the moon endure, throughout all generations.

title: Psalms 72:6 (#1)
content:
What does Solomon compare the king to?

He compares the king to rain falling on mown grass and to showers drenching the earth.

title: Psalms 72:8 (#1)
content:
How far does Solomon ask that the king rule?

He asks that the king rule from sea to sea and from the River to the ends of the earth.

title: Psalms 72:11 (#1)
content:
What does Solomon want all kings and nations to do?

He wants all kings to bow down to the king and all nations to serve him.

title: Psalms 72:13 (#1)
content:
How does the king treat the weak and the needy?

He has pity on the weak and the needy and saves their lives.

title: Psalms 72:16 (#1)
content:
What does Solomon ask for the land and the people of the cities?

He asks for an abundance of grain in the land and for the people of the cities to flourish like the grass of the earth.

title: Psalms 72:17 (#1)
content:
How long does Solomon ask that the king’s name endure?

He asks that the king’s name endure forever, and continue as long as the sun.

title: Psalms 72:18 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh alone do?

He alone does wonderful things.

title: Psalms 73:1 (#1)
content:
To whom is God good?

God is good to Israel, to those with a pure heart.

title: Psalms 73:2–3 (#1)
content:
Why did Asaph’s feet nearly slip?

He nearly slipped because he was envious of the arrogant when he saw the prosperity of the wicked.

title: Psalms 73:4–5 (#1)
content:
How did Asaph describe the wicked?

He said they have no suffering until they die, they are fat and well fed, they are free from the troubles that other people face, and they are not afflicted like other men.

title: Psalms 73:6 (#1)
content:
What are the characteristics that Asaph ascribes to the wicked?

Asaph says that they are filled with pride and openly display their violent actions.

title: Psalms 73:7 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say about the eyes and heart of the wicked?

Their eyes bulge out from fatness, and they are always thinking of more evil things to do.

title: Psalms 73:8–9 (#1)
content:
What do the wicked say and do?

They mock others and speak of doing evil and oppressive things to them; they speak with pride. They talk as if they are God and boast across the earth.

title: Psalms 73:11 (#1)
content:
What do the wicked say about God?

They say that God does not know or care about what they do, and that the Most High has no knowledge and will not judge their actions.

title: Psalms 73:13–14 (#1)
content:
Why does Asaph feel he guarded his heart in vain?

He has suffered and been punished every day, even though he kept his heart clean and has not committed sinful acts.

title: Psalms 73:15 (#1)
content:
What will happen if Asaph says these things?

He will betray the generation of God’s children.

title: Psalms 73:16–17 (#1)
content:
Where did Asaph go to gain understanding of these things?

Asaph went into the temple of God.

title: Psalms 73:19 (#1)
content:
What happens to the wicked?

They are destroyed in a moment; they come to an end in terrible ways.

title: Psalms 73:22 (#1)
content:
What did Asaph say he was like before God?

He was stupid and ignorant, like an animal before God.

title: Psalms 73:24 (#1)
content:
What will God do for Asaph after guiding him with his counsel?

Afterward, God will take Asaph to glory.

title: Psalms 73:25 (#1)
content:
What does Asaph say he desires?

He desires only God, both in heaven and on earth.

title: Psalms 73:27 (#1)
content:
Who will perish?

Those who are far from God will perish, and God will destroy all those who are unfaithful to him.

title: Psalms 73:28 (#1)
content:
What does Asaph say is good for him?

Being close to God is good for him. He has made Yahweh his refuge so that he can tell about all of God’s works.

title: Psalms 74:2 (#1)
content:
What does Asaph ask God to remember that he did for his people in ancient times?

Asaph asks God to remember his people that he chose long ago and redeemed from slavery to be his own.

title: Psalms 74:4–6 (#1)
content:
What damage did the enemy do in the sanctuary?

They set up their battle flags, swung axes like woodsmen in a forest, and broke down all the carvings with hatchet and hammers.

title: Psalms 74:7 (#1)
content:
What else did they do to the sanctuary?

They set it on fire, burned it down, and profaned the temple.

title: Psalms 74:8 (#1)
content:
What did the enemy do to the meeting places?

They burned all of the meeting places of God in the land.

title: Psalms 74:9 (#1)
content:
What did God’s people not see anymore?

They did not see any more signs, and there was no longer a prophet among them.

title: Psalms 74:12–13 (#1)
content:
Why has God been Asaph’s king since ancient times?

Asaph recognizes God’s work of salvation in the earth and his power to create order out of chaos.

title: Psalms 74:14 (#1)
content:
To what did Asaph compare the power of God?

Asaph compared the power of God to one who could crush the heads of monsters and leave their bodies as food to the desert-dwellers.

title: Psalms 74:16–17 (#1)
content:
What did God set in place?

God established the light and the sun, set all the boundaries of the earth, and formed the seasons of summer and winter.

title: Psalms 74:18 (#1)
content:
What does the enemy do that Asaph wants Yahweh to remember?

Asaph wants Yahweh to remember that Yahweh’s enemies have insulted and mocked him, and that foolish people have despised his name.

title: Psalms 74:20 (#1)
content:
Why does Asaph ask God to regard his covenant?

He asks because violence fills the dark places of the land.

title: Psalms 74:22 (#1)
content:
What does Asaph want God to arise and defend?

Asaph wants God to arise and plead his own cause against the insults of foolish people.

title: Psalms 75:1 (#1)
content:
For what do the people give thanks?

They give thanks because God is near to them, and they tell others about his wonderful deeds.

title: Psalms 75:2–3 (#1)
content:
What will God do at the appointed time?

He will judge everyone fairly and when the earth shakes, he will hold it steady.

title: Psalms 75:4–5 (#1)
content:
What does Asaph tell the boastful and wicked not to do?

He tells them not to boast or brag about their power, and not to speak arrogantly.

title: Psalms 75:7 (#1)
content:
What does Asaph say about God?

God is the judge and he brings some down and raises others up.

title: Psalms 75:8 (#1)
content:
To what does Asaph compare Yahweh’s judgment of the wicked?

Asaph compares Yahweh’s judgment of the wicked to a cup of foaming wine that all the wicked people on earth must drink down to the last drop.

title: Psalms 75:9 (#1)
content:
How will Asaph praise the God of Jacob?

He will continually tell what God has done and sing praises to him and will never stop.

title: Psalms 75:10 (#1)
content:
What does God say he will do to the power of the wicked and the righteous?

He will destroy the power of the wicked and increase the power of the righteous.

title: Psalms 76:2 (#1)
content:
Where does the psalmist say God has his dwelling place?

His dwelling place is on Mount Zion in Jerusalem.

title: Psalms 76:4 (#1)
content:
How does the psalmist describe God?

God is glorious and majestic.

title: Psalms 76:6 (#1)
content:
What happened when the God of Jacob rebuked his enemies?

At his rebuke, both horse and rider fell down dead.

title: Psalms 76:8 (#1)
content:
What happened when God’s judgment came from heaven?

When his judgment came, the earth was afraid and silent.

title: Psalms 76:10 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say the anger of people will do?

Even the anger of people will bring God praise.

title: Psalms 76:11 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say people should do regarding vows to Yahweh their God?

They should make vows to Yahweh their God and keep them.

title: Psalms 76:12 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say God does to princes and kings?

God humbles the spirit of princes, and kings of the earth fear him.

title: Psalms 77:2–3 (#1)
content:
What did Asaph do in the day of his trouble?

He sought the Lord, praying all night, and he thought about God and meditated on him.

title: Psalms 77:5 (#1)
content:
What did Asaph think about when he could not sleep at night?

He thought about previous years, about times long ago.

title: Psalms 77:6 (#1)
content:
What did Asaph recall to mind during the night?

He called to mind the songs he once sang.

title: Psalms 77:10 (#1)
content:
What is causing Asaph’s sadness?

He says his sadness is caused because it seems like the Most High God is no longer using his power for their protection.

title: Psalms 77:11 (#1)
content:
Which deeds of Yahweh does Asaph think about?

He thinks about Yahweh’s wonderful deeds of the past.

title: Psalms 77:13–15 (#1)
content:
How is God different from all other gods?

There is no other god like God; he does wonders, reveals his strength, and performs miracles.

title: Psalms 77:16–17 (#1)
content:
How did Asaph compare the power of nature to the power of God?

Asaph describes nature as being afraid of God and trembling; the clouds poured water, the skies thundered, and the depths of the waters shook.

title: Psalms 77:18–20 (#1)
content:
How did God lead his people?

God led his people as a shepherd leads his flock of sheep; his path went through the sea, and his way through deep waters.

title: Psalms 78:2 (#1)
content:
How does Asaph say he will teach his people?

Asaph says he will open his mouth in a parable and speak about things from long ago that are difficult to understand.

title: Psalms 78:4 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say he will tell the next generation?

He says he will tell them to praise Yahweh for his strength and the wonders that he has done.

title: Psalms 78:6 (#1)
content:
Why did Yahweh command the people to teach his law to their children?

Yahweh commanded this so that the later generation and children not yet born would know his law and in turn tell it to their own children.

title: Psalms 78:7–8 (#1)
content:
Why was it important for the fathers to teach Yahweh’s commandments to their children?

It was important for the fathers to teach Yahweh’s commandments to their children so that they would trust in God, remember what he had done, and keep his commandments, and would not be like their stubborn and rebellious ancestors.

title: Psalms 78:10 (#1)
content:
How did their fathers act wrongly against God?

They did not keep their covenant with God and refused to obey his laws.

title: Psalms 78:14 (#1)
content:
How did God lead their fathers through the wilderness?

He led them in the daytime with a cloud and all through the night with the light of fire.

title: Psalms 78:18 (#1)
content:
How did Israel test God?

They tested God in their hearts by demanding food to satisfy their appetites.

title: Psalms 78:19 (#1)
content:
What did Israel say when they spoke against God?

They insulted God by questioning whether God was able to provide food for them in the wilderness.

title: Psalms 78:22 (#1)
content:
Why was Yahweh angry with Israel?

Yahweh was angry because they did not believe in him and did not trust in his salvation.

title: Psalms 78:23–24 (#1)
content:
How did God provide food for Israel even though they did not believe in him?

God commanded the sky to open and rain down manna, a grain from heaven, for them to eat.

title: Psalms 78:31 (#1)
content:
What did God do to Israel in his anger?

He killed some of their strongest men and sent the young men of Israel to their graves.

title: Psalms 78:34 (#1)
content:
How did the people of Israel respond whenever God caused some of them to die?

They would seek God and return and look earnestly for him.

title: Psalms 78:37 (#1)
content:
What was the condition of Israel’s heart before God?

Their hearts were not steadfast with him, and they were not faithful to his covenant.

title: Psalms 78:38–39 (#1)
content:
How did God show mercy to the people of Israel?

He forgave their iniquity, did not destroy them, and held back his anger many times. He remembered that they were only human and that their lives were brief.

title: Psalms 78:44 (#1)
content:
What did God do to the rivers of Egypt?

He turned the rivers to blood so that the people could not drink from their streams.

title: Psalms 78:51 (#1)
content:
What did God do to the firstborn of the Egyptians?

He struck every firstborn in Egypt, the firstborn of every family, so that he died.

title: Psalms 78:52 (#1)
content:
How did God lead his people out of Egypt?

He led them like a shepherd leads his sheep and guided them through the wilderness like a flock.

title: Psalms 78:55 (#1)
content:
What did God do to the nations?

He drove out the nations before the Israelites and gave the land to the tribes of Israel as their inheritance.

title: Psalms 78:57 (#1)
content:
How did the people of Israel act like their ancestors?

They turned back and were unfaithful to God, just as their ancestors had done.

title: Psalms 78:58 (#1)
content:
With what did Israel make God angry?

They made him angry with their worship at the high places and provoked him to jealousy with their carved images.

title: Psalms 78:62–63 (#1)
content:
To what did God deliver his people?

He delivered them over to the sword, and fire destroyed their young men.

title: Psalms 78:68 (#1)
content:
Which tribe did God choose from Israel?

God chose the tribe of Judah and Mount Zion, which he loved.

title: Psalms 78:70 (#1)
content:
Who did God choose to be the shepherd of Israel?

God chose David, his servant, and brought him from tending the sheep to shepherd the people of Israel.

title: Psalms 79:1 (#1)
content:
What happened when the foreign nations came into Israel?

They defiled the temple and turned Jerusalem into a heap of ruins.

title: Psalms 79:4 (#1)
content:
What has Israel become to their neighbors?

They have become a reproach to their neighbors, a scorn and derision to those around them.

title: Psalms 79:6 (#1)
content:
On whom does Asaph ask God to pour out his wrath?

He asks God to pour out his wrath on the nations that do not know God and on the kingdoms that do not call upon God’s name.

title: Psalms 79:8 (#1)
content:
What does Asaph ask God to do?

He asks God not to remember their former sins against them and to be merciful to them.

title: Psalms 79:10 (#1)
content:
What does Asaph not want the nations to say?

He does not want the nations to say, “Where is their God?”

title: Psalms 79:13 (#1)
content:
What does Asaph say that Israel is to God?

He says they are God’s people and the flock of God’s pasture.

title: Psalms 80:1 (#1)
content:
What is the psalmist asking the Shepherd of Israel to do?

The psalmist is asking him to pay attention and to reveal his glory to them.

title: Psalms 80:2 (#1)
content:
What is the psalmist asking the Shepherd of Israel to do in the sight of the tribes of Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasseh?

He is asking the Shepherd of Israel to stir up his power and come and save them.

title: Psalms 80:3 (#1)
content:
What is the psalmist asking God to do?

He is asking God to restore their strength, regard them favorably, and save them.

title: Psalms 80:4 (#1)
content:
What was Yahweh’s response when his people prayed?

He was angry at his people so when they prayed, he did not answer.

title: Psalms 80:5 (#1)
content:
What has Yahweh caused them to experience?

He has caused them to experience punishment through constant sorrow just as if he gave them tears for their food and drink.

title: Psalms 80:6 (#1)
content:
What are Israel’s neighbors and enemies doing to them?

The nations are hostile to them, and their enemies mock and make fun of them.

title: Psalms 80:8 (#1)
content:
What did God do with the people that he brought out of Egypt?

He drove out nations before them and allowed his people to settle in it like a vine that was transplanted from one place to another.

title: Psalms 80:9 (#1)
content:
What did God do to prepare for his people to move into the land?

God removed the foreign nations just as a farmer clears land for a new plant.

title: Psalms 80:10 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say about the people of God?

He says they became so numerous it was like a vine that covered the mountains, and whose branches were like the great cedars.

title: Psalms 80:11 (#1)
content:
How far did the people’s influence extend?

They controlled territory as far as the sea in the west and the Euphrates River in the east.

title: Psalms 80:12 (#1)
content:
What has God allowed to happen?

The land has been conquered and its protective walls broken down so that those who pass by can take whatever they want.

title: Psalms 80:13 (#1)
content:
What will the enemies do to the country?

They will destroy it until it is as if wild boars had chewed up a vine and other wild animals ate what was left.

title: Psalms 80:14 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist ask the God of armies to do for his people?

He asks the God of armies to turn around and look down from heaven and see and respond to his people who are like a vine that he had planted.

title: Psalms 80:15 (#1)
content:
Who planted the people and made them grown strong in the land?

The right hand of the God of armies planted the people and caused them to become strong.

title: Psalms 80:16 (#1)
content:
What is happening to the people?

Their enemies are destroying them as if someone had cut down and burned a vine.

title: Psalms 80:17 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist want God to do for his own people?

The psalmist wants God to help them and to restore their power.

title: Psalms 80:18 (#1)
content:
What will the people do if God revives them?

They will worship him and not turn back to worship other gods.

title: Psalms 80:19 (#1)
content:
What will happen if Yahweh, the God of armies, restores the people?

If Yahweh restores them, they will be saved.

title: Psalms 81:1 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist tell the people to do to God?

He tells them to shout joyfully to God, their strength, and to shout out to the God of Jacob.

title: Psalms 81:2 (#1)
content:
What instruments do the psalmist tell the people to use as they raise a song?

The psalmist tells the people to play tambourines, harps, and lyres.

title: Psalms 81:3 (#1)
content:
When should the people blow the shofar?

They should blow it at the new moon and at the full moon for the day of their festival.

title: Psalms 81:4 (#1)
content:
Who gave these commands for Israel?

The God of Jacob gave these commands for Israel.

title: Psalms 81:5 (#1)
content:
What did God tell their ancestors to observe?

He told their ancestors to observe these things when he delivered them from slavery in the land of Egypt.

title: Psalms 81:6 (#1)
content:
What did God remove from the shoulder of the people?

He removed the burden from their shoulder, and their hands no longer had to carry heavy baskets full of bricks.

title: Psalms 81:7 (#1)
content:
What happened when the people called out in their distress?

God delivered them and answered them from the secret place of thunder, and he tested them at the waters of Meribah.

title: Psalms 81:9 (#1)
content:
What did God say about strange gods?

God said there must be no strange god among Israel, and they must not bow down to any god that other nations worship.

title: Psalms 81:10 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh say he did for Israel?

He brought them up from slavery in the land of Egypt.

title: Psalms 81:10 (#2)
content:
What promise did God make to the Israelites?

He promised them that if they depended on him, that he would provide everything they needed.

title: Psalms 81:11 (#1)
content:
What did Yahweh’s people, Israel, not do?

They did not listen to Yahweh’s voice, and Israel did not submit to him.

title: Psalms 81:12 (#1)
content:
What did Yahweh do when his people refused to listen to him?

He sent them away in the stubbornness of their heart, and they walked in their own counsels.

title: Psalms 81:13 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh long for his people to do?

Yahweh wants his people to listen to him and walk in his ways.

title: Psalms 81:14 (#1)
content:
What would Yahweh do if his people would listen to him and walk in his ways?

He would easily subdue their enemies and turn his hand against their adversaries.

title: Psalms 81:15 (#1)
content:
According to Yahweh, what would happen to those who hate him?

They would cringe before him, but the Israelites would always prosper.

title: Psalms 81:16 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh say he would do for Israel?

Yahweh would feed them with the fat of the wheat and satisfy them with honey from the rock.

title: Psalms 82:1 (#1)
content:
From where does God render judgment?

God takes his place in the assembly that he governs and pronounces his judgments there.

title: Psalms 82:2 (#1)
content:
What does God say to the rulers in the assembly?

God asks them how long they will judge unjustly and show favoritism to the wicked.

title: Psalms 82:3 (#1)
content:
What does God tell the rulers to do for the poor and the orphan?

God tells them to judge the poor and the orphan fairly and to vindicate the poor and the destitute.

title: Psalms 82:4 (#1)
content:
What does God tell the rulers to do for the poor and needy?

God tells them to rescue the poor and needy and deliver them from the hand of the wicked.

title: Psalms 82:5 (#1)
content:
What does God say about the rulers who do not know or understand?

God says they walk about in darkness, foolishness, and ignorance, and no longer live by the basic principles that make a society fair.

title: Psalms 82:6–7 (#1)
content:
What does God say will happen to the gods he calls sons of the Most High?

God says they will die like ordinary men and fall like one of the princes.

title: Psalms 82:8 (#1)
content:
Why does the psalmist ask God to arise and judge the earth?

He asks God to judge the earth because God is the ruler of the nations.

title: Psalms 83:2 (#1)
content:
What are God’s enemies doing?

They are defiantly approaching with a large army.

title: Psalms 83:3 (#1)
content:
Who do the enemies of God plot against?

They plot and conspire against God’s people whom he cherishes.

title: Psalms 83:4 (#1)
content:
What do God’s enemies say they will do to Israel?

They say they will destroy Israel so that it will no longer exist as a nation.

title: Psalms 83:4 (#2)
content:
What would happen to Israel if God’s enemies destroyed them?

No one will even remember that Israel existed.

title: Psalms 83:5 (#1)
content:
Against whom have God’s enemies conspired?

They conspired together against God and made an alliance against him.

title: Psalms 83:9–10 (#1)
content:
What does Asaph ask God to do to his enemies, as he did to Midian, Sisera, and Jabin?

He asks God to treat them as he treated those enemies, destroying them and leaving their dead bodies rotted on the ground.

title: Psalms 83:11–12 (#1)
content:
What did the nobles and princes of the enemies say?

They said they would take for themselves the land where God’s people dwell.

title: Psalms 83:13–14 (#1)
content:
What things does Asaph want God to make his enemies like?

He wants God to make them like tumbleweed that rolls away, like chaff that flies away in the wind, like fire that burns a forest, and like flames that burn up the hillsides.

title: Psalms 83:15 (#1)
content:
How does Asaph want God to pursue and terrify his enemies?

He wants God to pursue them until they run away as from a great storm that is driving them off.

title: Psalms 83:16 (#1)
content:
Why does Asaph ask Yahweh to disgrace his enemies?

He asks God to disgrace his enemies so that they will acknowledge who Yahweh is.

title: Psalms 83:17 (#1)
content:
What does Asaph desire to happen to God’s enemies?

He desires that they have shame and be terrified forever, and that they have disgrace and perish.

title: Psalms 83:18 (#1)
content:
What will God’s enemies know about Yahweh?

They will know that Yahweh alone is the Most High God who rules over everyone on the earth.

title: Psalms 84:1 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say about the temple of Yahweh?

He says the temple of Yahweh is a wonderful place.

title: Psalms 84:2 (#1)
content:
For what does the psalmist long?

He longs to be in the courtyards of Yahweh’s temple.

title: Psalms 84:2 (#2)
content:
To whom does the psalmist’s whole being cry out?

His whole being cries out to the only true God.

title: Psalms 84:3 (#1)
content:
Where has the sparrow built her house and the swallow a nest where she may lay her young?

They have built their house and nest near the temple of Yahweh, commander of heavenly armies.

title: Psalms 84:4 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say about those who live by Yahweh’s temple?

They will live a good life and worship Yahweh in his temple continually.

title: Psalms 84:5 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say about the man whose strength is in Yahweh?

The people whom Yahweh has made strong enough to travel to the temple will have a good life.

title: Psalms 84:6 (#1)
content:
What do those who pass through the Valley of Baca do to it?

They dig wells for water, and God sends the early rain to fill those wells with life-giving water.

title: Psalms 84:7 (#1)
content:
What happens to those who arrive at the temple of God?

They become stronger as they go.

title: Psalms 84:8 (#2)
content:
Who does the psalmist want to listen to what he is saying?

He wants the God whom Jacob’s descendants worship to listen to what he is saying and do what he is asking.

title: Psalms 84:8 (#1)
content:
Who does the psalmist want to hear his prayer?

He wants Yahweh, God of Armies, to hear his prayer.

title: Psalms 84:9 (#1)
content:
How does the psalmist ask God to treat the anointed king?

He asks God to treat favorably the king he has appointed to protect his people.

title: Psalms 84:10 (#2)
content:
What does the psalmist say he would rather do than dwell in the tents of wickedness?

He would rather stand at the entrance to the courtyard of God’s temple than stay in any of the comfortable homes where wicked people live.

title: Psalms 84:10 (#1)
content:
A day in Yahweh’s courts is better than what?

A day in Yahweh’s temple courts is better than a thousand spent anywhere else.

title: Psalms 84:11 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh do for his people?

Yahweh makes them prosper, protects them, is kind to them, honors them, and gives them every good thing that they need.

title: Psalms 84:12 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say about the man who trusts in Yahweh of Armies?

The man who trusts in Yahweh of Armies is happy.

title: Psalms 85:1 (#1)
content:
What has Yahweh done for his land and for the Israelites, the descendants of Jacob?

Yahweh has made his land prosperous again by bringing back the Israelites who were exiles.

title: Psalms 85:2 (#1)
content:
What has Yahweh done about the sins of his people?

He has forgiven his people all their sins.

title: Psalms 85:3 (#1)
content:
What has Yahweh done with his wrath and burning anger?

Yahweh stopped punishing his people and ceased being angry with them.

title: Psalms 85:4 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist ask of God?

He asks God to save his people, to stop being upset with them, and make them strong again.

title: Psalms 85:6 (#1)
content:
What will God’s people do if God revives them again?

God’s people will rejoice in him.

title: Psalms 85:7 (#1)
content:
What is the psalmist asking God do for his people?

He is asking Yahweh to treat them kindly as he promised and save them from their troubles.

title: Psalms 85:8 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say Yahweh will say to his people?

Yahweh will say that he will make his people thrive if they are loyal to him and do not do foolish things anymore.

title: Psalms 85:9 (#1)
content:
What will happen when Yahweh’s salvation comes for those who deeply revere him?

Yahweh will be gloriously present with them in their land.

title: Psalms 85:10 (#1)
content:
What will the people who revere Yahweh experience?

God’s faithful kindness and truth as well as his righteousness and peace.

title: Psalms 85:11 (#1)
content:
What will happen on the earth and from heaven when people revere God?

People on earth will be faithful to God, and he will act justly toward them from heaven.

title: Psalms 85:12 (#1)
content:
What will happen when Yahweh gives what is good?

The land will give its produce.

title: Psalms 85:13 (#1)
content:
What will Yahweh do as he considers what to do?

Righteousness walks before Yahweh so he will recognize what the right thing is to do and he will do that.

title: Psalms 86:1 (#1)
content:
Why does David ask Yahweh to listen to and answer him?

He asks Yahweh to answer him because David is poor and needy.

title: Psalms 86:2 (#1)
content:
What does David ask Yahweh to do for him when he is faithful and trusts in him?

David asks Yahweh to protect him and save him.

title: Psalms 86:3 (#1)
content:
What does David ask when he cries out to the Lord?

David asks the Lord to be kind to him.

title: Psalms 86:4 (#1)
content:
When David worships the Lord, what is he asking from the Lord?

David asks the Lord to make him glad.

title: Psalms 86:5 (#1)
content:
What happens to all those who cry out to the Lord who is good?

The Lord faithfully loves everyone who prays to him and is ready to forgive their sins.

title: Psalms 86:6 (#1)
content:
Who does David ask to listen to his prayer and hear his pleas?

David asks Yahweh to listen and do what he asks.

title: Psalms 86:7 (#1)
content:
What will Yahweh do when David calls on him when he is in trouble?

Yahweh will answer and help David.

title: Psalms 86:8 (#1)
content:
Who compares to the Lord among the gods?

There is no one who compares to the Lord and none of the other gods have done the great things he has done.

title: Psalms 86:9 (#1)
content:
What will all the nations that he has made do before the Lord?

All the nations will come and bow before the Lord and praise him.

acai.preferred_label: Bring Honor and Glory on Oneself

title: Psalms 86:10 (#1)
content:
Who alone is truly God?

Yahweh is the only true God and he does great and wonderful things.

title: Psalms 86:11 (#2)
content:
What will happen when Yahweh teaches David?

David will act as Yahweh wishes him to because he sincerely desires to honor Yahweh.

title: Psalms 86:11 (#1)
content:
What does David ask Yahweh to teach him?

David asks Yahweh to teach him how he wants him to live.

title: Psalms 86:12 (#1)
content:
What does David tell God he will do?

David will thank God wholeheartedly and praise him forever.

acai.preferred_label: Bring Honor and Glory on Oneself

title: Psalms 86:13 (#1)
content:
What does David say God has done in order to keep his covenant with him?

God has kept David from dying and going down to Sheol.

title: Psalms 86:14 (#1)
content:
What does David say the arrogant and violent people are doing to him?

They are attacking David and by trying to kill him, showing that they have no respect for God.

title: Psalms 86:15 (#1)
content:
How does David describe the Lord?

David describes the Lord as a merciful and gracious God who does not quickly become angry and is abundantly and faithfully kind and true to his people.

title: Psalms 86:16 (#1)
content:
What does David ask the Lord to do for him?

David asks the Lord to consider his situation and be kind to him, making him strong.

title: Psalms 86:17 (#1)
content:
What will happen when Yahweh shows David a sign of his favor?
