Those who hate David will see Yahweh helping and comforting him and be put to shame.

title: Psalms 87:1 (#1)
content:
Where did Yahweh establish his city?

He established it on the mountains that he made holy.

title: Psalms 87:2 (#1)
content:
How much does Yahweh love the city of Zion?

He loves them more than all other places where Israelites live.

title: Psalms 87:3 (#1)
content:
What things are said of the city of God?

People say wonderful and glorious things about this city that belongs to God.

title: Psalms 87:4 (#1)
content:
In what other places does Yahweh mention there are people who know him?

He says he will mention people from Egypt, Babylon, Philistia, Tyre, and Cush among those who know him.

title: Psalms 87:5 (#1)
content:
What will the Most High do for Zion?

God Most High himself will establish Zion and keep her strong.

title: Psalms 87:6 (#1)
content:
What will Yahweh record as he registers the peoples?

He will record that each of those people was born in Zion.

title: Psalms 87:7 (#1)
content:
What do the singers and musicians say?

They will celebrate and say that everything that makes them flourish comes from Zion.

title: Psalms 88:1 (#1)
content:
When does the psalmist cry out to Yahweh, the God of his salvation?

The psalmist cries out continually to ask Yahweh to help him.

title: Psalms 88:2 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist ask Yahweh to do for him?

He asks Yahweh to pay attention to his prayer as he cries out to him.

title: Psalms 88:3 (#1)
content:
What is the psalmist experiencing?

He is experiencing so many bad things that he feels he is about to die.

title: Psalms 88:4 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say others expect to happen to him?

People expect him to die soon because he has so little strength left.

title: Psalms 88:5 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say about the dead who lie in the grave?

He says that it seems as if Yahweh is no longer aware of people who have died and has stopped taking care of them.

title: Psalms 88:6 (#1)
content:
How does the psalmist describe where he feels as if Yahweh has placed him?

He says it is as though Yahweh has thrown him to the bottom of a deep, dark pit.

title: Psalms 88:7 (#1)
content:
What feels like an oppressive burden to the psalmist?

He feels that Yahweh is so angry with him that it feels as if he is drowning in Yahweh’s anger.

title: Psalms 88:8 (#1)
content:
Why do the psalmist’s acquaintances avoid him?

Yahweh has made his illness so unpleasant that his friends stay away from him and he is not able to visit any of them.

title: Psalms 88:9 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say about his eyes?

His eyes are swollen from crying out in prayer to Yahweh about his affliction.

title: Psalms 88:10 (#1)
content:
What questions does the psalmist ask Yahweh about the dead?

He asks Yahweh if he will do a miracle to help him before he dies and is no longer able to praise Yahweh.

title: Psalms 88:11–12 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist remind Yahweh about dead people?

He reminds Yahweh that if he dies, he will no longer be able to talk about how kind and faithful Yahweh is or all the amazing things he does or how good he is.

title: Psalms 88:13 (#1)
content:
When does the psalmist’s prayer come before Yahweh?

His prayer comes before Yahweh in the morning as if it were already there waiting for Yahweh when he gets up.

title: Psalms 88:14 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist feel like Yahweh has done to him?

The psalmist feels like Yahweh has rejected him and is ignoring him.

title: Psalms 88:15 (#1)
content:
How long has the psalmist been sick and on the verge of death?

Since he was young, the psalmist has been so ill that he has nearly died.

title: Psalms 88:16 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say Yahweh’s anger has done to him?

Because of Yahweh’s anger, the terrible illness that he has permitted has destroyed the good life the psalmist could have had.

title: Psalms 88:17 (#1)
content:
What have the bad things Yahweh has allowed in the psalmist’s life done to him?

They are like floodwaters that continually surround the psalmist and are about to drown him.

title: Psalms 89:1 (#1)
content:
Of what will the psalmist sing forever?

He will sing about how faithfully Yahweh has loved his people as he promised.

title: Psalms 89:1 (#2)
content:
What will the psalmist make known to future generations?

He will tell future generations that Yahweh always does what he promises.

title: Psalms 89:2 (#1)
content:
How has Yahweh’s faithfulness been established?

The fact that Yahweh is faithful to his people is as permanent as the heavens.

title: Psalms 89:3 (#1)
content:
With whom has a covenant been made?

Yahweh has made a covenant and a solemn promise with David, the man he chose to be king of Israel.

title: Psalms 89:4 (#1)
content:
How long will David’s descendants rule as kings?

Yahweh promised that David’s descendants would always rule as kings.

title: Psalms 89:5 (#1)
content:
What will the angels in heaven be praising Yahweh about?

The angels in heaven will praise Yahweh for the wonderful things he does and celebrate how he always does what he promises.

title: Psalms 89:7 (#1)
content:
How do the council of holy ones treat God?

When the holy beings gather together, they all treat God with respect and honor.

title: Psalms 89:8 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say about Yahweh’s faithfulness?

Yahweh is always faithful in every way.

title: Psalms 89:9 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say about Yahweh’s rule of the sea?

He says that Yahweh calms the waves of the sea so it will not become too violent.

title: Psalms 89:10 (#1)
content:
What did Yahweh use to scatter and defeat his enemies?

He used his great power.

title: Psalms 89:11 (#1)
content:
What belongs to Yahweh who made the world and all it contains?

The heavens and the earth belong to Yahweh who created the world and everything in it.

title: Psalms 89:12 (#1)
content:
What did Yahweh create?

Yahweh created the full extent of the world in every direction.

title: Psalms 89:13 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say about Yahweh using the images of his arm and hand?

Yahweh is very powerful and uses his power to do great things.

title: Psalms 89:14 (#1)
content:
How does Yahweh rule?

Yahweh always does what is right and just and is faithful and true in everything he does.

title: Psalms 89:15–16 (#1)
content:
What happens to the people who worship Yahweh?

They are have truly good lives in which they enjoy Yahweh’s favor, and they rejoice in who Yahweh is and how he always does what is right.

title: Psalms 89:17 (#1)
content:
What did Yahweh give the people because of his favor?

Because Yahweh was pleased with his people, made them strong and glorious and gave them a good king.

title: Psalms 89:18 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say belongs to Yahweh, the Holy One of Israel?

The people’s king is the one who protects them and he belongs to Yahweh, the Holy One of Israel.

title: Psalms 89:19 (#1)
content:
What did Yahweh say in a vision to his faithful ones?

He said that he had given strength to a mighty warrior from among the people and had chosen him to be their king.

title: Psalms 89:20–23 (#1)
content:
What did Yahweh say he will do for his chosen king David?

He said he had anointed him, will support him, strengthen him, and defeat his enemies.

title: Psalms 89:24 (#1)
content:
How does Yahweh promise he will treat David?

Yahweh will always be faithful to David and treat him kindly, and by Yahweh’s authority, make him a great ruler.

title: Psalms 89:26 (#1)
content:
What will David call out to Yahweh?

He will call out to Yahweh as his Father, his God, and the one who protects and saves him.

title: Psalms 89:27 (#1)
content:
How will Yahweh treat David?

He will treat him as if he were his firstborn son and make him the greatest of all kings on the earth.

title: Psalms 89:28 (#1)
content:
What will Yahweh do for David?

Yahweh will always love David faithfully always honor his covenant with him.

title: Psalms 89:29 (#1)
content:
How long will David’s descendants rule and his throne last?

His descendants will always rule as kings and his dynasty will last as long as the skies exist.

title: Psalms 89:30–32 (#1)
content:
What will Yahweh do to David’s descendants if they disobey Yahweh’s rules?

Yahweh will punish them to correct them because of the wrong things they have done.

title: Psalms 89:33–34 (#1)
content:
What promises does Yahweh make to David even if the people disobey his rules?

Yahweh promises not to stop faithfully loving David and doing what he promised for his descendants. He will not break his covenant or take back what he said.

title: Psalms 89:35–37 (#1)
content:
By what does Yahweh swear once and for all that he will keep these promises to David?

Yahweh swears by his own holy character that he guarantees his promise to David.

title: Psalms 89:38 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist now say about how the anointed one is being treated by Yahweh?

The psalmist says that it appears that Yahweh has rejected the anointed king and has abandoned him.

title: Psalms 89:41 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say is happening to the people of Israel as represented by their king?

Their city is being plundered by people who to steal from the city and the people of Israel are being ridiculed by the people around them.

title: Psalms 89:42 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say Yahweh has done regarding the enemies of Israel?

Yahweh has allowed their enemies to become strong and celebrate how they have defeated the people of Israel.

title: Psalms 89:43 (#1)
content:
What happened when the Israelites went into battle?

Their armies have had to retreat from battles because Yahweh had not helped them.

title: Psalms 89:44 (#1)
content:
What has happened to the kingdom of Israel?

The kingdom is no longer glorious and they no longer have a king.

title: Psalms 89:45 (#1)
content:
What has happened to Israel?

They are no longer a strong nation as they had been and are completely disgraced.

title: Psalms 89:46 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say about Yahweh and his anger?

He asks Yahweh to come to help them and not be angry with them any more.

title: Psalms 89:47 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist ask Yahweh to remember?

He asks Yahweh to remember how short life is and that he created all people as mere mortals.

title: Psalms 89:49 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist remind the Lord about his promises?

The psalmist reminds the Lord that he promised David that he would faithfully love his people.

title: Psalms 89:50–51 (#1)
content:
What else does the psalmist ask the Lord to remember?

He asks the Lord to remember the insulting things people are saying about his people and how Yahweh’s enemies have been mocking the actions of his anointed king.

title: Psalms 89:52 (#1)
content:
How long does the psalmist say Yahweh will be blessed?

Yahweh will be blessed forever.

title: Psalms 90:1 (#1)
content:
How long has the Lord been like a home for his people?

The Lord has been like a home for them throughout all generations.

title: Psalms 90:3 (#1)
content:
To what does the Lord cause people to return when they die?

He causes people to return to dust.

title: Psalms 90:4 (#1)
content:
What are a thousand years like in the sight of the Lord?

They are like one short day that passes, or like a few short hours in the night.

title: Psalms 90:5–6 (#1)
content:
To what are the lifetimes of people compared?

They are like the grass that sprouts up in the morning and then withers and dries up in the evening.

title: Psalms 90:7–8 (#1)
content:
Why does Moses say mankind is terrified by the Lord’s wrath?

They are terrified because the Lord has seen their sins and is angry. It is as if even their secret sins are spread out where the Lord can see them.

title: Psalms 90:10 (#1)
content:
What do people experience throughout their lives?

People experience much pain and trouble throughout the time they have to live.

title: Psalms 90:12 (#1)
content:
What does Moses ask the Lord to teach mankind?

He asks the Lord to teach mankind to realize the short time they will live, so that they may live wisely.

title: Psalms 90:14 (#1)
content:
With what does Moses want Yahweh to show mankind each morning?

He wants Yahweh to show mankind that it is enough for them if Yahweh loves them faithfully as he has promised that he would do, so that they may rejoice and be glad all their lives.

title: Psalms 90:16 (#1)
content:
What does Moses want Yahweh to let his servants see?

He wants Yahweh to enable his servants to see the great things that he does, and their descendants to see his glorious power.

title: Psalms 90:17 (#1)
content:
What does Moses ask the Lord to do for his people?

He asks the Lord to bless his people and to cause them to be successful in everything they do.

title: Psalms 91:2 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say of Yahweh?

The psalmist says that Yahweh is his refuge and his fortress, his God, in whom he trusts.

title: Psalms 91:3–4 (#1)
content:
What will Yahweh do for the one who trusts in him?

Yahweh will rescue him from hidden traps and from deadly diseases, and will protect him like a bird who covers her young under her wings.

title: Psalms 91:5–6 (#1)
content:
Of what does the one who trusts in Yahweh need not be afraid?

The one who trusts in Yahweh need not be afraid of things that happen during the night that could terrorize you or of arrows that your enemies will shoot at you during the day, of the plague that infects people in the night or of other evil forces that kill people in the light of day.

title: Psalms 91:9 (#1)
content:
What is Yahweh for the psalmist?

Yahweh is the refuge for the psalmist.

title: Psalms 91:10–11 (#1)
content:
Why will evil not happen to the one who trusts in Yahweh?

Evil will not happen to the one who trusts in Yahweh because Yahweh will command his angels to protect him in all his ways.

title: Psalms 91:12 (#1)
content:
How will the angels protect the one who trusts in Yahweh?

The angels will lift him up in their hands so he will not hurt his foot on a stone.

title: Psalms 91:14–16 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh do for the one who is devoted to him?

Yahweh will deliver and protect him, answer him when he calls, be with him in trouble, rescue and honor him, satisfy him with a long life, and show him Yahweh’s salvation.

acai.preferred_label: Bring Honor and Glory on Oneself

title: Psalms 92:1 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist consider to be a good thing?

It is a good thing to give thanks and sing praises to the name of Yahweh.

title: Psalms 92:2 (#1)
content:
When does the psalmist say to proclaim Yahweh’s covenant faithfulness and truthfulness?

He says to proclaim Yahweh’s covenant faithfulness every morning and his truthfulness every night.

title: Psalms 92:4 (#1)
content:
How has the psalmist responded to the great things Yahweh has done?

Yahweh’s great deeds have made him glad so that he will sing for joy.

title: Psalms 92:5–6 (#1)
content:
What kind of person does not know or understand the things Yahweh has done?

A foolish or stupid person does not know the things Yahweh has done.

title: Psalms 92:7 (#1)
content:
What happens to the wicked who seem to thrive?

Yahweh will destroy all those who do evil.

title: Psalms 92:9 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say will happen to Yahweh’s enemies?

Yahweh’s enemies will perish, and all those who do evil will be scattered.

title: Psalms 92:10 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say Yahweh has done for him?

Yahweh has caused him to be strong and joyful.

title: Psalms 92:13 (#1)
content:
Where are the righteous planted?

They are planted as securely as if they were trees with roots deep in Yahweh’s temple grounds.

title: Psalms 92:14–15 (#1)
content:
What shows that Yahweh is just?

The righteous remain strong and full of energy like trees that continue to bear fruit even when they are old.

title: Psalms 92:15 (#1)
content:
Why is Yahweh the rock of the psalmist?

Yahweh is like a huge rock behind which the psalmist is safe and he never does anything that is unjust.

title: Psalms 93:1 (#1)
content:
Who put the world in its place so that it cannot be moved?

Yahweh the King is the one who put the world firmly in place, and no one can move it.

title: Psalms 93:2 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say about Yahweh’s throne?

Yahweh has been king since long ago, and has always existed.

title: Psalms 93:3 (#1)
content:
How have the oceans lifted up their voice?

The oceans rise and their waves pound against the shore with a roar that is like a powerful voice.

title: Psalms 93:4 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say about Yahweh in relation to the mighty waters?

Yahweh is more powerful than the mighty breakers of the sea.

title: Psalms 93:5 (#1)
content:
How does the psalmist describe Yahweh’s decrees and holiness?

The psalmist says that Yahweh’s decrees are completely reliable and his temple is a holy place.

title: Psalms 94:1 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist call Yahweh in this psalm?

The psalmist calls Yahweh the God of vengeance.

title: Psalms 94:2 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist ask Yahweh, the judge of the earth, to do to proud people?

The psalmist asks Yahweh to give the proud people what they deserve.

title: Psalms 94:3 (#1)
content:
What are the wicked people doing that the psalmist says is not right?

The wicked people just continue to be glad and rejoice.

title: Psalms 94:4 (#1)
content:
What do all the wicked people say?

All those who do evil things praise themselves arrogantly.

title: Psalms 94:5 (#1)
content:
What do the wicked do to Yahweh’s people?

It is as though those wicked people were crushing Yahweh’s people.

title: Psalms 94:6 (#1)
content:
Who do the wicked murder?

The wicked murder widows, foreigners, and orphans.

title: Psalms 94:7 (#1)
content:
What do the wicked say about Yahweh?

The wicked say that Yahweh does not see the evil things they are doing.

title: Psalms 94:9 (#1)
content:
What argument does the psalmist use to show that Yahweh can hear and see?

The psalmist says that the one who made ears can of course hear and the one who created eyes can of course see the evil things they are doing.

title: Psalms 94:11 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh know the people’s thoughts?

Yahweh knows everything that people are thinking and that it is evil and useless.

title: Psalms 94:12 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say about those whom Yahweh instructs?

The psalmist says those whom Yahweh teaches from his law are truly fortunate.

title: Psalms 94:12–13 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh give the man he instructs during days of evil?

Yahweh relieves him from bad things when they happen and punishes the wicked who do them.

title: Psalms 94:14 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say Yahweh will not do to his people?

Yahweh will not forsake his people or desert those who belong to him.

title: Psalms 94:15 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say about the return of judgment?

The psalmist says that someday judges will again decide matters fairly for people, and all honest people will be pleased about that.

title: Psalms 94:16 (#1)
content:
Who does the psalmist say will stand up for him against evildoers?

The psalmist says that no one will defend him against the wicked things people did to him.

title: Psalms 94:17 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say would have happened without Yahweh’s help?

Without Yahweh’s help, the psalmist would have quickly died.

title: Psalms 94:18 (#1)
content:
What did Yahweh do when the psalmist thought he was about to die?

Yahweh saved him by being faithful and loving to him.

title: Psalms 94:19 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh do when the psalmist has many worries?

Yahweh comforts him and causes him to be happy when he is worried.

title: Psalms 94:20–21 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say about rulers who establish laws that create injustice?

Such rulers cannot be Yahweh’s friends as they conspire how to destroy righteous people, and condemn innocent people.

title: Psalms 94:22 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say Yahweh has been to him?

Yahweh has been like a fortress of protection to the psalmist.

title: Psalms 94:23 (#1)
content:
What will Yahweh do to the wicked in the end?

Yahweh will do to those wicked leaders the terrible things that they have done to others and destroy them in their wickedness.

title: Psalms 95:1–2 (#1)
content:
How does the psalmist encourage everyone to come into Yahweh’s presence?

The psalmist encourages everyone to enter Yahweh’s presence singing joyfully with thanksgiving.

title: Psalms 95:3 (#1)
content:
How does Yahweh compare to other gods?

Yahweh is a great God who rules as king over all other gods.

title: Psalms 95:4–5 (#1)
content:
How is Yahweh above all other gods?

Yahweh controls the whole earth and because he made it all, it all belongs to him.

title: Psalms 95:6–7 (#1)
content:
Why should everyone worship Yahweh?

Everyone should worship Yahweh, their maker, because he is their God and they are the people whom he protects, like sheep that a shepherd takes care of.

title: Psalms 95:9 (#1)
content:
How did the ancestors of Israel respond to Yahweh?

They tested whether Yahweh would continue to be patient with them, even though they had seen him perform miracles.

title: Psalms 95:10 (#1)
content:
How did Yahweh describe the people who disobeyed him?

Yahweh said that those people are unreliable and completely refuse to obey his commands.

title: Psalms 95:11 (#1)
content:
What did Yahweh vow in his anger?

Yahweh vowed in his anger that the people who disobeyed him would never enter into the land where Yahweh would have given them rest.

title: Psalms 96:1 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist call on all the people on earth to do?

The psalmist calls on all the earth to sing a new song to Yahweh.

title: Psalms 96:2 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist encourage everyone to announce?

The psalmist encourages everyone to announce that Yahweh has saved them.

title: Psalms 96:3–4 (#1)
content:
Why should everyone tell of Yahweh’s glory and his marvelous things he has done?

Everyone should tell of how glorious Yahweh is and all he has done because Yahweh is great, and deserves to be praised and be revered more than all other gods.

title: Psalms 96:5 (#1)
content:
What contrast does the psalmist draw between the gods of other peoples and Yahweh?

The gods of other peoples are only idols, but it is Yahweh who made the heavens.

title: Psalms 96:6 (#1)
content:
What qualities does the psalmist say Yahweh has?

Yahweh is magnificent, majestic, strong, and beautiful.

title: Psalms 96:8 (#1)
content:
What should everyone do to give to Yahweh the glory he deserves?

Everyone should praise Yahweh, bring an offering, and come to his temple.

title: Psalms 96:10 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist encourage everyone to say to all people groups?

The psalmist encourages everyone to tell all people that Yahweh reigns.

title: Psalms 96:10 (#2)
content:
How does Yahweh judge the peoples?

Yahweh judges the peoples fairly.

title: Psalms 96:11–13 (#1)
content:
Why should the heavens be glad and the earth rejoice?

The heavens should be glad and the earth rejoice because Yahweh is coming.

title: Psalms 96:13 (#1)
content:
What will Yahweh do when he comes?

When Yahweh comes, he will judge the world with righteousness and the peoples with his faithfulness.

title: Psalms 97:1 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist declare about Yahweh?

The psalmist declares that Yahweh reigns and calls for everyone on earth to rejoice and be glad.

title: Psalms 97:2 (#1)
content:
What is the foundation of Yahweh’s throne?

The foundation of Yahweh’s throne is righteousness and justice.

title: Psalms 97:3 (#1)
content:
What is the result of the fire that goes before Yahweh?

The fire that goes before Yahweh burns all of his enemies.

title: Psalms 97:4 (#1)
content:
What happens in Yahweh’s presence?

Yahweh’s lightning lights up the world, people on the earth see it, and it causes them to be afraid.

title: Psalms 97:6 (#1)
content:
What declares Yahweh’s righteousness and glory?

Everything that people can see in the heavens makes it clear that he is righteous and all the people groups see how glorious he is.

title: Psalms 97:7 (#1)
content:
Who will be shamed by Yahweh?

All those who worship carved images and are proud of their useless idols should be shamed by Yahweh.

title: Psalms 97:8 (#1)
content:
Why did Zion hear and the daughters of Judah rejoice?

All the people of Jerusalem and all of Judah rejoiced because Yahweh judges people justly.

title: Psalms 97:9 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say about Yahweh?

The psalmist says that Yahweh is the supreme king who rules over all the earth and more powerful than all other spirit beings.

title: Psalms 97:10 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh do for his faithful?

Yahweh protects the lives of his faithful ones and rescues them from the wicked.

title: Psalms 97:11 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say Yahweh provides for righteous people?

The psalmist says that good things happen for the righteous and they can rejoice.

title: Psalms 97:12 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist encourage the righteous to do?

The psalmist encourages the righteous to be glad in Yahweh and thank him, the one we all know to be holy.

title: Psalms 98:1 (#1)
content:
Why is Yahweh able to save his people?

Yahweh has saved his people by being powerfully holy.

title: Psalms 98:2 (#1)
content:
What has Yahweh openly shown to all the nations?

He has openly shown that he is righteous and that he saves his people.

title: Psalms 98:3 (#1)
content:
Who will see the salvation of our God?

All the people of the earth will see that God saves his people.

title: Psalms 98:4 (#1)
content:
What should be the response of everyone to Yahweh?

Everyone should shout for joy and make music, singing joyful praises to Yahweh.

title: Psalms 98:5–6 (#1)
content:
What musical instruments does the psalmist say to use when praising Yahweh?

The psalmist says to use harps, trumpets, and the shofar when praising Yahweh.

title: Psalms 98:7–8 (#1)
content:
How does the psalmist encourage Yahweh’s creation to respond to his coming?

The psalmist says the sea, the rivers, the mountains, and everyone on the earth should praise Yahweh together.

title: Psalms 98:9 (#1)
content:
How will Yahweh judge the world?

Yahweh will judge the people of the world justly and fairly.

title: Psalms 99:1 (#1)
content:
How should the people respond to Yahweh’s reign?

The people should tremble in response to Yahweh’s reign.

title: Psalms 99:2 (#1)
content:
How is Yahweh high above all the peoples?

Yahweh is the supreme ruler of all the peoples.

title: Psalms 99:3 (#1)
content:
Why should everyone praise Yahweh?

Everyone should praise Yahweh because he is holy.

title: Psalms 99:4 (#1)
content:
How does the psalmist describe the king?

The psalmist says the king is mighty because he is righteous and always acts justly toward the people of Israel.

title: Psalms 99:5 (#1)
content:
How and why does the psalmist say that people should respond to Yahweh?

The psalmist says that people should praise Yahweh and bow down to worship him because he is holy.

title: Psalms 99:6 (#1)
content:
Who were the men mentioned whom Yahweh answered when they cried out and prayed to him?

Some of those men who cried out to Yahweh and he helped them were Moses, Aaron, and Samuel.

title: Psalms 99:7 (#1)
content:
How did Yahweh respond to the men who prayed to him for help?

Yahweh spoke to Moses and Aaron from the pillar of cloud and they obeyed all he told them.

title: Psalms 99:8 (#1)
content:
What did Yahweh do for the men who prayed to him?

Yahweh helped them and forgave them even though he also punished them for the things they did wrong.

title: Psalms 99:9 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist encourage everyone to do?

The psalmist says to praise Yahweh and worship him at his temple because Yahweh is holy.

title: Psalms 100:1 (#1)
content:
Who does the psalmist invite to shout joyfully to Yahweh?

He invites all the earth to shout joyfully to Yahweh.

title: Psalms 100:2 (#1)
content:
How should people come into Yahweh’s presence?

They should come before his presence with joyful singing.

title: Psalms 100:3 (#1)
content:
What image does the psalmist use to show how people belong to Yahweh?

He says Yahweh made us and we are like sheep that he cares for as a shepherd does.

title: Psalms 100:4 (#1)
content:
How should people enter into Yahweh’s gates and courts?

They should enter into his gates with thanksgiving and into his courts with praise.

title: Psalms 100:5 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say will last forever?

He says that Yahweh’s covenant faithfulness and truthfulness will last to eternity.

title: Psalms 101:1 (#1)
content:
Of what two qualities of Yahweh will David sing praises?

He will sing of covenant faithfulness and justice.

title: Psalms 101:3 (#1)
content:
What will David not put before his eyes?

He will not tempt himself to do any bad thing.

title: Psalms 101:5 (#1)
content:
Who will David destroy?

He will destroy whoever secretly slanders someone else.

title: Psalms 101:6 (#1)
content:
What kind of people does David want to help him rule?

The faithful of the land and those who walk in the way of integrity may serve him.

title: Psalms 101:7 (#1)
content:
Who will David not allow to work for him?

He will not allow a deceitful person to work for him.

title: Psalms 101:8 (#1)
content:
How often does David say that he will destroy all the wicked of the land?

Every day he will work to keep those who are wicked from the city of Yahweh.

title: Psalms 102:2 (#1)
content:
When distressing things happen, what does the psalmist ask Yahweh not to do?

When the psalmist calls out to Yahweh, he asks Yahweh to hear him and not to ignore him.

title: Psalms 102:4 (#1)
content:
To what does the psalmist compare the way he feels?

The psalmist says he feels like grass that has withered.

title: Psalms 102:5 (#1)
content:
What has happened due to the psalmist’s distress?

The psalmist is so miserable that he groans and his bones protrude under his skin.

title: Psalms 102:8 (#1)
content:
How do those who mock the psalmist use his name?

Those who mock the psalmist use his name when they curse people.

title: Psalms 102:10 (#1)
content:
How does the psalmist say Yahweh has treated him in anger?

The psalmist says it feels as if Yahweh has lifted him up and thrown him down.

title: Psalms 102:12 (#1)
content:
How long will Yahweh be remembered?

The psalmist says that people of all times will talk about Yahweh.

title: Psalms 102:14 (#1)
content:
What do the servants of Yahweh cherish?

Yahweh’s servants cherish even the stones and dust of Jerusalem.

title: Psalms 102:15 (#1)
content:
Why will the kings of the earth show respect for Yahweh?

All the kings of the earth will recognize Yahweh’s glory.

title: Psalms 102:17 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh do when the destitute pray?

Yahweh listens to the prayers of the destitute and does not ignore them.

title: Psalms 102:18 (#1)
content:
How does the psalmist show how far into the future Yahweh’s praise will continue?

He writes that people who are not even born yet will praise Yahweh.

title: Psalms 102:19 (#1)
content:
What did Yahweh see from heaven?

From heaven Yahweh saw what was happening on the earth.

title: Psalms 102:22 (#1)
content:
For what purpose are the peoples and kingdoms gathered together?

The peoples and kingdoms gather together to serve Yahweh.

title: Psalms 102:24 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist plead with God not to do?

The psalmist pleads with God not let him die too soon.

title: Psalms 102:25 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say Yahweh did in long ago?

The psalmist says that long ago Yahweh made the earth and the heavens.

title: Psalms 102:27 (#1)
content:
How long will Yahweh endure?

Yahweh will have no end.

title: Psalms 102:28 (#1)
content:
Where does the psalmist say the descendants of Yahweh’s servants will live?

The descendants of Yahweh’s servants will live in his presence.

title: Psalms 103:2 (#1)
content:
What does David not want to forget?

He does not want to forget all of the kind things Yahweh has done for him.

title: Psalms 103:4 (#1)
content:
With what does David say Yahweh will bless him?

He blesses him with covenant faithfulness and acts of mercy.

title: Psalms 103:6 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh do for all who are oppressed?

Yahweh does acts of righteousness and justice for all who are oppressed.

title: Psalms 103:7 (#1)
content:
What did Yahweh make known to the children of Israel?

He made known his deeds to the children of Israel.

title: Psalms 103:9 (#1)
content:
What does David say that Yahweh will not always do?

David says Yahweh will not always rebuke, and will not remain angry forever.

title: Psalms 103:10 (#1)
content:
What does David say about how Yahweh deals with people’s sins?

Yahweh does not punish them for their sins as much as they deserve.

title: Psalms 103:13 (#1)
content:
In what special way does Yahweh have compassion on those who fear him?

Yahweh has compassion on those who fear him in the same way as a father has compassion on his children.

title: Psalms 103:17 (#1)
content:
How long does the covenant faithfulness of Yahweh last?

The covenant faithfulness of Yahweh is forever for those fearing him.

title: Psalms 103:19 (#1)
content:
Where has Yahweh established his throne?

Yahweh has established his throne in the heavens.

title: Psalms 103:20 (#1)
content:
Who are the ones who are called to bless Yahweh and obey his commands?

His angels, who are warriors of great strength, are called to bless Yahweh and obey his commands.

title: Psalms 103:21 (#1)
content:
Who are those that David says do Yahweh’s pleasure?

All of Yahweh’s army of angels serve him and do what he desires.

title: Psalms 104:1 (#1)
content:
How does the psalmist describe how great Yahweh is?

He says that Yahweh is clothed with splendor and majesty.

title: Psalms 104:2 (#1)
content:
In what way does Yahweh spread out the heavens?

He spreads out the heavens as if it were his tent.

title: Psalms 104:5 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say will never happen to the earth?

The earth that Yahweh created will never be moved.

title: Psalms 104:6–7 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say made the waters recede?

Yahweh’s rebuke made the waters recede.

title: Psalms 104:9 (#1)
content:
Why will the waters not cover the earth again?

Yahweh set a boundary for them that they cannot cross.

title: Psalms 104:14 (#1)
content:
How does Yahweh provide for both animals and people?

He makes grass for the cattle to eat and plants for people from which they can make food to eat.

title: Psalms 104:19 (#1)
content:
What did Yahweh make the moon and the sun to mark?

He made the moon to indicate times for festivals and the sun to set each day.

title: Psalms 104:20–22 (#1)
content:
What happens to the young lions?

The young lions prowl at night for food and when the sun rises, they retreat and lie down in their dens.

title: Psalms 104:25 (#1)
content:
With what is the sea full?

The sea is full of many living creatures, both great and small.

title: Psalms 104:27 (#1)
content:
To whom do all living creatures look to give them their food?

They all look to Yahweh to give them their food at the right time.

title: Psalms 104:29 (#1)
content:
What happens to the creatures if Yahweh hides his face or takes away their breath?

When he hides his face, they have no food to eat and when he takes away their breath, they die.

title: Psalms 104:31 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist want Yahweh to do because of his creation?

The psalmist wants Yahweh to rejoice about everything that he has created.

title: Psalms 104:33 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist promise to sing?

He promises to sing praise to his God as long as he lives.

title: Psalms 104:35 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist hope will happen to sinners and the wicked on the earth?

He wants sinners to disappear from the earth and the wicked to be no more.

title: Psalms 105:1 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say about what Yahweh has done?

The psalmist says that people should tell everyone about what Yahweh has done.

title: Psalms 105:3 (#1)
content:
Who does the psalmist tell to rejoice?

The psalmist tells those who seek Yahweh to rejoice.

title: Psalms 105:4 (#1)
content:
How often should people seek the presence of Yahweh?

The psalmist calls people to seek his presence continually.

title: Psalms 105:8 (#1)
content:
For how long does the psalmist say Yahweh remembers his covenant?

The psalmist says Yahweh remembers his covenant forever.

title: Psalms 105:9 (#1)
content:
What covenant does the psalmist say Yahweh calls to mind?

Yahweh calls to mind the covenant that he made with Abraham and his oath to Isaac.

title: Psalms 105:11 (#1)
content:
What has Yahweh given as an inheritance to Israel?

Yahweh promised Israel that the land of Canaan will be what they and their descendants inherit from him.

title: Psalms 105:12 (#1)
content:
When did Yahweh make the covenant with Israel?

The psalmist says that Yahweh made this covenant with Israel when they were only few in number and strangers in that land.

title: Psalms 105:14–15 (#1)
content:
Whom did Yahweh tell kings not to touch?

Yahweh told them not to harm his chosen people or his prophets.

title: Psalms 105:17 (#1)
content:
How did Yahweh send Joseph ahead of Israel?

He sent Joseph ahead of them by having him sold by his brothers as a slave.

title: Psalms 105:19 (#1)
content:
What did Yahweh do for Joseph while he was in prison?

While he was in prison, Yahweh taught Joseph to trust him more.

title: Psalms 105:21 (#1)
content:
What role did the king give Joseph?

The king appointed Joseph as lord of his house and ruler over all of his possessions.

title: Psalms 105:23 (#1)
content:
Where did Jacob live when he came to Egypt?

Jacob lived for a time in the land of Ham.

title: Psalms 105:25 (#1)
content:
Whom did Yahweh cause to hate his people?

Yahweh caused the rulers of Egypt to hate the people of Israel.

title: Psalms 105:27 (#1)
content:
Where did Moses and Aaron perform Yahweh’s signs?

Moses and Aaron performed Yahweh’s signs among the Egyptians who lived in the land of Ham.

title: Psalms 105:29 (#1)
content:
What did Yahweh do to the Egyptians’ water and fish?

Yahweh turned the Egyptians’ water into blood and killed their fish.

title: Psalms 105:32 (#1)
content:
What did Yahweh send along with the hail in Egypt?

Along with the hail, Yahweh sent fire that burned throughout their land.

title: Psalms 105:36 (#1)
content:
Who did Yahweh kill in Egypt?

Yahweh killed every firstborn son of the Egyptians.

title: Psalms 105:38 (#1)
content:
Why were the people of Egypt glad when the Israelites went away?

The Egyptians were glad when the Israelites went away because they had become very afraid of the Israelites.

title: Psalms 105:40 (#1)
content:
With what kind of food did Yahweh provide for the Israelites?

Yahweh satisfied them with quail to eat and bread from heaven.

title: Psalms 105:42 (#1)
content:
Which holy promise did Yahweh remember?

Yahweh remembered his holy promise that he made to Abraham his servant.

title: Psalms 105:44 (#1)
content:
What did Yahweh give his people?

He gave his people the land and planted fields of the people that lived there.

title: Psalms 106:1 (#1)
content:
Why does the psalmist say people should give thanks?

The psalmist says to give thanks because Yahweh’s covenant faithfulness lasts forever.

title: Psalms 106:3 (#1)
content:
What will make a person happy?

The person who acts fairly and does what is right will be happy.

title: Psalms 106:5 (#1)
content:
What will cause the psalmist to rejoice?

He will rejoice when he sees Yahweh’s chosen people prosperous and happy again.

title: Psalms 106:7 (#1)
content:
How did the ancestors of the psalmist respond to Yahweh’s marvelous deeds?

His ancestors did not appreciate Yahweh’s marvelous deeds and they forgot them and rebelled.

title: Psalms 106:8 (#1)
content:
Why did Yahweh save the psalmist’s ancestors?

He saved them because of who he is, so that he might show his power.

title: Psalms 106:11 (#1)
content:
What happened to the adversaries of Israel?

The waters covered their adversaries; not one of them remained alive.

title: Psalms 106:14 (#1)
content:
What did the people do when they had intense cravings in the wilderness?

They tested God by doing evil things.

title: Psalms 106:17 (#1)
content:
What happened to Dathan and the people of Abiram?

The ground opened up and buried Dathan and the people of Abiram.

title: Psalms 106:20 (#1)
content:
What did the people worship at Horeb?

They made a statue of a bull at Horeb and worshiped it instead of their God.

title: Psalms 106:23 (#1)
content:
Why did God not annihilate the Israelites?

Moses persuaded God not to destroy them.

title: Psalms 106:26 (#1)
content:
What did Yahweh swear he would do?

Yahweh swore to them that he would cause them to die in the desert.

title: Psalms 106:29 (#1)
content:
What happened to the people of Israel when their actions made Yahweh angry?

A plague broke out among them.

title: Psalms 106:30 (#1)
content:
What happened when Phinehas rose to intervene for the people?

When Phinehas intervened, the plague ended.

title: Psalms 106:32–33 (#1)
content:
Why did Moses suffer?

Because the people made Moses angry, he spoke foolishly.

title: Psalms 106:34 (#1)
content:
What did the people not do that Yahweh had told them to do?

The people of Israel did not destroy the other people groups as Yahweh had told them to.

title: Psalms 106:35–37 (#1)
content:
What happened to the people when they mingled with the nations and worshiped their idols?

They sacrificed their sons and their daughters to demons that the idols represented.

title: Psalms 106:41 (#1)
content:
What happened to Israel when they disobeyed Yahweh?

Yahweh allowed the other people groups to conquer Israel and rule over them.

title: Psalms 106:45 (#1)
content:
Why did Yahweh relent and decide to stop punishing Israel?

He relented because of the covenant he had made with them to faithfully love them.

title: Psalms 106:47 (#1)
content:
What reason does the psalmist state for Yahweh to bring Israel back from among the nations?

The psalmist declares that if Yahweh would bring Israel back, they would give thanks to his holy name and joyfully praise him.

title: Psalms 107:1 (#1)
content:
How long does Yahweh’s covenant faithfulness last?

He faithfully loves his people forever.

title: Psalms 107:2–3 (#1)
content:
From where has Yahweh rescued his redeemed?

He rescued them from their enemies by bring them back from many foreign lands.

title: Psalms 107:6 (#1)
content:
What did Yahweh do for his redeemed when they called out to him in their distress?

He rescued them from what was distressing them.

title: Psalms 107:8 (#1)
content:
For what should people praise Yahweh?

They should praise him for his covenant faithfulness and for the amazing things he has done for all people.

title: Psalms 107:12 (#1)
content:
How did Yahweh humble the people?

He let them experience difficult things so that they would no longer be proud.

title: Psalms 107:15–16 (#1)
content:
What reason does the psalmist give the people for thanking Yahweh?

They should thank him because he has set them free as if from prison.

title: Psalms 107:17 (#1)
content:
Why were the people afflicted?

They were afflicted because of their sins.

title: Psalms 107:22 (#1)
content:
What kind of sacrifices should people offer to Yahweh?

They should offer sacrifices of thanksgiving.

title: Psalms 107:23–24 (#1)
content:
What did the people see who traveled and did business on the sea in ships?

They saw the amazing creatures that Yahweh had made in the deep sea.

title: Psalms 107:27 (#1)
content:
What happened to the sailors as the storm raged?

They staggered like drunken men and everything that they tried to do was useless.

title: Psalms 107:28–29 (#1)
content:
What happened when the men called out to Yahweh in their distress?

He rescued them from what was distressing them and calmed the storm.

title: Psalms 107:32 (#1)
content:
Where should people exalt and praise Yahweh?

They should praise him wherever all the people gather together with their leaders.

title: Psalms 107:34 (#1)
content:
What did Yahweh do to a fruitful land because of the wickedness of the people?

He turned a fruitful land into a salty wasteland because of the wickedness of its people.

title: Psalms 107:37 (#1)
content:
What did the people sow and plant?

They sowed fields and planted vineyards which produced a harvest.

title: Psalms 107:40 (#1)
content:
What happened to the leaders who oppressed Yahweh’s people?

He caused them to wander as if they were in a wilderness where there are no roads.

title: Psalms 107:42 (#1)
content:
What happens when the people who live rightly see what Yahweh has done for them and rejoice?

The wicked people have nothing to say in reply.

title: Psalms 107:43 (#1)
content:
Who does the psalmist call upon to ponder the ways Yahweh has shown that he loves them?

The psalmist calls upon whoever is wise to ponder the ways Yahweh has shown that he faithfully loves them as he promised.

title: Psalms 108:1 (#1)
content:
With what does David say he will sing praises?

David says he will sing and make music with his whole being.

title: Psalms 108:4 (#1)
content:
How does David describe how great is Yahweh’s covenant faithfulness?

David says that Yahweh’s covenant faithfulness is so great that it is like the distance between the heavens and the earth.

title: Psalms 108:5 (#1)
content:
Where does David ask for God’s glory to be exalted?

David asks that God’s glory be exalted all over the earth.

title: Psalms 108:8 (#1)
content:
What has God spoken about Ephraim and Judah?

God spoke of the tribe of Ephraim as his protection in battle and Judah is where his kings come from.

title: Psalms 108:9 (#1)
content:
What does God say he will do over Philistia?

God says he will shout triumphantly because he has defeated the people of Philistia.

title: Psalms 108:12 (#1)
content:
Whose help does David say is futile?

David asks for God’s help because man’s help is futile.

title: Psalms 108:13 (#1)
content:
How does David describe his triumph with God’s help?

David says that with God’s help they will win, and God will enable them to defeat their enemies.

title: Psalms 109:2 (#1)
content:
Who does David say speaks lies against him?

David says that wicked and deceitful people speak lies about him.

title: Psalms 109:4 (#1)
content:
What do the wicked give in return for David’s love?

David says that in return for his love, they accuse him of doing evil things.

title: Psalms 109:7 (#1)
content:
What does David hope will happen when his enemy is judged?

David hopes that when his enemy is judged, he may be found guilty.

title: Psalms 109:10 (#1)
content:
What is David’s request for the children of his enemy?

David asks that his enemy’s children would have to wander about and beg for food.

title: Psalms 109:11 (#1)
content:
What does David hope will happen to his enemy’s earnings?

David hopes that strangers will take what his enemy earns.

title: Psalms 109:12 (#1)
content:
What does David hope regarding his enemy and his enemy’s children?

David hopes that no one will show covenant faithfulness to his enemy and that no one will pity his enemy’s fatherless children.

title: Psalms 109:15 (#1)
content:
What is David’s request from Yahweh concerning his enemy?

David asks that Yahweh will cause everyone on earth to completely forget who they were.

title: Psalms 109:16 (#1)
content:
Why does David ask Yahweh to make sure no one remembers his enemy?

David asks this because his enemy persecuted poor, needy, and brokenhearted people until they died.

title: Psalms 109:17 (#1)
content:
What does David say about his enemy’s attitude toward cursing and blessing?

David says that because his enemy loved to curse others, now people are cursing him, and because his enemy did not bless others, there will be no one who blesses him.

title: Psalms 109:21 (#1)
content:
What does David ask Yahweh to do for him, and why?

David asks Yahweh to be kind to him for the sake of Yahweh’s name and to rescue him because of the promise Yahweh made to faithfully love him.

title: Psalms 109:23 (#1)
content:
To what does David compare his time left to remain alive?

David says that his life is fading away as quickly as a shadow that lengthens at evening or as a man shakes off a locust.

title: Psalms 109:25 (#1)
content:
What do David’s accusers do when they see him?

David says that when they see him, his accusers shake their heads to show that they despise him.

title: Psalms 109:26 (#1)
content:
Why does David think Yahweh will save him?

David asks Yahweh to save him because Yahweh has faithfully loved him according to his covenant.

title: Psalms 109:26–27 (#1)
content:
What does David say will be the result of Yahweh saving him?

When Yahweh saves him, his enemies will know that it was Yahweh who has done it.

title: Psalms 109:28 (#1)
content:
What does David say will happen when his accusers curse him?

David says that when his accusers curse him, Yahweh will bless him and cause him to rejoice.

title: Psalms 109:31 (#1)
content:
What does David say will happen when Yahweh defends the needy person?

Yahweh will save the needy person from those who condemn him.

title: Psalms 110:1 (#1)
content:
Where does Yahweh ask David’s lord to sit, and for how long?

Yahweh asks him to sit at his right hand until he defeats his enemies.

title: Psalms 110:2 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh extend from Zion?

Yahweh extends the kingdom from Zion for the king to rule over his enemies.

title: Psalms 110:3 (#1)
content:
What do the people do on the day the king goes to battle?

They willingly offer themselves to serve him and show their devotion in holiness.

title: Psalms 110:4 (#1)
content:
What did Yahweh promise that he will never change his mind about?

Yahweh promised that the king would be a priest forever, in the same way that Melchizedek was a priest.

title: Psalms 110:5 (#1)
content:
What does the Lord do to other kings when he becomes angry?

The Lord crushes and defeats kings when he is angry.

title: Psalms 110:6 (#1)
content:
What does the Lord do to the nations?

He punishes the people from other nations, causing many enemy soldiers to fall dead.

title: Psalms 110:7 (#1)
content:
What does the king do after he drinks from the stream along the road?

He will be victorious.

title: Psalms 111:1 (#1)
content:
When does the psalmist say he will give thanks to Yahweh?

He will give thanks to Yahweh whenever the upright gather to meet.

title: Psalms 111:3 (#1)
content:
How long will Yahweh’s righteousness stand?

His righteousness will last forever.

title: Psalms 111:5 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh always remember?

He always remembers his covenant.

title: Psalms 111:6 (#1)
content:
How did Yahweh show his people how powerful he is?

He showed his people how powerful he is by enabling them to capture the lands of the nations around them.

title: Psalms 111:8 (#1)
content:
How does the psalmist describe Yahweh’s instructions?

Yahweh’s instructions are meant to be kept forever since he created them in order to do what is best for us, and they are completely right.

title: Psalms 111:9 (#1)
content:
How has Yahweh redeemed his people?

Yahweh rescued his people from being slaves in Egypt.

title: Psalms 111:10 (#1)
content:
What is the beginning of wisdom?

Having a profound respect for Yahweh is the way to become wise.

title: Psalms 111:10 (#2)
content:
What do those obeying Yahweh’s instructions have?

Those who obey Yahweh’s instructions have good understanding.

title: Psalms 112:1 (#1)
content:
What kind of person does the psalmist say will be happy?

The person who respects Yahweh and happily obeys his commandments will be happy.

title: Psalms 112:2 (#1)
content:
What happens to the descendants of the man who obeys Yahweh and who greatly delights in his commandments?

His descendants will prosper in their land and will be blessed.

title: Psalms 112:3 (#1)
content:
What happens to the household of the man who obeys Yahweh?

His family will be wealthy.

title: Psalms 112:4 (#1)
content:
For whom does the psalmist say light shines in the darkness?

Light shines in the darkness for those who are upright, gracious, compassionate, and just.

title: Psalms 112:5 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say about the person who is gracious and lends to others?

Such a person is good and conducts his affairs with honesty.

title: Psalms 112:7 (#1)
content:
What does the righteous man do rather than fear bad news?

He does not fear, but he is confident, trusting in Yahweh.

title: Psalms 112:9 (#1)
content:
What happens to the righteous person who generously gives to the poor?

People will greatly honor the righteous person who gives to the poor.

title: Psalms 112:10 (#1)
content:
What happens to the wicked person who sees the righteous person being honored?

The wicked person will become angry sees the righteous person being honored.

title: Psalms 113:1 (#1)
content:
Who does the psalmist call to praise Yahweh?

He calls the servants of Yahweh to praise him.

title: Psalms 113:2 (#1)
content:
For how long should the name of Yahweh be praised?

His name should be praised both now and forevermore.

title: Psalms 113:3 (#1)
content:
Who should praise Yahweh for who he is?

He should be praised by everyone everywhere.

title: Psalms 113:5 (#1)
content:
According to the psalmist, who is like Yahweh our God?

There is no one who is like Yahweh.

title: Psalms 113:7–8 (#1)
content:
How does Yahweh cause the poor and the needy person to be treated?

Yahweh causes people to honor him by making him a leader of his people.

title: Psalms 113:9 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh do for barren women?

He enables barren women to become joyful mothers of children.

title: Psalms 114:1 (#1)
content:
What country did the people of Israel leave where people spoke a foreign language?

The people of Israel left Egypt.

title: Psalms 114:3 (#1)
content:
What happened to the sea and the Jordan River when the Israelites came to them?

At both places, the water stopped flowing so the Israelites could cross.

title: Psalms 114:4 (#1)
content:
What did the mountains and the hills do?

The mountains shook as if they were skipping like rams, and the hills jumped like lambs.

title: Psalms 114:7 (#1)
content:
Why does the psalmist say the earth should tremble?

The earth should tremble because of the presence of God.

title: Psalms 114:8 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say God did with the rock?

God caused springs to flow from the rock.

title: Psalms 115:1 (#1)
content:
Who does the psalmist say should be given honor?

The psalmist says that only Yahweh deserves honor.

title: Psalms 115:4 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say about the nations’ idols?

He says their idols are only handmade items made of silver and gold.

title: Psalms 115:5–6 (#1)
content:
What are the idols not able to do?

They are not able to speak, see, hear, or smell.

title: Psalms 115:11 (#1)
content:
Why should those who respect Yahweh trust in him?

They should trust in Yahweh because he is the one who helps and protects them.

title: Psalms 115:13 (#1)
content:
Whom does the psalmist say Yahweh will bless?

Yahweh will bless all those who respect him, whether they are considered important or not.

title: Psalms 115:16 (#1)
content:
To whom do the heavens and earth belong?

The heavens belong to Yahweh, but the earth he has given to mankind.

title: Psalms 115:17–18 (#1)
content:
Who does the psalmist say should praise Yahweh?

Since the dead are no longer able to praise Yahweh, those who are alive will praise him as long as they live.

title: Psalms 116:1 (#1)
content:
For what reason does the psalmist say he loves Yahweh?

He loves Yahweh because Yahweh hears him when he cries out to him for help.

title: Psalms 116:3 (#1)
content:
Why did the psalmist say he felt like he was tied up with cords of death?

He was so distressed and full of sorrow that he felt as if he were about to die.

title: Psalms 116:6 (#1)
content:
Who does Yahweh guard?

Yahweh guards and protects those who are helpless.

title: Psalms 116:8 (#1)
content:
In what ways did Yahweh rescue the psalmist?

Yahweh saved the psalmist from dying, from being sorrowful, and from making bad mistakes.

title: Psalms 116:8–9 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say he will do because Yahweh rescued him?

Because Yahweh rescued him, he will live as Yahweh directs him as long he is alive.

title: Psalms 116:10 (#1)
content:
What did the psalmist do even when he was suffering?

He continued to trust in Yahweh even when he was suffering.

title: Psalms 116:12 (#1)
content:
What did the psalmist say he could never repay Yahweh for?

The psalmist felt he could never repay Yahweh for all the good things he had done for him.

title: Psalms 116:14 (#1)
content:
Where does the psalmist say he will fulfill his vows to Yahweh?

He will fulfill his vows in the presence of all his people.

title: Psalms 116:15 (#1)
content:
What is precious in the eyes of Yahweh?

It is precious to Yahweh when any of his faithful people die.

title: Psalms 116:16–17 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say he will offer to Yahweh for taking away his bonds?

He says he will pray to Yahweh and offer to him a sacrifice to thank him.

title: Psalms 116:18–19 (#1)
content:
Where will the psalmist present his offerings to Yahweh?

He will present them in the courtyard outside his temple in Jerusalem in the presence of all the people.

title: Psalms 117:1 (#1)
content:
Who does this psalmist call upon to praise Yahweh?

He calls upon all the people of every nation to praise Yahweh.

title: Psalms 117:2 (#1)
content:
What reasons does the psalmist give for the people to praise Yahweh?

Because Yahweh is fully committed to love them faithfully, just as he promised to do, and he can be trusted to be faithful forever.

title: Psalms 118:1 (#1)
content:
What are the two reasons the psalmist gives for thanking Yahweh?

People should thank Yahweh because he is good and because his faithful love will last forever.

title: Psalms 118:5 (#1)
content:
How did Yahweh respond when the psalmist called out to him?

Yahweh answered him and set him free.

title: Psalms 118:8 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say it is better to do than to trust in other people?

It is better to rely on Yahweh than to trust in people.

title: Psalms 118:12 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist compare his enemies to when they surrounded him?

He compares them to angry bees that swarmed around him.

title: Psalms 118:15 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say is heard from the people who honor God?

Those who honor God shout out joyful songs of celebration because Yahweh has powerfully defeated their enemies.

title: Psalms 118:18 (#1)
content:
What has Yahweh not done even though the psalmist feels that Yahweh has punished him severely?

Yahweh has not allowed him to die.

title: Psalms 118:19 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say he will do when the gates are opened through which those who obey Yahweh may enter?

He will enter through the gates and give thanks to Yahweh.

title: Psalms 118:22 (#1)
content:
What has happened to the stone that the builders rejected?

The stone that the builders rejected has become the most important stone in the building.

title: Psalms 118:24 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say they should do on the day that Yahweh has made?

They should rejoice and be glad in it.

title: Psalms 118:27 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say the people should do with the sacrifice?

They should tie the sacrifice to the horns of the altar.

title: Psalms 118:28 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say he will do for Yahweh, his God?

He will give thanks to Yahweh and tell everyone how great he is.

title: Psalms 119:2 (#1)
content:
How does the psalmist describe people who do what Yahweh tells them to do?

Those are the people who sincerely want to know him.

title: Psalms 119:5–6 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say would keep him from being ashamed?

If he could obey everything that Yahweh commands, he would not have shame when he looks at all Yahweh’s commandments.

title: Psalms 119:7 (#1)
content:
When does the psalmist give thanks to Yahweh?

He gives thanks when he learns all of Yahweh’s just regulations.

title: Psalms 119:9 (#1)
content:
How can a young person be sure to live in the right way?

A young person can be sure to live in the right way by obeying Yahweh’s word.

title: Psalms 119:11 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist do in order to not sin again Yahweh?

He memorized Yahweh’s commands so that he might not sin against him.

title: Psalms 119:14 (#1)
content:
In what does the psalmist rejoice more than in all riches?

He rejoices in obeying Yahweh’s instructions more than in all riches.

title: Psalms 119:15 (#1)
content:
What will the psalmist do with Yahweh’s precepts?

He will meditate on Yahweh’s precepts and study the way of living that Yahweh has taught him.

title: Psalms 119:18 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist ask Yahweh to do so that he can see the marvelous things in Yahweh’s teaching?

He asks Yahweh to help him to understand Yahweh’s instructions.

title: Psalms 119:20 (#1)
content:
How does the psalmist feel as he longs for Yahweh’s instructions?

He feels weak with longing for Yahweh’s instructions.

title: Psalms 119:21 (#1)
content:
Who does the psalmist Yahweh rebukes when he disobeys Yahweh’s commandments?

The proud are rebuked when they disobey Yahweh’s commandments.

title: Psalms 119:23 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist do even though rulers sit and plan ways to harm him?

He meditates on what Yahweh has commanded him.

title: Psalms 119:25 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist ask Yahweh to do according to Yahweh’s word?

He asks Yahweh to allow him to live as he has promised.

title: Psalms 119:27 (#1)
content:
Why does the psalmist ask Yahweh to help him understand the way of Yahweh’s precepts?

He wants to understand the way of Yahweh’s precepts so he can meditate on how amazing Yahweh’s instructions are.

title: Psalms 119:29 (#1)
content:
From what does the psalmist ask Yahweh to prevent him?

He asks Yahweh to prevent him from telling lies.

title: Psalms 119:36 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist ask Yahweh to cause him to do?

He asks Yahweh to cause him to want to do what Yahweh says rather than to want to get things that belong to other people.

title: Psalms 119:37 (#1)
content:
From what does the psalmist ask Yahweh to not allow him to do?

He asks Yahweh to not allow him to desire things that are not good for him.

title: Psalms 119:43 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist ask Yahweh to allow him to do?

He asks Yahweh to allow him to truthfully tell others how Yahweh saved him.

title: Psalms 119:45 (#1)
content:
Why does the psalmist say that he will walk about freely?

He will walk about freely and safely because he always tries to obey Yahweh’s regulations.

title: Psalms 119:47 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say he delights in and loves?

He delights in and loves Yahweh’s commandments.

title: Psalms 119:49 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist ask Yahweh to remember?

He asks Yahweh to remember to do what he said he would do for him, by which Yahweh gave him hope.

title: Psalms 119:51 (#1)
content:
Even though the proud have scoffed at him, what has the psalmist not done?

The psalmist has not stopped obeying Yahweh’s teaching.

title: Psalms 119:54 (#1)
content:
What does psalmist say Yahweh’s statutes are like to him?

Yahweh’s statutes are like music to the psalmist.

title: Psalms 119:58 (#1)
content:
How did the psalmist entreat Yahweh to be merciful to him?

He earnestly pleaded with Yahweh to be merciful to him as he promised that he would do.

title: Psalms 119:61 (#1)
content:
What has the psalmist not forgotten when the wicked try to ensnared him into doing wrong?

He has not forgotten Yahweh’s teaching.

title: Psalms 119:63 (#1)
content:
What kind of people is the psalmist a friend to?

He is a friend of all who revere Yahweh and obey what he tells them to do.

title: Psalms 119:66 (#1)
content:
Why does the psalmist ask Yahweh to teach him good discernment and understanding?

He asks because he trusts in Yahweh’s commandments.

title: Psalms 119:69 (#1)
content:
What did the psalmist do when the arrogant lied about him?

He obeyed what Yahweh had told him to do.

title: Psalms 119:71 (#1)
content:
Why does the psalmist say that it is good that he has suffered?

It was good for him to suffer so that he would learn Yahweh’s statutes.

title: Psalms 119:72 (#1)
content:
The psalmist says the teaching of Yahweh is more beneficial for him than what?

The teaching of Yahweh’s mouth is more beneficial for him than many riches.

title: Psalms 119:74 (#1)
content:
Why does the psalmist say that those who revere Yahweh will rejoice when they see what Yahweh has done for him?

Then they will be glad, because they will see how good it is that the psalmist has trusted Yahweh to do what he said.

title: Psalms 119:75 (#1)
content:
Why does the psalmist say that Yahweh has made him suffer?

Yahweh has made the psalmist suffer only because he faithfully loves him.

title: Psalms 119:76 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say Yahweh’s faithful love will do for him?

The psalmist says that Yahweh’s faithful love would comfort him.

title: Psalms 119:80 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say will keep him from being ashamed?

The psalmist says that he will not be ashamed if he obeys Yahweh’s regulations.

title: Psalms 119:82 (#1)
content:
What is the psalmist tired of waiting for?

He is tired of waiting for Yahweh to help him as he promised to do.

title: Psalms 119:86 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say about Yahweh’s commandments?

He says all of Yahweh’s commandments are true.

title: Psalms 119:88 (#1)
content:
Why does the psalmist ask Yahweh to keep him alive?

He asks Yahweh to keep him alive so that he may continue to obey what Yahweh has instructed.

title: Psalms 119:90 (#1)
content:
How long does Yahweh’s faithfulness last?

Yahweh’s faithfulness lasts through every generation.

title: Psalms 119:93 (#1)
content:
Why will the psalmist be preserved alive?

He will be able to live because he obeyed what Yahweh had declared for him to do.

title: Psalms 119:96 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say about Yahweh’s commandment compared to all that people can achieve?

He says there is a limit to what people can achieve, but Yahweh’s commandments are limitless.

title: Psalms 119:99 (#1)
content:
Why does the psalmist say he has more insight than all his teachers?

He has more insight than all his teachers because he continually thinks about what Yahweh tells him.

title: Psalms 119:103 (#1)
content:
The psalmist says Yahweh’s word is sweeter than what?

Reading Yahweh’s word is like eating something sweeter than honey.

title: Psalms 119:104 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist hate because he understands what Yahweh has declared he should do?

The psalmist hates all evil activities because he understands what Yahweh has declared he should do.

title: Psalms 119:106 (#1)
content:
What has the psalmist sworn and promised that he will do?

He has solemnly promised that he will always obey Yahweh’s regulations.

title: Psalms 119:111 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say will make him joyful?

Knowing that Yahweh has given him instructions and that they are his forever.

title: Psalms 119:114 (#1)
content:
Since Yahweh is his hiding place and his shield, what is the psalmist waiting for?

The psalmist is waiting for Yahweh to answer his prayer.

title: Psalms 119:118 (#1)
content:
Why does Yahweh reject all those who disregard his statutes?

He rejects all those who disobey his statutes, for they deceive others by lying.

title: Psalms 119:120 (#1)
content:
Why does the psalmist tremble?

His trembles because he fears Yahweh’s punishment for those who do not obey his rules.

title: Psalms 119:123 (#1)
content:
What is the psalmist tired of waiting for?

He is tired of watching and waiting for Yahweh’s salvation which he has promised.

title: Psalms 119:125 (#1)
content:
Why does the psalmist ask Yahweh for understanding?

He asks for understanding so that he can learn what Yahweh has instructed him to do.

title: Psalms 119:128 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist hate?

He hates all of the evil things that people do.

title: Psalms 119:130 (#1)
content:
To what does the psalmist compare understanding Yahweh’s words?

When someone explains Yahweh’s words, it is as though he is opening a door to a bright light that allows people to see what they did not see before.

title: Psalms 119:132 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist ask Yahweh to do?

He asks Yahweh to turn to him and be gracious to him.

title: Psalms 119:134 (#1)
content:
Why does the psalmist ask Yahweh to rescue him from the people who oppress him?

He asks Yahweh to rescue him so that he may obey Yahweh’s instructions.

title: Psalms 119:136 (#1)
content:
Why is the psalmist sad?

He is crying because people do not keep Yahweh’s law.

title: Psalms 119:137 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say about Yahweh and his rules?

Yahweh is righteous and his rules are just.

title: Psalms 119:140 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say he, Yahweh’s servant, loves?

He loves all the perfectly dependable things that Yahweh has said.

title: Psalms 119:141 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist not do despite the fact that he is small and despised?

He does not forget Yahweh’s precepts.

title: Psalms 119:143 (#1)
content:
How does the psalmist feel about Yahweh’s commandments, even when he is stressed and anxious?

Yahweh’s commandments are still his delight.

title: Psalms 119:146 (#1)
content:
What will the psalmist do if Yahweh saves him when he calls out?

He will keep Yahweh’s instructions.

title: Psalms 119:152 (#1)
content:
What did the psalmist learn long ago from Yahweh’s commandments?

He learned that Yahweh established his commandments to last forever.

title: Psalms 119:153 (#1)
content:
Why does the psalmist ask Yahweh to see his affliction and rescue him?

He asks Yahweh to rescue him because he has not forgotten Yahweh’s law.

title: Psalms 119:155 (#1)
content:
What happens to the wicked because they do not obey what Yahweh has said?

Yahweh will not save them, for they have not obeyed him.

title: Psalms 119:158 (#1)
content:
Why does the psalmist view the treacherous with disgust?

He views the treacherous with disgust because they have not obeyed Yahweh’s instructions.

title: Psalms 119:160 (#1)
content:
How long does every c of Yahweh’s righteousness last?

Every judgement Yahweh has made is right and will last forever.

title: Psalms 119:161 (#1)
content:
How does the psalmist respond when rulers pursue him without cause?

He still deeply respects Yahweh’s words.

title: Psalms 119:164 (#1)
content:
How often does the psalmist praise Yahweh?

He praises Yahweh throughout the day.

title: Psalms 119:168 (#1)
content:
Why does the psalmist obey Yahweh’s instructions?

He obeys Yahweh’s instructions because Yahweh knows everything that he does.

title: Psalms 119:170 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist ask Yahweh to do when he prays for his help?

He asks Yahweh to rescue him as he said he would do.

title: Psalms 119:172 (#1)
content:
Why does the psalmist want to sing about Yahweh’s word?

He wants to sing about Yahweh’s word because all of his commandments are right.

title: Psalms 119:176 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist ask Yahweh to do when the psalmist has strayed like a sheep who has left its flock?

He asks Yahweh to search for him, because he has not forgotten Yahweh’s commandments.

title: Psalms 120:1 (#1)
content:
What did Yahweh do when the psalmist called out in distress?

The psalmist says that Yahweh answered him.

title: Psalms 120:2 (#1)
content:
Who does the psalmist ask Yahweh to rescue him from?

The psalmist asks Yahweh to rescue him from those who tell lies and try to deceive.

title: Psalms 120:3–4 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say Yahweh will do to people who lie and deceive?

Yahweh will punish them as with a warrior’s sharp arrows and with burning coals.

title: Psalms 120:6–7 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say about peace?

The psalmist says that he has lived for too long with those who hate peace and he is for peace.

title: Psalms 121:1 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist look up toward?

The psalmist looks up to the mountains.

title: Psalms 121:2 (#1)
content:
From whom does the psalmist say his help comes?

The psalmist says his help comes from Yahweh.

title: Psalms 121:3 (#1)
content:
How will Yahweh help the people of Israel?

Yahweh will not allow them to slip and will protect them.

title: Psalms 121:4 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say the protector of Israel never does?

The one who protects the people of Israel never sleeps.

title: Psalms 121:5 (#1)
content:
Who is watching over Israel?

Yahweh is watching over Israel and protects them like a shade from the sun.

title: Psalms 121:6 (#1)
content:
What will not harm Israel?

The sun will not harm them by day nor the moon by night.

title: Psalms 121:7–8 (#1)
content:
Who will protect Israel and keep them safe?

Yahweh will protect them in all they do.

title: Psalms 122:1 (#1)
content:
What made David rejoice?

He rejoiced when people invited him to go to the temple of Yahweh in Jerusalem.

title: Psalms 122:2 (#1)
content:
Where are the people standing?

They are standing inside the gates of Jerusalem.

title: Psalms 122:3 (#1)
content:
How was Jerusalem built?

Jerusalem was built in a way that everything fits closely together.

title: Psalms 122:4 (#1)
content:
Why do the tribes of Israel go up to Jerusalem?

The tribes go up to Jerusalem to give thanks to Yahweh as he told them to do.

title: Psalms 122:5 (#1)
content:
What purpose do the thrones in Jerusalem serve?

The kings who are descendants of King David sit on their thrones there and judge the people.

title: Psalms 122:6 (#1)
content:
What are the people to pray concerning Jerusalem?

They are to pray that those who love Jerusalem will have peace and will prosper.

title: Psalms 122:7 (#1)
content:
What does David ask for concerning Jerusalem?

He asks that those living within the city walls will have peace and prosperity.

title: Psalms 122:8 (#1)
content:
For whose sake does David pray for peace in Jerusalem?

He prays for peace for the sake of his fellow Israelites.

title: Psalms 122:9 (#1)
content:
Why does David seek good for Jerusalem?

He intends to always do what is best for Jerusalem because Yahweh has his temple there.

title: Psalms 123:1 (#1)
content:
To whom does the psalmist look up toward?

The psalmist looks up toward Yahweh, the one who lives in heaven.

title: Psalms 123:2 (#1)
content:
To what does the psalmist compare the way the people look to Yahweh their God?

They look to Yahweh like servants watch and wait for their master to provide for them.

title: Psalms 123:3 (#1)
content:
Why do the people ask Yahweh to have mercy on them?

Because people have despised them so much that they cannot endure any more.

title: Psalms 124:2–3 (#1)
content:
What would have happened if Yahweh had not been on the side of Israel when their enemies attacked them?

If Yahweh had not been helping the people of Israel, the enemies who attacked them would have destroyed them.

title: Psalms 124:4–5 (#1)
content:
To what does David compare what their enemies would have done to Israel?

Their enemies’ attack would have overwhelmed them like raging waters that would have drowned them.

title: Psalms 124:6 (#1)
content:
What did the people do after Yahweh did not let their enemies destroy them?

The people praised Yahweh.

title: Psalms 124:7 (#1)
content:
What is the escape of the Israelites like?

Their escape is like a bird that escaped from the snare of the trappers.

title: Psalms 124:8 (#1)
content:
From where does David say the Israelites’ help comes?

Their help comes from Yahweh who made heaven and earth.

title: Psalms 125:1 (#1)
content:
What are those who trust in Yahweh like?

They are as secure as Mount Zion, unshakable and standing firm forever.

title: Psalms 125:2 (#1)
content:
To what does the psalmist compare the way that Yahweh protects his people?

The psalmist compares the way Yahweh protects his people to the way the mountains surrounding Jerusalem protect the city.

title: Psalms 125:3 (#1)
content:
Who must not rule over the land that God gave to righteous people?

Wicked people must not rule or the righteous people will start doing what is wrong.

title: Psalms 125:4 (#1)
content:
To whom does the psalmist request that Yahweh do good?

He requests that Yahweh do good to people who do good things for others and thus obey him sincerely.

title: Psalms 125:5 (#2)
content:
What does the psalmist want Yahweh to give Israel?

The psalmist wants Yahweh to bless the people of Israel with peace.

title: Psalms 125:5 (#1)
content:
What will happen to those who choose to do evil things?

Yahweh will send them away along with everyone else who does evil things.

title: Psalms 126:1 (#1)
content:
What did it seem like when Yahweh brought the people back to Zion after the captivity?

It seemed like they were dreaming.

title: Psalms 126:2 (#1)
content:
What was the peoples’ response when Yahweh returned them to Zion after the captivity?

They laughed and shouted joyfully.

title: Psalms 126:4 (#1)
content:
To what does the psalmist compare the way Yahweh restored them to their land after the captivity?

The psalmist compares Yahweh restoring them after their enemies captured them to the way he makes the water flow again in the streams in the Negev desert after being dry.

title: Psalms 126:5 (#1)
content:
What will happen to those who sow while crying?

They will shout joyfully when they gather the harvest.

title: Psalms 126:6 (#1)
content:
What will happen to the person who goes out weeping and carrying seed for sowing?

He will return with shouts of joy, bringing his bundles of grain with him.

title: Psalms 127:1 (#1)
content:
What happens if Yahweh does not approve of building a house and does not watch over a city?

If Yahweh does not approve of building a house, those who build it labor uselessly, and if Yahweh does not watch over a city, it is useless for the watchman to stay awake to guard it.

title: Psalms 127:2 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh give to those whom he loves?

Yahweh gives sleep to those whom he loves.

title: Psalms 127:3 (#1)
content:
What are an inheritance and a reward from Yahweh?

Children are an inheritance and a gift from Yahweh.

title: Psalms 127:4 (#1)
content:
To what are sons one has when he is young compared to?

Those sons will be as useful for him as arrows in the hand of a warrior.

title: Psalms 127:5 (#1)
content:
Why will the man who has many children not be defeated?

When he argues with an opponent at the place where people settle disputes, the opponent will not defeat him.

title: Psalms 128:1 (#1)
content:
