What does the psalmist say about the person who reveres Yahweh and does what he tells them to do?

That person will have a good life.

title: Psalms 128:2 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say will happen to the person who works hard?

That person will enjoy eating the food that he has worked hard for, and it will make him healthy.

title: Psalms 128:3 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say about the wife of the person who reveres Yahweh and works hard?

She will have many children who will grow strong and fill the room around their table.

title: Psalms 128:4 (#1)
content:
What will happen to the person who reveres Yahweh?

Every person who reveres Yahweh will be blessed.

title: Psalms 128:5–6 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist pray that Yahweh will do for the person who reveres him?

The psalmist prays that Yahweh will bless him so that he may see the people of Jerusalem prosper, and live long enough to see his grandchildren.

title: Psalms 129:1–2 (#1)
content:
How long has Israel been oppressed but not defeated?

Israel has been oppressed but not defeated since it became a nation.

title: Psalms 129:3 (#1)
content:
To what does the psalmist compare the way Israel was oppressed?

Their oppression was as severe as if the enemies were plowing across their back, making long wounds like furrows in a field.

title: Psalms 129:4 (#1)
content:
What has Yahweh done for Israel?

Yahweh no longer allows wicked people to control Israel.

title: Psalms 129:5 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist want to happen to those who hate Zion?

He wants for those who hate the people of Zion to all be ashamed and go away.

title: Psalms 129:8 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist not want people to say about those who hate Zion?

He does not want them to call down the blessing of Yahweh on those people or to bless them in the name of Yahweh.

title: Psalms 130:1–2 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist cry out to Yahweh?

The psalmist calls out to Yahweh to listen as he calls out to Yahweh for mercy.

title: Psalms 130:4 (#1)
content:
Why does the psalmist say Yahweh should be revered?

Yahweh should be revered because there is forgiveness with him.

title: Psalms 130:5 (#1)
content:
For whom does the psalmist wait and hope?

He waits for Yahweh and hopes because Yahweh has said that he would help him.

title: Psalms 130:7–8 (#1)
content:
Why does the psalmist tell Israel to hope in Yahweh?

The people of Israel can trust Yahweh to help them because he faithfully loves them, wants to save them, and does not punish them for all the sins they have committed.

title: Psalms 131:1 (#1)
content:
What does David say he is not?

David says he is not a proud or haughty person.

title: Psalms 131:2 (#1)
content:
To what does David compare his soul?

His inner being is peaceful and quieted like a contented child.

title: Psalms 131:3 (#1)
content:
When does David tell Israel to hope in Yahweh?

He tells them to hope in Yahweh now and forever.

title: Psalms 132:1–2 (#1)
content:
What did the psalmist ask Yahweh to remember?

He asked Yahweh to remember David’s suffering and how David made a solemn promise to the Yahweh, the Mighty One who Jacob worshiped.

title: Psalms 132:3–5 (#1)
content:
David vowed that he would not enter his house or sleep until he did what?

He said he would not rest until he built a home for Yahweh.

title: Psalms 132:7 (#1)
content:
Where will the people go and what will they do when they get there?

They will go to the place where Yahweh lives and worship.

title: Psalms 132:9 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist want the priests and the people to do?

The psalmist wants the priests to always do what is right and the people who are faithful to Yahweh to shout joyfully.

title: Psalms 132:10 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist ask Yahweh not to do, for the sake of David?

The psalmist asks Yahweh not to reject David, the king whom he has chosen.

title: Psalms 132:11 (#1)
content:
What is the oath Yahweh swore to David?

Yahweh promised that one of David’s own descendants would sit on his throne as king.

title: Psalms 132:13–14 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh declare about Zion?

Yahweh chose Zion as his dwelling place and declares that he will stay there forever.

title: Psalms 132:15 (#1)
content:
What will Yahweh do for the people of Zion?

Yahweh will provide everything that the people of Zion need, so that even the poor who live there will have enough food to satisfy them.

title: Psalms 132:18 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh promise the king?

Yahweh will cause the enemies of the chosen king to be defeated and ashamed, but his kingdom will flourish.

title: Psalms 133:1 (#1)
content:
What does David say about God’s people?

He says it is good and pleasant when God’s people live together in a unified way.

title: Psalms 133:2–3 (#1)
content:
To what does David compare when God’s people live happily together?

It is as delightful as seeing the priest be anointed with oil or feeling the dew coming down on the mountains of Zion.

title: Psalms 133:3 (#1)
content:
Where did Yahweh bless his people with the promise of life forevermore?

He commanded the blessing of life forevermore on the mountains of Zion.

title: Psalms 134:1–2 (#1)
content:
What should all those who serve Yahweh do?

They should bless Yahweh and praise him by lifting up their hands in prayer toward the holy place.

title: Psalms 134:3 (#1)
content:
Where will Yahweh, who made everything that exists, bless those who serve him?

He will bless them from his temple on Mount Zion.

title: Psalms 135:1–2 (#1)
content:
Who should praise Yahweh?

Those who serve Yahweh in his temple and courtyards should praise Yahweh.

title: Psalms 135:3 (#1)
content:
Why should those who serve Yahweh praise and sing to him?

They should praise Yahweh because he is good, and they should sing praises to him because doing that is pleasant.

title: Psalms 135:4 (#1)
content:
What did Yahweh do for the people of Israel?

Yahweh chose the descendants of Jacob, the people of Israel, to belong only to him as his special possession.

title: Psalms 135:5–6 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist know about Yahweh?

He knows that Yahweh is great, he is more powerful than all other gods, and he does whatever he wants to do anywhere on earth or in heaven.

title: Psalms 135:7 (#1)
content:
What acts does Yahweh do that show his greatness?

Yahweh brings the clouds, makes lightning bolts accompany the rain, and brings the wind from wherever he stores it.

title: Psalms 135:8–9 (#1)
content:
What did Yahweh do to the Egyptians?

He killed the firstborn man and animals of Egypt and he did amazing miracles against Pharaoh and all his servants.

title: Psalms 135:12 (#1)
content:
What did Yahweh do with the land of the nations that other kings ruled over?

He gave their land as an inheritance to Israel his people.

title: Psalms 135:13–14 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say about Yahweh’s name, and what does Yahweh do for his people?

People will remember Yahweh’s name forever, because he defends his people and shows compassion to those who serve him.

title: Psalms 135:15–17 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say about the nations’ idols?

They are handmade statues of silver and gold that have mouths, eyes, and ears but they do not speak, see, hear, nor breathe.

title: Psalms 135:18 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say about people who make or trust in idols?

Those who make idols and those who trust in them will become as helpless as the lifeless idols are.

title: Psalms 135:19–20 (#1)
content:
Who should bless Yahweh?

The descendants of Israel, Aaron, Levi, and those that revere and honor Yahweh should bless Yahweh.

title: Psalms 136:1 (#1)
content:
Why should the people give thanks to Yahweh?

They should give thanks to him for he is good, because he faithfully loves them forever.

title: Psalms 136:4 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh do that no one else does?

Yahweh alone does wonderful miracles.

title: Psalms 136:10 (#1)
content:
What did Yahweh do to the firstborn of Egypt?

He killed all the firstborn of the Egyptians.

title: Psalms 136:13–14 (#1)
content:
What did Yahweh do for Israel when he divided the Sea of Reeds?

He enabled the Israelites to pass through the middle of the Sea of Reeds on dry land.

title: Psalms 136:16 (#1)
content:
How was Yahweh faithful to his people?

He led his people safely through the wilderness.

title: Psalms 136:21 (#1)
content:
What did Yahweh do with the land of the great kings?

He gave their land as an inheritance to the people of Israel because he loves them forever.

title: Psalms 136:26 (#1)
content:
Why does the psalmist say to give thanks to the God who rules from heaven?

People should give thanks to God because he faithfully loves them forever.

title: Psalms 137:1 (#1)
content:
Where were the captives when they sat down and wept?

They were by the rivers of Babylon when they cried at the memory of the temple in Jerusalem.

title: Psalms 137:3 (#1)
content:
What did the captors demand that the captives sing?

Their captors demanded that they sing joyful songs about Zion.

title: Psalms 137:5–6 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say should happen to him if he forgets about Jerusalem?

He says he should lose his ability to play the harp and be unable to sing.

title: Psalms 137:7 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist ask Yahweh to remember about the Edomites?

He asks Yahweh to remember and punish the Edomites for what they did when Jerusalem fell. They shouted for it to be completely torn down to its foundations.

title: Psalms 137:8 (#1)
content:
Who does the psalmist say will be happy?

He says the one who repays Babylon for what they did to Israel will be happy.

title: Psalms 138:1 (#1)
content:
How does the psalmist say he will thank Yahweh?

He will thank Yahweh sincerely and praise him in the presence of the idols of other gods.

title: Psalms 138:2 (#1)
content:
What has Yahweh exalted above everything?

He has exalted his word and his name above everything.

title: Psalms 138:3 (#1)
content:
What did Yahweh do for the psalmist when he called?

Yahweh helped him and enabled him to be brave and strong.

title: Psalms 138:4 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist hope the kings of the earth will do?

He hopes they will thank Yahweh because they will have heard what he has said.

title: Psalms 138:5 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say the kings should sing about?

He says they should sing about what Yahweh has done, for he is glorious.

title: Psalms 138:6 (#1)
content:
For whom does Yahweh care?

He takes care of humble people.

title: Psalms 138:7 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say Yahweh will do when he walks through trouble?

Yahweh will keep him safe and will rescue him from his enemies.

title: Psalms 138:8 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist ask Yahweh not to do?

He asks that Yahweh not abandon the people that he has made because he faithfully loves them forever.

title: Psalms 139:1 (#1)
content:
What does David say Yahweh has done?

Yahweh has thoroughly examined him and knows him completely.

title: Psalms 139:2 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh understand from far away?

Yahweh knows everything that David does and understands what he is thinking.

title: Psalms 139:6 (#1)
content:
How does David describe Yahweh’s complete knowledge of him?

That knowledge that Yahweh knows everything about him is so wonderful that David is not even able to comprehend it.

title: Psalms 139:7 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say about escaping from Yahweh’s Spirit?

There is nowhere he can go to get away from Yahweh’s Spirit or flee from Yahweh’s presence.

title: Psalms 139:8 (#1)
content:
Where can David not go to escape from Yahweh’s presence, because Yahweh is there?

David says that even if he could go up to the heavens or down to Sheol where the dead go, Yahweh would be there.

title: Psalms 139:12 (#1)
content:
According to the psalmist, how does Yahweh see darkness compared to light?

Yahweh can see whether in the darkness and the light.

title: Psalms 139:13 (#1)
content:
Where did Yahweh form David?

Yahweh formed him inside his mother’s womb.

title: Psalms 139:16 (#1)
content:
When did Yahweh record each day of David’s life?

Yahweh recorded all the days of David’s life in Yahweh’s book even before the first one happened.

title: Psalms 139:17 (#1)
content:
How does David describe God’s thoughts?

God’s thoughts are precious to David and very numerous.

title: Psalms 139:19 (#1)
content:
What does David want God to do to the wicked and violent men?

David wants God to kill all wicked people and get the violent men away from him.

title: Psalms 139:23 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist ask God to search and know?

He asks God to search him and know what he is thinking, and to examine him and know what worries him.

title: Psalms 139:24 (#1)
content:
In what way does David want God to lead him?

David asks God to teach him to live in the way that lasts forever.

title: Psalms 140:1 (#1)
content:
From whom does David need Yahweh to rescue him?

David needs Yahweh to rescue him from evil people and protect him from violent people.

title: Psalms 140:3 (#1)
content:
What does David say about the wicked?

David says they say things to people that hurt them and are as deadly as the venom of a viper.

title: Psalms 140:4 (#1)
content:
What do the violent men plan to do to David?

They have planned to destroy him.

title: Psalms 140:5 (#1)
content:
What have proud people tried to do to David?

They are trying to destroy him as though they had hidden traps to catch him.

title: Psalms 140:6 (#1)
content:
To what does David ask Yahweh to listen?

David asks Yahweh to listen to him as he pleads for his help.

title: Psalms 140:7 (#1)
content:
What did Yahweh do for David during battles?

Yahweh powerfully saved David and protected him during battles.

title: Psalms 140:9 (#1)
content:
What does David want to happen to the leaders who surround him?

David wants the harmful things that they have said to others to happen to them.

title: Psalms 140:11 (#1)
content:
What does David want to happen to those who slander others?

David wants anyone who slanders others to have evil things happen to them.

title: Psalms 140:12 (#1)
content:
What does David know Yahweh will do for the poor and the needy?

David knows that Yahweh will do what is just and right for poor people.

title: Psalms 140:13 (#2)
content:
What will happen to the upright people?

They will live in Yahweh’s presence.

title: Psalms 140:13 (#1)
content:
What will the righteous people surely do?

The righteous people will surely give thanks to Yahweh.

title: Psalms 141:1 (#1)
content:
What is David crying out to Yahweh?

He is crying out for Yahweh to come to help him and to listen to him when he calls.

title: Psalms 141:2 (#1)
content:
What does David want his prayer and lifted hands to be like for Yahweh?

David wants Yahweh to accept his prayer as though it were an offering of incense to Yahweh and his hands lifted in prayer as an evening sacrifice.

title: Psalms 141:3 (#1)
content:
What does David ask Yahweh to guard?

He asks Yahweh guard him against saying things that are bad or wrong.

title: Psalms 141:4 (#1)
content:
What does David want Yahweh to prevent him from doing?

He asks Yahweh to prevent him from wanting to do evil things, joining wicked men in their deeds, and eating their delicacies.

title: Psalms 141:5 (#1)
content:
What does David say it means if a righteous man corrects him?

He says if it is a righteous person who strikes him, he is acting faithfully and kindly toward David to correct him.

title: Psalms 141:5 (#2)
content:
What does David say it will be like if a righteous man corrects him?

He says it will be as if they have honored him by anointing his head with oil, which he will not refuse.

title: Psalms 141:5 (#3)
content:
What does David always pray against wickedness?

He always prays that Yahweh will punish the wicked because of the wicked deeds that they do.

title: Psalms 141:6 (#1)
content:
What will happen to the wicked people’s judges?

Their judges will be thrown down from a cliff, and the wicked will hear that David’s words are right and good.

title: Psalms 141:7 (#1)
content:
What do the wicked say will happen to their bones?

They say their bones will be scattered on the way to the place where dead people are, just as the earth is scattered when the ground is broken up.

title: Psalms 141:8 (#1)
content:
Who is David relying on?

David is relying on Yahweh to protect his life.

title: Psalms 141:9 (#1)
content:
From what does David want Yahweh to protect him?

David wants Yahweh to protect him from the snares of people who do evil things by trying to trap and trick him.

title: Psalms 141:10 (#1)
content:
What does David want to happen to the wicked?

David wants the wicked to fall into their own traps that they set to catch him while he escapes.

title: Psalms 142:2 (#1)
content:
What does David pour out to Yahweh?

David pours out his complaints about his problems and declares his distress to Yahweh.

title: Psalms 142:3 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh know when David is discouraged?

Yahweh knows what David must do when he is discouraged.

title: Psalms 142:5 (#1)
content:
What does David say Yahweh is to him?

David says Yahweh is like a shelter to him since he protects him.

title: Psalms 142:6 (#1)
content:
Why does David need Yahweh to rescue him from his pursuers?

David asks Yahweh to rescue him from his pursuers because they are stronger than he is.

title: Psalms 142:7 (#1)
content:
Why will the righteous gather around David?

The righteous will gather around David to join him in praising Yahweh because Yahweh will have fulfilled David’s request.

title: Psalms 143:1 (#1)
content:
What does David ask Yahweh to do in response to his prayer?

David asks Yahweh to hear his prayer and answer him according to Yahweh’s faithfulness and righteousness.

title: Psalms 143:2 (#1)
content:
What reason does David give for not wanting Yahweh to judge him?

David asks Yahweh not to judge him because he knows that no one alive is completely innocent before Yahweh.

title: Psalms 143:3 (#1)
content:
What has the enemy done to David?

The enemy has pursued him and defeated him.

title: Psalms 143:5 (#1)
content:
What does David think about when he remembers previous days?

David thinks about all the great things that Yahweh has done.

title: Psalms 143:6 (#1)
content:
How does David describe his longing for Yahweh?

David says he needs Yahweh just as much as a very dry land needs water.

title: Psalms 143:7 (#1)
content:
What would cause David to join those who have died?

David would feel as if he would die soon if Yahweh does not answer him.

title: Psalms 143:8 (#1)
content:
What does David want to hear in the morning because he trusts Yahweh?

Because David trusts Yahweh, he wants to remember that Yahweh faithfully loves him.

title: Psalms 143:8 (#2)
content:
What does David want Yahweh to show him because he depends on Yahweh for his life?

Because David depends on Yahweh for his life, he wants Yahweh to show him the things he should do.

title: Psalms 143:9 (#1)
content:
Where does David say he hides when asking Yahweh to rescue him from his enemies?

David says he hides in Yahweh and relies on his protection.

title: Psalms 143:10 (#1)
content:
Who does David want Yahweh’s good Spirit to show him?

David wants Yahweh to teach him to do what pleases him and Yahweh’s good Spirit to show him the best way to live.

title: Psalms 143:11 (#1)
content:
Why does David ask Yahweh to preserve his life?

David asks Yahweh to preserve his life and rescue him from his enemies because of how righteous Yahweh is.

title: Psalms 143:12 (#1)
content:
What does David ask Yahweh to do to his enemies?

David asks Yahweh to destroy his enemies who want to kill him.

title: Psalms 144:1 (#1)
content:
How does David say Yahweh will protect him?

Yahweh equips David to fight well in wars.

title: Psalms 144:2 (#1)
content:
What does David say Yahweh does for him?

David says Yahweh keeps him safe and helps him escape from danger and enables him to rule people under him.

title: Psalms 144:3 (#1)
content:
What does David think about Yahweh’s attention to people?

David finds it amazing that Yahweh pays any attention to people, since they are so insignificant.

title: Psalms 144:4 (#1)
content:
To what does David compare people’s lives?

David says people live only a short time just as a mist or a shadow quickly disappears.

title: Psalms 144:5 (#1)
content:
What would the mountains do if Yahweh touched them?

Yahweh would cause the mountains to smoke if he touched them.

title: Psalms 144:6 (#1)
content:
What does David ask Yahweh to send against his enemies?

David asks Yahweh to send lightning bolts to send his enemies running.

title: Psalms 144:7 (#1)
content:
How does Yahweh rescue David from the power of foreigners?

Yahweh reaches down from heaven and rescues David from the power of these foreign enemies.

title: Psalms 144:9 (#1)
content:
On what instrument will David sing a new song to God?

David will sing a new song to God and praise him with a lyre which is a harp with ten strings.

title: Psalms 144:10 (#1)
content:
What does David say God does for kings and for him?

David says God saves kings and rescues him from danger in battle.

title: Psalms 144:11 (#1)
content:
What do the mouths of the foreigners speak?

Their speak things that are not true and swear false oaths.

title: Psalms 144:12 (#1)
content:
What does David want the sons of the Israelites to be like?

He wants them to be strong like plants that grow to full size in their youth.

title: Psalms 144:12 (#2)
content:
What does David want the daughters of the Israelites to be like?

He wants them to be as beautiful and stately as pillars that craftsmen carve to decorate a palace.

title: Psalms 144:13 (#1)
content:
What does David ask God to provide?

David asks that the barns be full of many kinds of crops and that the flocks multiply greatly in the fields.

title: Psalms 144:14 (#1)
content:
What does David ask God to spare the nation from?

David asks that there would be no enemies who could break through their walls, no one going into exile, and no crying out in distress in the city squares.

title: Psalms 144:15 (#1)
content:
Who does David say are the people who are happy?

He says those who worship Yahweh as their God will be happy and have a good life.

title: Psalms 145:1 (#1)
content:
Whom does David say he will exalt and bless?

David says he will exalt his God and King and praise him forever and ever.

title: Psalms 145:2 (#1)
content:
How often does David bless God?

Every day David will bless God.

title: Psalms 145:4 (#1)
content:
What will one generation proclaim to the next?

One generation will proclaim all God has done to the next generation.

title: Psalms 145:5 (#1)
content:
On what will David meditate?

He will think about how very glorious and majestic Yahweh is and on his wonderful deeds.

title: Psalms 145:7 (#1)
content:
What do people declare and sing about?

They will celebrate and declare Yahweh’s goodness and sing joyfully about his righteousness.

title: Psalms 145:10 (#1)
content:
What will thank and bless Yahweh?

All the creatures that Yahweh has made will give thanks to him and his faithful ones will bless him.

title: Psalms 145:11 (#1)
content:
What will Yahweh’s faithful ones tell others about?

They will tell others about how gloriously Yahweh rules as king and about how powerful he is.

title: Psalms 145:13 (#1)
content:
How long will Yahweh’s kingdom last?

Yahweh will never stop ruling as king.

title: Psalms 145:14 (#1)
content:
Who does Yahweh support and help?

Yahweh supports and helps people who are struggling with difficult circumstances.

title: Psalms 145:15 (#1)
content:
Who looks expectantly to Yahweh for provision?

All the creatures Yahweh made look to him expectantly, waiting for the food he will give them when they need it.

title: Psalms 145:16 (#1)
content:
How does Yahweh satisfy the desire of every living thing?

Yahweh gives generously and satisfies the desire of every living thing.

title: Psalms 145:18 (#1)
content:
Who is Yahweh ready to help?

Yahweh is ready to help everyone who asks him for help when they do that sincerely.

title: Psalms 145:20 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh do for those who love him?

Yahweh protects all those who love him.

title: Psalms 145:20 (#2)
content:
What will Yahweh do to all the wicked?

He will destroy all the wicked.

title: Psalms 146:2 (#1)
content:
How long will the psalmist praise Yahweh?

He will praise Yahweh as long as he lives.

title: Psalms 146:3 (#1)
content:
What should one not put their trust in?

People should not put their trust in any human being to save them.

title: Psalms 146:4 (#1)
content:
What happens when a person’s breath stops?

When a person’s breath stops, he returns to the ground; on that day his plans end.

title: Psalms 146:5 (#1)
content:
Who does the psalmist say will have happiness?

Those people who confidently expect Yahweh their God to help them will have a very good life.

title: Psalms 146:6 (#1)
content:
What has Yahweh made?

Yahweh made the sky, the land, the sea, and all that is in them.

title: Psalms 146:7 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh do for the oppressed and the hungry?

Yahweh defends people whom others oppress and gives food to the hungry.

title: Psalms 146:8 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh do for the blind and those who are struggling?

Yahweh enables people who are blind to see again and helps people who are struggling.

title: Psalms 146:9 (#1)
content:
Who does Yahweh protect?

Yahweh protects foreigners as well as orphans and widows.

title: Psalms 146:10 (#1)
content:
How long will Yahweh reign?

Yahweh will reign forever, for all generations.

title: Psalms 147:1 (#1)
content:
Why should people praise Yahweh?

People should sing praises to Yahweh because he deserves it and it is good thing to do.

title: Psalms 147:2 (#1)
content:
How does Yahweh help his people?

Yahweh is rebuilding Jerusalem and bringing back the people of Israel who had been scattered.

title: Psalms 147:3 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh do for the brokenhearted?

He comforts them and heals their pain.

title: Psalms 147:4 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh do with the stars?

Yahweh counts the stars and gives each one a name.

title: Psalms 147:5 (#1)
content:
How great is the Lord’s understanding?

His understanding cannot be measured.

title: Psalms 147:6 (#1)
content:
What does Yahweh do to the wicked?

Yahweh makes wicked people fail in what they want to do.

title: Psalms 147:9 (#1)
content:
How does Yahweh care for the animals and ravens?

Yahweh provides food for the animals and feeds the young ravens when they cry out.

title: Psalms 147:11 (#1)
content:
In whom does Yahweh take pleasure?

Yahweh takes pleasure in those who deeply respect him and in those who confidently expect him to be faithful to his covenant promises.

title: Psalms 147:14 (#1)
content:
How does Yahweh bless the people of Jerusalem?

Yahweh gives them peace by keeping their borders safe and satisfies them with plenty of wheat to eat.

title: Psalms 147:15 (#1)
content:
What makes thing happen on the earth?

Things happen on the earth as soon as Yahweh commands them to.

title: Psalms 147:17 (#1)
content:
How does Yahweh send down hail?

Yahweh casts his hail down like small stones.

title: Psalms 147:19 (#1)
content:
To whom does Yahweh declare how he wants them to live?

Yahweh declares this word to the descendants of Jacob.

title: Psalms 147:20 (#1)
content:
What does the psalmist say about other nations?

The other nations do not know his laws.

title: Psalms 148:1–2 (#1)
content:
Who is to praise Yahweh?

Everyone in the heavens, all his angels, and all his heavenly armies are to praise Yahweh.

title: Psalms 148:3–4 (#1)
content:
Who is to praise Yahweh?

The sun, moon, shining stars, highest heavens, and the waters above the heavens are to praise Yahweh.

title: Psalms 148:5 (#1)
content:
Why should Yahweh be praised?

Yahweh should be praised because he commanded and everything was created.

title: Psalms 148:7–8 (#1)
content:
Who should praise Yahweh from the earth?

The sea creatures and everything deep in the ocean, fire and hail, snow and clouds, and the strong winds should praise Yahweh.

title: Psalms 148:9–10 (#1)
content:
Who also should praise Yahweh?

The mountains, hills, fruit and other trees, wild animals and livestock, crawling creatures, and birds should all praise Yahweh.

title: Psalms 148:11–12 (#1)
content:
Who else should praise Yahweh?

Kings of the earth and all peoples, rulers and all judges, young men and women, old people, and children should all praise Yahweh.

title: Psalms 148:13 (#1)
content:
Why should Yahweh be praised?

Yahweh should be praised because he alone is truly great and more glorious than everything on earth and in heaven.

title: Psalms 148:14 (#1)
content:
Who are Yahweh’s faithful ones?

The people of Israel who are close to him are respected as Yahweh’s faithful people.

title: Psalms 149:1 (#1)
content:
How should the faithful praise Yahweh?

They should sing a new song to Yahweh and praise him when the faithful people gather together.

title: Psalms 149:2 (#1)
content:
In whom should Israel rejoice?

The people of Israel should rejoice because of what God has done for them, and because he is their king.

title: Psalms 149:3 (#1)
content:
How should the faithful praise Yahweh?

They should praise his name by dancing and making music to him with tambourines and harps.

title: Psalms 149:4 (#2)
content:
What does Yahweh do for the humble?

He honors humble people by rescuing them.

title: Psalms 149:4 (#1)
content:
In whom does Yahweh take pleasure?

Yahweh takes pleasure in his people.

title: Psalms 149:5 (#1)
content:
How should the faithful exult?

God’s faithful people should celebrate with joyful songs because he has honored them.

title: Psalms 149:6 (#1)
content:
What should the faithful shout about?

They should shout loud praises to God.

title: Psalms 149:6–7 (#1)
content:
What is the purpose of the sword in the hands of the faithful?

The sword in their hand is to punish the people of other nations for the sins they have committed against God.

title: Psalms 149:8–9 (#1)
content:
What will the faithful do to the kings and nobles of the nations?

They will bind their kings with chains and their nobles with shackles of iron in order to carry out the judgment that God has decreed against them..

acai.preferred_label: Bring Honor and Glory on Oneself

title: Psalms 149:9 (#1)
content:
What is the honor of all of God’s faithful?

It is an honor for all of his faithful to carry out the judgment that God has decreed against their leaders.

title: Psalms 150:1 (#1)
content:
Where should everyone praise God?

Everyone should praise God in his temple here on earth, and praise him in the heavens that he created by his power.

title: Psalms 150:2 (#1)
content:
For what should everyone praise God?

Everyone should praise God for the mighty things he has done and for his greatness.

title: Psalms 150:3–5 (#1)
content:
With what instruments should everyone praise God?

Everyone should praise God with shofars, lyres, harps, tambourines, stringed instruments, flutes, and cymbals.

title: Psalms 150:6 (#1)
content:
Who should praise Yahweh?

Everything that breathes should praise Yahweh.
